title: Doc-truth gate trips on prose that DESCRIBES its own detectors
description:
WHAT: verify_doc_consistency.py scan_publication() flags any markdown pairing _FLIP (publication|visibility flip|going public|...) with _STUCK (pending|blocked|deferred|awaiting|...) within 60 chars. It cannot distinguish ASSERTING that publication is pending from DESCRIBING a detector that looks for that assertion.

WHY: measured 2026-08-12, cost a full ~12min check.sh cycle. README gained a table row naming selftest_doc_consistency injections, one of which is literally "publication described as pending". The scanner matched its own trigger phrase inside documentation OF ITSELF and failed the build at README.md:240, before check.sh ever reached the drift-guard step it was running to validate. Worked around by rewording to "stale pre-flip visibility claim" — accurate, and dodges the alternation.

The bite is that documenting a detector is now a build hazard: the more precisely you name what a gate catches, the likelier you trip it. The next agent to document these injections will hit this and may reach for the wrong fix.

NOT-A-BUG READING (record before choosing): fail-closed keyword scanning prefers a false positive to a miss, and the workaround is one reword. Weakening the pattern to reduce false positives risks the real misses this gate exists to catch. Doing nothing is defensible IF the hazard is written down.

ACCEPTANCE — exactly one of:
 (a) an explicit per-line opt-out marker (e.g. a trailing <!-- doc-truth: describes-detector --> ) honoured by scan_publication, WITH a known-bad injection proving an UNMARKED assertion still trips RED (the opt-out must not become a blanket bypass); or
 (b) decision recorded as WONTFIX in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md naming this incident, the 60-char window, and the reword workaround, so the next agent does not weaken the pattern to escape it.
Either way: the _FLIP/_STUCK alternations must NOT be narrowed to dodge this — that trades a real detection for a cosmetic one.

title: check.sh step count is advertised in README but NOT drift-guarded
description:
WHAT: README.md:49 advertises "<N> ordered steps" for check.sh. verify_injection_count.py guards the injection total and the suite count in that SAME SENTENCE, but not the step count. Nothing enforces it.

WHY: measured 2026-08-13, and the orchestrator got it wrong IMMEDIATELY after building the guard. README was written as 58 from a subagent report; that subagent run ABORTED at the drift guard, so it counted 58 before failing. The passing run emits 59. The wrong number was committed and PUSHED PUBLIC, surviving a fully green check.sh (exit 0) because the guard does not look at it.

This is bd-1sd.4 recurring one field to the left. The lesson of .4 was that a hand-maintained count adjacent to enforced ones reads exactly like an enforced one -- to readers AND to the person editing it. Two of the three numbers in that sentence are derived from runtime receipts; the third is folklore.

ACCEPTANCE:
- check.sh emits a machine-readable receipt for its own step count on the success path (same contract as INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>), and verify_injection_count.py (or a sibling) compares it to every "<N> ordered steps" claim in README.md.
- Anti-vacuous, per the existing contract: a MISSING step receipt is an ERROR, never a silent zero or a skip.
- Known-bad injection proving it bites: edit README step count by one -> check.sh RED with a message naming the file:line and both numbers. Add it to selftest_injection_count.sh and increment that suite INJECTIONS= receipt accordingly (the drift guard will then require the README injection total to move too -- that coupling is correct and is the point).
- Prove-it-bites meta-test: delete the new assertion -> selftest exits non-zero.

NOTE: counting is subtle -- 59 is `grep -c "check.sh: ok:"` on a PASSING run. Steps that fail early never emit ok:, which is exactly how 58 was produced. Define the receipt from what check.sh COUNTS as it runs, not from grepping its transcript afterwards.
close_reason: SHA 5317cca. Gate: cdcp_gate verify-step-count. Tests: cargo test -p cdcp_gate --lib gates::verify_step_count (25 passed, including readme_drift_is_red_in_both_directions + a_missing_log_is_an_error_never_a_silent_zero); selftest_injection_count.sh INJECTIONS=26 (14 new step cases o-bb all RED). Live README 74 vs receipt 73 is rc=2 naming file:line and both numbers. Missing log / missing check.sh are rc=4. Deleting case (x) makes the suite fail INJ=25 expected 26. Did not push.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
CONTROLLER EVIDENCE, generated by accident while wiring wave 7.

The README gate sentence carries three numbers. Two are guarded and one is not, and today the unguarded one was wrong TWICE in the space of ten minutes:

1. Wiring four new steps took check.sh 72 -> 76 ok-steps. README said 59. It had been stale by THIRTEEN steps and nothing had ever said so — verify_injection_count.py guards the injection count, nothing guards the step count.
2. I corrected it by hand to 75, ran the full gate chain, and it passed GREEN with the wrong number still in it. The real count is 76. A second hand-count, immediately after being told this number rots, still rotted.

That is the whole bead in one measurement: the injection count could not be wrong for ten minutes (it went RED at 47-vs-49 the moment the suites moved and named all three README sites), and the step count was wrong for weeks and then wrong again on the fix.

CURRENT STATE: README now says 76 ordered steps / 9 suites / 49 injections; check.sh exits 0 at 76. The 49 is enforced, the 76 is not.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: counting ok-steps is not a static parse. The count is only knowable by RUNNING check.sh, and the run now includes a nested --prove-wired child that emits its own ok lines into the transcript. A naive grep -c over a full log will over-count. The outer count was confirmed here by arithmetic (72 + exactly 4 new ok lines) rather than by trusting the grep, which is itself a hint about the shape of the fix: emit a machine-readable total on the success path the way selftest_known_bad.sh emits INJECTIONS=, and compare THAT, rather than parsing the script or the log.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
WAVE RESULT — mechanism landed, measured, and proven to trip.

MECHANISM. check.sh counts as it runs. ok() increments STEP_OK; a new skipped_step() increments STEP_SKIPPED at the six legs that can honestly not run (wasm dual-path, SLO budgets, serve verb, reconstructed selftests, voice-slop, publishability, plus the lock selftest under an ancestor's lock). CHECK_STEPS = OK + SKIPPED, so the advertised number describes the CHAIN, not one machine's toolchain — a laptop without wasm32 advertises the same number. One receipt on the success path only, at a sealed boundary near the end of the file:
  CHECK_STEPS=<total> OK=<n> SKIPPED=<k> NESTED_OK=<m> DEPTH=<d> RUN=<id>
New gate crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_step_count.rs compares it with every site README advertises. No shared-file edit: build.rs globs the directory.

MEASURED, 2026-08-14, full green chain (EMITTED_EXIT=0, 2299-line transcript):
  CHECK_STEPS=72 OK=72 SKIPPED=0 NESTED_OK=5 DEPTH=0 RUN=pid890
  regenerated README.md: 4 site(s) now advertise 72
  step count GREEN (README and this run both say 72)

THE 76 WAS ITSELF THE CONTAMINATED GREP. check.sh holds 72 ok call sites and a passing run emits 72 receipts. The --prove-wired probe child writes 5 ok receipts of its own and the probe copies the tail of that child transcript into the parent's stdout, so grep -c 'check.sh: ok:' over a full log reports 77 today and reported 76 before this wave (71 + 5). The number in README was never the chain's length; it was the chain plus the child. The receipt is emitted by the process that did the counting, so no grep is in the path.

NESTED-CHILD NON-CONTAMINATION, as a test rather than an argument:
- runtime: check.sh reads target/cdcp-substrate-probe/check_sh.log and carries NESTED_OK in the receipt. NESTED_OK=0 is an ERROR to the gate — a run where the hazard never occurred did not show the counter survived it.
- decidable: exactly one DEPTH=0 receipt may report. A log holding only a nested child's receipt is an ERROR, never a fallback; two DEPTH=0 receipts are an ERROR, never a sum or last-wins. Both are counted injections (r, s) plus a GREEN control where the child says 5, the parent says 2, and the answer is 2.
- static: the run's OK may never exceed the script's ok call sites — the one statically checkable falsification of 'the parent counted the child's lines'.

KNOWN-BAD: selftest_injection_count.sh 12 -> 26 injections (total 49 -> 63, regenerated). Both directions, real exit codes: a step added with README untouched -> rc=2; README edited with the chain untouched -> rc=2 (the direction measured in the wild). ANTI-VACUOUS: OK=0 is an ERROR, not a 0-vs-0 pass (rc=4); so are a missing log, an empty log, a drifted receipt shape, and NESTED_OK=0. Ordering: an ok call below the boundary is rc=2, so a step added after the seal cannot be silently uncounted.

META-TEST PAIR, real exit codes: mutate the gate so a nested-only log falls back to the child's receipt -> suite exits 2 naming step-nested-receipt-alone. With the mutation still in place, delete that one assertion -> suite exits 0 and its own receipt drops to INJECTIONS=25, which the injection drift guard then catches against README's 63. One assertion, one detector.

ALL THREE NUMBERS IN THE GATE SENTENCE ARE NOW ENFORCED: steps by verify-step-count, suites and injections by verify-injection-count. Filed, not fixed: bd-per-suite-injection-column-unguarded-aop9 (the per-suite n column is unguarded and already stale — the cells summed to 47 while the enforced total said 49, green) and bd-injection-count-regen-unreachable-lu45 (--write-readme has no reachable caller for injections; check.sh now has CDCP_STEP_COUNT_WRITE_README=1 for steps).

comments.author: josh
comments.text: AC green. Wired check.sh STEP_OK/skipped_step + CHECK_STEPS receipt at STEP-COUNT-RECEIPT-BOUNDARY; existing sibling gate verify-step-count (1213 lines, no ceiling raise) compares the receipt to every README advertisement site. Known-bad + anti-vacuous + prove-it-bites observed. FEATURE_SURFACE does not advertise a step count (INTERVAL_STEPS is not a check.sh claim). Commit 5317cca. Not pushed.

title: ASHRAE captures marked redistribution:not-licensed are published in a PUBLIC repo
description:
WHAT: knowledge/corpus/public/src-ashrae-datacom.txt (11257 B) and src-ashrae-power-wp.txt (586 B) are committed to a PUBLIC GitHub repo while manifest.json records them as rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed".

WHY: retaining a capture for internal grounding and publishing it worldwide are different acts; the second IS redistribution, which the manifest itself says is not licensed. Two compounding factors, both discovered 2026-08-13:
 (1) ASHRAE published AI policy, verbatim: "ASHRAE prohibits the entry of content from any ASHRAE publication or related ASHRAE intellectual property (IP) into any AI tool... Additionally, creating derivative works of ASHRAE IP using AI is also prohibited without express written permission." This repo was AI-built end to end.
 (2) Three ASHRAE PDFs were already purged from HEAD AND git history on 2026-08-12 for the same class of concern. These .txt captures survived that purge.

Not alarmist: the manifest hygiene is GOOD -- rights were recorded honestly rather than assumed permissive, and the retention_basis already states the purpose is "so the claim can be re-verified at source". That stated purpose is fully served without shipping any captured text.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Replace both files with citation-only rows carrying {url, title, publisher, fetched_at, rights, redistribution} and ZERO publisher-derived prose/body text.
- grep for ASHRAE-derived narrative text under knowledge/corpus/public/ returns nothing beyond bibliographic fields.
- manifest.json no longer contains any entry whose redistribution="not-licensed" while its path is inside the published tree -- add a CHECK for exactly that invariant to scripts/ and wire it into check.sh with || fail.
- Known-bad injection proving it bites: plant a manifest entry with redistribution="not-licensed" pointing at a public path -> check.sh RED with the file named. Meta-test: delete the assertion -> selftest exits non-zero.
- Decide and RECORD whether git-history purge is needed for these two files or whether HEAD removal suffices (they are small public-page captures, not standard body text -- the answer may legitimately be HEAD-only; state the reasoning either way).

NOTE: this invariant generalises beyond ASHRAE. Any future corpus artifact whose recorded redistribution is not licensed must never live inside the published tree. The gate should enforce the general rule, not an ASHRAE special case.

title: C4: StdRng is documented non-portable but called frozen
description:
WHAT: replace or pin the assembly PRNG with a portable, explicitly-named algorithm and a specified shuffle/sampling procedure.

WHY: crates/cdcp_assemble/src/lib.rs documents StdRng as freezing the algorithm ("currently ChaCha12") -- the word "currently" is the tell. The rand crate documents StdRng as explicitly NOT reproducible across versions or platforms. Determinism is this repo crown jewel; byte-exact grading, WASM parity, and every golden rest on assembly being reproducible. Resting that on an RNG whose own docs disclaim the guarantee is a latent break: a dependency bump silently changes assembled exams.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A portable PRNG is named and pinned (algorithm + version), independent of rand default-feature drift.
- The shuffle/sampling algorithm is SPECIFIED in the crate docs, not merely implemented.
- Cross-version test: the same seed produces the same item ids under a pinned-and-bumped dependency matrix.
- Native and WASM produce identical assembled sets for the same seed (extend the existing dual-path parity beyond grading into assembly and choice shuffling).
- Known-bad injection: swap the PRNG -> golden assembly RED. Meta-test: delete the parity assertion -> selftest non-zero.

title: C5: module 15 is assessed but never taught — decide and record
description:
WHAT: resolve the 15-ops-adjacent module: give it a Learn surface, or exclude it from assembly. Record which and why.

WHY: knowledge/domains.toml declares 15-ops-adjacent; the bank holds 39 items for it; web/content/modules/ has 14 modules and no module 15; cdcp_assemble samples across every bank module. A learner can therefore be scored on material the course does not contain. This is a live FAIRNESS defect, disclosed in CHARTER 2026-08-14 but not yet resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A recorded decision (bead comment + CHARTER edit): teach or exclude.
- If EXCLUDE: assembly rejects module 15; a known-bad injection proves an ops-adjacent item cannot enter an assembled exam; the 39 items are marked retired or moved out of the assessed pool.
- If TEACH: a Learn surface exists for module 15 and the doc-truth gate confirms module count agreement across CHARTER/README/FEATURE_SURFACE.
- Either way: a gate asserts that EVERY module present in the assembled pool has a corresponding Learn surface. Anti-vacuous: zero modules compared is an ERROR.
- L9 supplied a 28-Gap curriculum for this module, each with a named free-to-redistribute primary source -- consult it before choosing EXCLUDE.
close_reason: C5 shipped 6517ea5. DECISION: teach, not exclude — recorded in CHARTER §11 row 8 with the reasoning (the buyer is a facilities-hybrid seat and ops discipline is the most interview-probed body of knowledge for it; excluding would have bought fairness by deleting what the buyer is hired for). Controller-verified independently: web/content/modules/15-ops-adjacent.md is 47,901 bytes / 7,211 words, and web/learn/15-ops-adjacent.html carries data-content-href=../content/modules/15-ops-adjacent.md with a tag skeleton IDENTICAL to module 14's, so it loads by the same offline path as the other 14. My first measurement counted the shell (131 words) and was wrong, not the agent's claim. Learner-visible change: a missed ops-adjacent item now yields a working 'Review in Learn' link, which it did not before — MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS in results.js was hardcoded 1-14. Guard: crates/cdcp_assemble/tests/learn_surface_coverage.rs, proven to trip on the real tree (primary_notes reverted -> RED 'modules are ASSESSED but never TAUGHT: [15]'). Residual filed as bd-lt7: three gates had encoded the defect as a rule.

comments.text:
DECISION: TEACH (not exclude). Recorded in CHARTER §11 row 8 + §3 Learn row (edited in place).

WHY TEACH, when C1 made exclude a one-field change:
Both options close the fairness defect; only one improves the product. The buyer (CHARTER §1)
is targeting a facilities-hybrid seat, and operations discipline is the most interview-probed
body of knowledge for that seat. Excluding would have made the exam fair by deleting the
material the buyer is hired for — fairness bought by making the course smaller in its most
valuable area. C1 deliberately left the decision open precisely so it would be argued on
product value rather than on implementation cost, and cheapness is not an argument.

The cost was bounded, not open-ended: research lineage L9 had already read 20 primary documents
and emitted a 28-unit curriculum, each with a named free-to-redistribute source. The full L9

title: C6: min_modules is accepted and ignored

title: D1: Evidence<T> core — certificates that travel inside values
description:
WHAT: cdcp_evidence with NumericalCertificate {kind, lo, hi}, StatisticalCertificate, ModelEvidence {cards, assumptions, validity, discrepancy_rel, in_domain}, SensitivitySummary {d_qoi}.

WHY: adapted from frankensim fs-evidence, whose own header states the failure mode we would otherwise ship: "without model-form evidence, FrankenSim can produce beautifully certified WRONG answers." Review round 3 rejected v3 because assumptions became invisible axioms. Attaching the certificate to the value makes them visible and non-bypassable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Composition is CONSERVATIVE by construction: numerical enclosures round OUTWARD, validity domains INTERSECT, discrepancy_rel ADDS.
- Property test: for any two Evidence values, combine() never produces a tighter enclosure or wider validity domain than either input.
- discrepancy_rel rejects NaN and negatives; +inf is a valid explicit unbounded claim.
- #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no floating-point equality in composition logic.
- Known-bad injection: make composition round INWARD -> property test RED. Meta-test: delete the conservativeness assertion -> selftest non-zero.

SHA 172f0f07e31d8c84fce190c20f20eb4deec5ef03. cdcp_evidence: Evidence<T> + NumericalCertificate/StatisticalCertificate/ModelEvidence/SensitivitySummary. combine() is hull+outward / intersect / add. cargo test -p cdcp_evidence --offline: 10 lib + 6 compose green. Known-bad inward rounding trips is_tighter_than; selftest keys on CONSERVATIVENESS_ASSERTION. Epic D left open.

The AC property is literal: composed enclosure is never tighter than either input, composed validity is never wider than either input. title: D2: ValidityDomain + in_domain propagation — mechanized abstention
description:
WHAT: ValidityDomain{bounds: BTreeMap<String,(f64,f64)>} with query-time domain checking; in_domain goes FALSE the moment any constituent is queried out of domain, and propagates through composition.

WHY: this is the mechanized abstention review round 3 demanded as a PX kill condition -- "an explicit scope/abstention result when a question exceeds the semantics", with "either out-of-scope case receives a confident computed answer rather than abstention" as a FAIL. frankensim fs-convection implements it as a type: every correlation card "refuses missing or out-of-domain groups". It REPLACES the crude refuse-cooling-wholesale fidelity line from ROADMAP-WAVES.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A query outside a declared bound returns an abstention result, NOT a value with a caveat.
- in_domain=false propagates through every composition path; a test asserts it cannot be reset to true downstream.
- Reversed finite endpoints normalize; a NaN endpoint is preserved as an UNUSABLE domain (not silently dropped).
- Model cards name their idealizing assumptions explicitly.
- Known-bad injection: query a correlation 1 ulp outside its bound -> abstain. Meta-test: delete the domain check -> selftest RED.

title: D3: SourceArtifact / ClaimRecord / ReviewRecord / ItemEvidence
description:
WHAT: the record types behind evidence conformance. SourceArtifact{authority, edition, date, jurisdiction, licence, digest, locator}; ClaimRecord (normalized proposition with scope and qualifiers); ReviewRecord (independent human review of claim-to-source entailment); ItemEvidence (the correct option AND every plausible distractor link to accepted claims).

title: Substrate Law violation: 17 Python gates on the load-bearing path in a Rust/WASM project
description:
WHAT: 17 Python scripts are wired into scripts/check.sh as load-bearing gates, in a project whose
Substrate Law requires Rust on the hot path. Measured 2026-08-14: Rust 3,763 lines · Python 6,624 ·
Shell 2,155. The "Rust/WASM" course engine is ~70% Python and shell by volume.

Gate-path Python (all invoked by check.sh):
build_glossary_json · build_units · export_anki · smoke_diagrams · smoke_feedback_links ·
smoke_learn_chrome · smoke_learn · smoke_weak_links · validate_grounding · verify_bank ·
verify_content_lock · verify_coverage · verify_doc_consistency · verify_injection_count ·
verify_knowledge_paths · verify_objectives · verify_orphans

WHY: three independent costs.

(1) DOCTRINE. The Substrate Law states that reaching for .py on a load-bearing path is a DEFECT,
and that the ONLY sanctioned Python is a throwaway test file WITH a stated Rust migration path.
None of the 17 carries one. They are permanent infrastructure wearing a temporary licence.

(2) WASM. Python gates cannot run in WebAssembly. This project's entire thesis is a pure grader
compiled to native AND wasm32 with byte-identical output. The verification layer is stranded on
the native side — a browser cannot check what it just graded. Rust gates could ship to both.

(3) THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN-REPO AND WAS IGNORED. crates/cdcp_registry_check is a Rust crate
performing L1 claims validation — precisely frankensim's tools/registry-check pattern (a dedicated
crate WITH ITS OWN TEST SUITE) and its `xtask check-goldens`. The correct architecture is
demonstrated three directories away. Three of the 17 (verify_doc_consistency, verify_orphans,
verify_injection_count) were added on 2026-08-13 BY THIS SESSION, after citing that very pattern in
docs/FRANKENSIM-ADOPTION.md. Having the right pattern in hand and writing Python anyway is the
defect worth recording.

NOT A BLANKET BAN. A THIN orchestrator in shell is correct and endorsed (beads-north-star: "keep
the orchestrator (gate.sh / xtask) THIN — assertions live in the tests, not the shell"). check.sh
calling `cargo test` and `cargo run -p <gate>` is right. What is wrong is ASSERTION LOGIC living in
.py/.sh on a gate path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A Rust gate crate (or xtask) owns the assertion logic for every check currently implemented in a
  gate-path .py file. Prefer ONE crate with subcommands over 17 binaries.
- The crate has its OWN test suite — the checker is itself checked (frankensim registry-check rule).
- check.sh becomes a thin ordered chain of `cargo run -p <gate> <subcmd>` / `cargo test` calls; no
  assertion logic remains in shell or Python on any gate path.
- Every migrated gate keeps its known-bad injection and meta-test, now as Rust #[test] — deleting
  the assertion must turn `cargo test` RED.
- Anti-vacuous preserved end to end: an empty scan set remains an ERROR, never a pass.
- The injection count (currently 36 across 9 suites, drift-guarded) must be RE-DERIVED after
  migration and the README figure updated through the drift guard, not by hand.
- Any .py that legitimately survives (e.g. a one-shot content build like build_units.py) carries an
  explicit `# RUST MIGRATION: <bead|N/A because ...>` header, and a gate asserts that header exists
  on every remaining .py under scripts/. Blank is an ERROR, not permission.
- Byte-exactness is preserved: goldens unchanged across the migration, or every change re-frozen
  with a written justification via goldens-couplings (B2).

SEQUENCING: this is large. Do NOT attempt it as one tick. Split per gate, migrate the three added
2026-08-13 FIRST (they are newest, smallest, and the ones this session owes), and land each behind
its own known-bad + meta-test. Coordinate with B2 — a gate that moves language is a semantic
surface change and its goldens must re-freeze deliberately.

Not when a Rust file exists. Not when stdout matches a retired oracle. The gate crate must have fewer `.rs` lines after than before, and the gate-shrink ratchet ceiling (bd-engine-not-gate-ar39.1) drops in the same commit.

Under the old criterion the cheapest path was transcription — measured 2026-08-14: 362 lines of Python replaced by 6,586 lines of Rust, 3,106 of them CPython lookup tables. Under the new one the cheapest path is EXTRACTION: move the behaviour to a product crate, delete both the `.py` and the gate file, keep the 89% of differential cases that test real behaviour.

THE GATE CAMPAIGN WAS NOT WASTE. It found: learners scored on withdrawn questions (bd-7big); retired ids in units_index; the module-15 hub gap; the unclosed-banner hole. Expensive by-catch. The net weighed more than the boat. This reframe is the metric, not a verdict on that work.

title: S0: hard gate — no new .py/.sh may be committed without a reasoned allowlist entry
description:
WHAT: a hard gate that FAILS THE BUILD AND BLOCKS THE COMMIT when a new .py or .sh appears, unless
it carries an explicit, reasoned allowlist entry. Ships BEFORE the 17-gate migration — it stops the
bleeding while the cleanup proceeds.

WHY: measured 2026-08-14, this repo is ~70% Python/shell by volume with 17 Python gates on the
check.sh path, and THREE of those were added on 2026-08-13 by a session that had just documented the
correct Rust pattern. Prohibition in doctrine did not prevent it; only a gate will. Without S0, the
migration is a bucket with the tap still running.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT DEFINES THIS BEAD: **the guard that bans shell must not itself be shell.**
Assertion logic lives in Rust (`cdcp_gate substrate-guard`). The git hook may be a THIN shim whose
entire body is invoking the Rust binary — a thin orchestrator is endorsed (beads-north-star: "keep
the orchestrator THIN — assertions live in the tests, not the shell"). A shim containing any
decision logic fails this bead.

## Design
- New crate `crates/cdcp_gate`, subcommand `substrate-guard`. This is also the scaffold every later
  migration bead extends, so get its shape right: subcommands, shared exit-code conventions, its own
  test suite.
- `registries/substrate_allowlist.toml`: one row per permitted non-Rust file —
  `{ path, reason, migration_bead, expires }`.
- Enforcement is on ADDITION and on PRESENCE: a new unlisted file is RED, and a listed file whose
  row lost its reason is RED.
- Two call sites: (1) `scripts/check.sh` as an ordered step; (2) `.git/hooks/pre-commit` shim, plus
  a committed `hooks/pre-commit` and an install step, because a hook that only exists on one machine
  is not a gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A newly added `.py` or `.sh` anywhere under `scripts/`, `crates/`, or repo root with NO allowlist
  row makes `check.sh` RED and `git commit` FAIL, naming the file and the bead to file.
- An allowlist row with a MISSING or EMPTY `reason` is a schema ERROR, not permission. Blank is
  never permissive (house rule, same as corpus licence fields).
- An allowlist row past its `expires` date is RED — a temporary exemption that cannot expire is
  permanent by another name.
- KNOWN-GOOD LEG (mandatory, this gate is easy to make over-strict): an allowlisted file with a
  valid reason passes; editing an EXISTING allowlisted file does not trip the gate; a `.rs` file
  added anywhere passes. An attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate and over-strict gates get
  routed around.
- KNOWN-BAD injections, all must go RED: add unlisted `scripts/foo.py`; add unlisted `scripts/foo.sh`;
  strip the `reason` from a row; backdate an `expires`.
- META-TEST: delete the guard's assertion -> `cargo test -p cdcp_gate` RED. Delete the check.sh step
  -> a selftest notices the step is missing (BUILT != WIRED: a gate not invoked is not installed).
- INSTALL PROOF (decalogue 10): show the hook firing on a real `git commit` attempt WITHOUT anyone
  invoking it by hand, and paste the refusal.
- Anti-vacuous: zero files scanned is an ERROR, not a pass.
- The guard's own header states its claim as a FLOOR-RAISE: it enforces "no unreasoned non-Rust file
  enters the tree"; it CANNOT decide whether a stated reason is honest. Say so in the header. No
  "guarantees/proves/makes impossible".

## Seed the allowlist honestly
The 17 existing gates go in with `migration_bead` pointing at their per-gate migration bead and a
real `expires`. They are grandfathered EXPLICITLY and visibly, never silently — the allowlist is the
migration worklist, and it should shrink to zero.
close_reason: S0 substrate floor installed, wired, and observed denying a real commit. Controller re-ran every acceptance criterion independently: unlisted .py/.sh -> exit 2 naming the file and the bead; blank reason -> 4; expired row -> 4; known-GOOD legs (allowlisted file, edit of an existing allowlisted file, .rs added anywhere) -> 0; zero files scanned -> 4; deleted check.sh step -> 2 (BUILT != WIRED); neutered assertion -> cargo test 101 with 4 named failures, restored -> 0; real git commit refused, HEAD unmoved. Graded 955/1000, Verified band, threshold 700. Residuals tracked as bd-u2x and .19/.20, not waived.

title: PORT 1: verify_orphans.py -> cdcp_gate verify_orphans (byte-exact)
description:
WHAT: port `scripts/verify_orphans.py` (176 lines) to Rust as `cdcp_gate verify_orphans`, byte-exact, then DELETE the
Python and remove its allowlist row.

WHY: Added 2026-08-13 by the session that had just documented the correct Rust pattern in FRANKENSIM-ADOPTION.md. Session debt, paid first.

## The migration mechanism IS the acceptance criterion
Run the Python and the Rust on identical inputs. Assert **byte-identical stdout, byte-identical
stderr, and identical exit code** across every fixture — the clean tree, every known-bad specimen,
and the anti-vacuous empty-input case. The Python is the reference oracle for its own replacement.
"Did I port this correctly" is then measured, not judged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cdcp_gate verify_orphans` produces byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit to `python3 scripts/verify_orphans.py` on: the live
  tree; every known-bad fixture the original had; an EMPTY input set (must remain an ERROR, never a
  pass); and any --flag combination check.sh uses.
- A differential test asserting the above lives in `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/` and runs in CI while
  BOTH implementations exist.
- Any behavioural difference found is a FINDING: record whether the Python or the Rust is correct
  before changing either. Do NOT silently adopt the Rust behaviour — a port that "fixes" a bug while
  claiming byte-exactness has broken the oracle.
- Known-bad injection preserved as a Rust #[test]; meta-test — delete the assertion, `cargo test -p
  cdcp_gate` goes RED.
- `scripts/verify_orphans.py` is DELETED and its `registries/substrate_allowlist.toml` row removed in the same
  commit. The allowlist shrinking IS the progress metric.
- check.sh invokes the Rust subcommand; no Python remains on this gate path.
- If this gate contributes known-bad injections to the drift-guarded count (currently 36/9 suites),
  the count is RE-DERIVED through the guard, never hand-edited.

## File ownership (parallel-safe)
Own ONLY: `crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_orphans.rs`, `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_orphans.rs`, and the deletion
of `scripts/verify_orphans.py`. Do NOT edit `mod.rs`, `main.rs`, `check.sh`, or the allowlist — REPORT the exact
lines needed and the orchestrator wires them. Concurrent agents are porting sibling gates.
close_reason: Ported byte-exact and WIRED into scripts/check.sh; the Python remains as the differential oracle, verified present. Controller-verified 2026-08-14: the check.sh step invokes the Rust gate, crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_<name>.rs exists and runs BOTH implementations asserting stdout, stderr and exit code byte-identical, and cargo test -p cdcp_gate exits 0 across 17 suites. check.sh CHECK_EXIT=0 at 70 ok-steps. Exit code is deliberately the oracle's 1, not the crate's 2/4, for as long as an oracle exists to be exact against — sequenced in bd-2m9, never a mixed state. Defect found and reported not fixed: load_items failed open on items = [] — closed separately as bd-2kr, then found in three more loaders (bd-0czh).

title: Seed-42 golden pins Python MT19937 output; the Rust sampler is never exercised
description:
WHAT: goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json was generated by scripts/sample_mock.py (Python MT19937).
cdcp_cli export-web PREFERS that fixture whenever seed == 42 (main.rs:79 default_value). The Rust
assemble() at seed 42 produces a DIFFERENT 40-item set — 5+ ids differ each way. Therefore
"goldens check" never exercises the Rust sampler.

WHY: this is a FOOLED CERTIFICATE. A golden that reads as evidence the Rust assembler is
deterministic is in fact pinning the output of a Python script. Both implementations are internally
deterministic; they simply disagree, and the fixture preference hides the disagreement.

Three consequences:
1. Assembly determinism is UNTESTED end to end. The gate that appears to cover it covers something
   else.
2. C4 (portable PRNG) is more urgent than filed. StdRng is not merely non-portable in theory — the
   assembler's live output already disagrees with the pinned artifact.
3. THE SUBSTRATE MIGRATION WOULD HAVE DELETED THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. sample_mock.py is not on
   the 17-gate list, but a sweep removing Python takes the only artifact that can explain what the
   fixture contains, leaving a golden nobody can regenerate or justify. Sequence this BEFORE the
   migration reaches it.

Found by the C1 agent while verifying its own seed-42 diff; independently confirmed at
crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs:48,79 and scripts/sample_mock.py header.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A recorded decision on which implementation is CORRECT — the Python MT19937 stratification or the
  Rust sampler. Do NOT silently adopt whichever is more convenient; the divergence is a finding and
  the reasoning goes in the bead before either changes.
- The seed-42 golden is regenerated by the AUTHORITATIVE implementation, and export-web no longer
  bypasses the sampler at any seed (or the bypass is retained with an explicit, tested reason).
- A test asserts the Rust assemble() output at a pinned seed MATCHES the golden — i.e. the golden
  exercises the sampler it claims to certify. Known-bad: perturb the sampler, golden goes RED.
- Registered as a SEMANTIC SURFACE in goldens-couplings (B2) so any future re-freeze is deliberate
  and justified.
- Coordinate with C4: whatever PRNG is chosen must be portable and named, and the golden re-frozen
  under it once.
- Until resolved, scripts/sample_mock.py is PINNED — it may not be deleted by the substrate
  migration. Add it to the substrate allowlist with this bead as its migration_bead.

Rust seed-42 sample obtained by running `cdcp export-web --seed 42` from a cwd where the relative
fixture path does not resolve, so the seed-42 bypass could not fire (golden_pinned=false confirmed
in stdout). Bank: 804 items, bank_hash e82817572a82d13fad699393aab97613bdc0cf4c8503e264af490dc8dd7b71db.

ORDER-LEVEL: also fully divergent — 0 of the 3 shared ids sit at the same index.

STRATIFICATION: PRESERVED EQUALLY BY BOTH. Measured per-module counts:
  both cover all 15 modules; both peak at 3 items/module; both satisfy
  max_per_module=8 and min_modules=8. There is NO stratification-quality argument
  for either implementation. The divergence is the PRNG stream, not the algorithm.
  (CPython random.Random = MT19937 vs cdcp_assemble StdRng = ChaCha12.)

SECOND, LARGER FINDING — THE GOLDEN IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE BY ITS OWN PROVENANCE COMMAND.
  goldens/PROVENANCE.md states the fixture was made by
    python3 scripts/sample_mock.py --seed 42 --out goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json
  Re-running that command TODAY yields a different 40-item set: 17 shared, 23 differ.
  Cause: the bank drifted. Committed fixture bank_fingerprint = 0557953e8a49a3cf;
  live bank fingerprint = 5ff22c310349b2bd. scripts/regen_goldens_after_bank.py explicitly
  "does NOT reshuffle mock40 item_ids (fixture stays golden-pinned)", so bank_hash.txt and the
  grade digests were re-pinned against a growing bank while item_ids stayed frozen at the
  2026-08-11 snapshot.
  => The fixture is an ORPHANED artifact. NEITHER implementation reproduces it today.
     It is not a reference for anything; it is a frozen accident.

## DECISION (step 2): the RUST sampler `cdcp_assemble::assemble()` is AUTHORITATIVE.

Reasoning, in the order it decided the question:

1. THE PYTHON SIDE HAS NO CLAIM LEFT. The committed fixture is not what sample_mock.py produces
   today (23/40 differ). Adopting "Python" would not mean adopting the fixture — it would mean
   regenerating the fixture from Python, a change of the same magnitude as adopting Rust. The
   convenience argument for keeping the fixture as-is evaporates once you measure it.
2. RUST IS THE SHIPPED PATH. cdcp_assemble is what export-web runs at every seed != 42, what the
   product's practice forms come from, and what cdcp_wasm grades against. sample_mock.py ships to
   nobody. Pinning a shipped artifact to a non-shipped script is the defect, not the fix.
3. SUBSTRATE LAW. No .py on a load-bearing path. Declaring Python authoritative would permanently
   couple the seed-42 golden to a file the substrate migration is scheduled to delete — the exact
   trap this bead was filed to prevent.
4. NO QUALITY DIFFERENCE TO TRADE AWAY. Measured above: identical module breadth (15), identical
   peak per-module count (3), both inside policy. Choosing Rust costs nothing on the axis the
   sampler exists to serve.
5. RUST ENFORCES GATES PYTHON DOES NOT. sample_item_ids() filters to status==approved (C1) and
   hard-errors on NoApprovedItems / PoolTooSmall / ApprovedTooFewModules. sample_mock.py has no
   status concept and would silently draw draft/retired items. The filter is currently a NO-OP
   (804/804 approved) — not a cause of today's divergence, but a correctness property only Rust has.

Rejected alternative: keep Python authoritative and port MT19937 to Rust. That would import a
non-CSPRNG and a Python-shaped byte-stream contract into the shipped crate in order to preserve an
artifact that is already unreproducible. No.

## C4 INTERACTION (does not pre-empt C4)

This bead does NOT choose the PRNG. It pins the CURRENT PRNG's output and makes it observable.
When C4 replaces StdRng with a portable PRNG, the new assertion (assemble(42).item_ids == golden
fixture item_ids) goes RED — which is the correct and desired behaviour: C4 must re-freeze the
golden once, deliberately, under the portable PRNG. That re-freeze is now a visible gate trip
instead of a silent no-op, because before this bead export-web never called the sampler at seed 42
at all.

title: Class sweep: ten public corpus captures recorded redistribution=not-licensed are published
description:
WHAT: ten body captures under knowledge/corpus/public/ are committed to a PUBLIC repo while manifest.json records each of them rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed":

  src-epi-cdcp-page, src-exin-cdcp-page, src-nh-cdcp, src-tuv-22237,
  src-en-50600-overview, src-tia-942, src-tia-942-c-fotc, src-uptime-tiers,
  src-ocp-ready, src-curriculum-map-local

WHY: this is the SAME defect class already fixed for the two ASHRAE rows under bd-ashrae-redistribution-contradiction-p5n on 2026-08-14 -- retaining a capture for internal grounding and publishing it worldwide are different acts, and the second IS redistribution, which the manifest itself records as not licensed. These ten differ from the ASHRAE pair only in that no publisher AI policy aggravates them. The legal act is identical.

They were NOT removed in that pass, deliberately and on the record: scripts/validate_grounding.py consumes these bodies as its grounding corpus (~601k chars across 804 scanned items). Deleting them without a replacement grounding source would take the build red under four concurrently active agents. That is a cross-cutting change that needs its own bead, not one smuggled into an ASHRAE fix.

They are tracked, not tolerated. Each carries rights_review="OPEN" + rights_review_bead + rights_review_reason in manifest.json, and they are listed under [[open_violation]] in knowledge/corpus/rights-policy.toml. This is a reasoned, bead-referenced exception (CORPUS-R4), not a widened allowlist.

INVARIANT BEING VIOLATED -- CORPUS-R1 (knowledge/corpus/rights-policy.toml):
  no record with redistribution != "permitted" may be capture="body-retained" with a path inside the published tree.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide per source: is redistribution actually permitted (some may be -- OCP specs carry named open licences per document, and src-curriculum-map-local is our own local file that may simply be mis-recorded), or must the body go?
  * If permitted: correct rights/redistribution to the true value with evidence, and the row legitimately stays body-retained.
  * If not: replace with capture="citation-only" carrying {url, title, publisher, fetched_at, rights, redistribution} and zero publisher-derived prose, exactly as the ASHRAE rows were handled.
- Give validate_grounding.py a grounding source that does not depend on unlicensed publisher prose, BEFORE removing bodies. This is the actual blocker; without it the removal is a build break, not a fix.
- After the sweep, [[open_violation]] in rights-policy.toml is EMPTY, and the D4 corpus-rights gate can run CORPUS-R1 with no exceptions.
- Known-bad injection still trips (fixtures already declared in rights-policy.toml [[known_bad]]).

NON-GOALS: do not rewrite git history for these; the ASHRAE HEAD-only reasoning in docs/flywheel/PREPUBLISH-SCRUB-2026-08-14.md applies a fortiori (public web-page captures, no standards body text, repo already public).

title: Gate layer encodes known defects as invariants — rebase off derived facts, not hardcoded bounds
description:
WHAT: Sweep the gate layer for assertions that encode a KNOWN DEFECT as an
invariant, so that fixing the defect fails the gate. Rebase each off derived
facts instead of hardcoded bounds. Add a meta-test per gate proving the gate
still trips on the real bad input after the rebase.

WHY: Found 2026-08-14 while teaching module 15 (C5). Module 15 was assessed but
never taught — the fairness defect C5 closed. THREE independent gates had, over
time, written that defect down as a rule:

  - smoke_learn.py          asserted the hub MUST NOT link to module 15
  - smoke_feedback_links.py skipped module > 14 as "no Learn page required"
  - smoke_weak_links.py     REJECTED module 15 keys as "unexpected"

So the correct fix FAILED THREE GATES FOR BEING CORRECT. An agent without the
context to recognise this would read three red gates as three reasons the fix is
wrong, revert, and leave the defect in place with more evidence behind it than
before. That is worse than an ungated defect: the gate layer has become an
immune system attacking the repair.

THE CLASS, which is the point of this bead: a gate written by observing what the
tree currently does will encode the tree's current defects as requirements. The
defect is not "someone hardcoded 14". It is that the assertion was derived from
OBSERVED STATE rather than from a stated contract. Two sibling instances found
the same day, same root cause, unrelated subsystems:

  - smoke_diagrams.py hardcoded PRESENT to the three P0 diagrams, so it reported
    green without looking at four new P1 diagrams. FIXED (derives from
    docs/DIAGRAM-REGISTRY.md), 3 -> 7.
  - The migration epic enumerated "17 Python gates" from a remembered count;
    smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py were on the check.sh path and in no
    port bead. FIXED (.19/.20 filed).

Known remaining instances (C5 finding 3), both currently satisfied BY LUCK and
not by gate:
  - scripts/verify_coverage.py  range(1,15)  exempts module 15 from the coverage floor
  - scripts/build_units.py      <= 14        exempts module 15 from the micro-check floor

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify_coverage and build_units derive their module set from the same source
  the bank and Learn index use, not from a literal bound. Module 15 is subject to
  the coverage and micro-check floors, or its exemption is a RECORDED row with a
  reason, never a range literal.
- Each rebased gate ships a known-bad injection proving it still trips, AND a
  known-GOOD leg proving it does not refuse legitimate work.
- A grep for numeric module bounds (14, 15, range(1,15), <= 14) across scripts/
  and crates/ returns either zero hits or hits that are each justified in place.
- Anti-vacuous: zero modules discovered is an ERROR in every rebased gate.
- Meta-test per gate: delete the assertion -> selftest non-zero; restore -> 0.
  True exit codes recorded, never read through a pipe.
close_reason: Closed — open instances 5 -> 0, and the sweep is now COMPILED. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs scans scripts/** and crates/** for hardcoded module bounds and requires every hit to carry a verdict row; 23 inventoried, count pinned so it shrinks deliberately and never grows silently. It caught the controller mid-reconciliation, refusing to record '0 open' while a sixth prose line was uninventoried. domains_listed < 14 was removed with an argument rather than renumbered: once the module set derives from domains.toml the check compares the registry against ITSELF. KNOWN LIMIT, filed as bd-ggs7: the detector keys on NUMERIC bounds, so a hand-frozen module TABLE in smoke_weak_links is invisible to it — '0 open' means 'no numeric bound outside the inventory', not 'nothing hand-frozen'.

title: regen_goldens_after_bank.py manufactures the divergence it is checked against
description:
WHAT: scripts/regen_goldens_after_bank.py must call `cdcp goldens fixture`, or be
retired. Today it re-pins every derived digest around FROZEN item_ids.

WHY: Its stated behavior — "does NOT reshuffle mock40 item_ids" — is the exact
mechanism that produced bd-golden-sampler-divergence-09q. Measured 2026-08-14:
goldens/fixtures/mock40_seed42.json could not be reproduced by its own
provenance command. Re-running scripts/sample_mock.py --seed 42 today yields
23/40 different ids, because the bank drifted (fixture bank_fingerprint
0557953e8a49a3cf vs live 5ff22c310349b2bd) while this script froze item_ids and
re-pinned the digests around them. NEITHER implementation reproduced the
committed fixture: it was an orphaned artifact, not a reference.

Post-fix the hazard inverts and gets sharper. cdcp_cli now asserts the fixture
equals cdcp_assemble's output for seed 42. Running this script after a bank edit
re-pins the digests while leaving item_ids stale, which turns that assertion RED
— so the script now MANUFACTURES the divergence its own output is checked
against. A repair tool that reintroduces the fault is worse than no tool,
because it is reached for precisely when someone is trying to fix things.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either: the script regenerates item_ids via `cdcp goldens fixture` (which calls
  cdcp_assemble) before re-pinning any derived digest; or it is deleted and its
  substrate_allowlist row is deleted in the same commit.
- If retained: running it after a bank edit leaves `cargo test -p cdcp_cli`
  GREEN. Prove it — edit a bank item, run the script, run the test, record the
  true exit code.
- Anti-vacuous: a run that regenerates zero goldens is an ERROR, not a pass.
- goldens/PROVENANCE.md states which command is authoritative and which is not.
close_reason: Closed by DELETION, with the argument. It was not a stale-item_ids bug in a working tool: measured on a PRISTINE bank with zero edits it exited 0 printing 'ok' while writing bank_hash af6f14fa… against the Rust law's e8281757…. Three divergent re-implementations of three shipped algorithms, all drifted. grep -c status = 0 — it never read the C1 approved-only field, so 804 items / 0 approved would still have printed ok. Its allowlist reason claimed 'its output is gated by the Rust goldens check' while it wrote both the digests AND the pin that check compares against: it graded its own homework, and the exemption's stated reason was the cover. Repair was rejected because it meant shelling out to three cargo commands — a fourth name for a procedure that already has one, in the substrate we are migrating off. Script and allowlist row deleted together; the guard verified the coupling by erroring on the orphaned row.

title: Flip ported gates from oracle exit codes to cdcp_gate 0/2/3/4 — one commit, after the oracles die
description:
WHAT: After every port lands and the Python oracles are deleted, flip all ported
gates from the oracle's exit codes to cdcp_gate's convention in ONE commit:
0 ok / 2 violation / 3 usage / 4 error. Update crate::exit's doc, check.sh, and
every selftest that asserts a specific code.

WHY: A real fork, raised by the verify_orphans port agent 2026-08-14 rather than
resolved silently — which is why this bead exists instead of a surprise.

crate::exit states "every ported gate returns these and only these" (0/2/3/4).
scripts/verify_orphans.py exits 1 on failure and writes nothing to stderr. Those
cannot both hold. Routing a port through GateError changes the exit code AND adds
a stderr line on every RED, so the differential test — the only mechanism that
can tell a port BUG from an intended FIX — would fail on every red case for
reasons that have nothing to do with the port's correctness.

DECISION (controller, 2026-08-14): byte-exactness wins DURING the migration.
Ported gates reproduce the oracle's exit code, including `std::process::exit(1)`,
and document the departure in the module header. This is safe downstream because
check.sh invokes every gate as `cmd || fail "..."`, which distinguishes only zero
from non-zero; no caller reads the specific code today. Verified before deciding.

The convention is not being abandoned, it is being SEQUENCED. Once an oracle is
deleted there is nothing left to be byte-exact against, and the code becomes free.
Doing it per-gate as each port lands would leave the crate in a mixed state where
a reader cannot tell which convention a given gate follows — worse than either
convention consistently applied.

RISK IF THIS BEAD IS LOST: the crate ships with cdcp_gate's own guard on 0/2/4
and its ported gates on 0/1, with a doc comment asserting a uniformity that does
not hold. That is a false statement in the substrate, and the kind a reader stops
checking. This bead is the reason the departure is temporary rather than a lie.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Blocked until every bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.N port is closed AND its
  oracle .py is deleted with its allowlist row.
- One commit flips all gates; no mixed state is ever committed.
- crate::exit's doc comment matches reality at every commit in between — if the
  mixed state persists, the doc says so explicitly with a pointer to this bead.
- Every selftest asserting a numeric exit code is updated in the same commit.
- Anti-vacuous: a gate returning 0 on an input it could not evaluate is an ERROR
  (4), never a pass, under the new convention.
- Meta-test: a gate forced to violate returns exactly 2; forced to error, 4.

title: verify_orphans.py fails open on 'items = []' — a never-checked bank file reports as passed
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_orphans.py `load_items()` fails open on `items = []`. A bank
file whose entire body is `items = []` is scanned, contributes zero items, and
produces NO error and NO mention. Fix so a file yielding zero items is an ERROR.

WHY: Found 2026-08-14 by the verify_orphans port agent, reproduced faithfully in
the Rust port rather than fixed, and pinned in
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_orphans.rs under a KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT comment
so a change to either side breaks loudly.

    if "items" in data and isinstance(data["items"], list):
        for it in data["items"]: ...      # empty list -> adds nothing, no error
    elif "id" in data: ...
    else: errors.append(f"{path.name}: no id or items[]")

The `elif` never runs for an empty list, so the else-branch that would have
caught it never runs either. Verified empirically: dropping `items = []` into the
specimen bank leaves BOTH implementations at PASS, items=804, rc=0, byte-identical.

This is decalogue rule 3 — "an empty input set is an ERROR, never a pass" —
violated at FILE granularity while the script's own docstring asserts it at
WHOLE-BANK granularity. That gap is the whole defect: a file that was never
really checked reports exactly like one that passed, and the aggregate count
still looks healthy because 804 other items carried it.

Fixed in the Python FIRST, not the Rust, so the differential test keeps working:
change the oracle, watch diff_verify_orphans.rs go RED, then change the port to
match. Fixing the Rust first would make the port non-byte-exact and the test
would flag the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A bank file yielding zero items is reported by name and is non-zero exit.
- Known-bad: `items = []` planted in the live bank -> RED, names the file.
- Known-GOOD: a legitimate single-item file (`id = ...` form, no `items` key)
  still passes — the elif branch must not be broken by the fix.
- diff_verify_orphans.rs updated in the SAME commit; its KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT
  comment is deleted, not amended, because the defect is gone.
- Meta-test: delete the new assertion -> non-zero; restore -> 0. True exit codes.
close_reason: Fixed for verify_orphans, Python first, Rust matched, byte-identical. Controller-verified: a planted 'items = []' beside an 804-item bank is now named and RED in both implementations; before, both reported PASS / items=804 with zero mentions of the file. The KNOWN ORACLE DEFECT pin was DELETED, not amended. NOTE: this closed ONE of FOUR instances — verify_coverage, verify_bank and verify_objectives carried it identically and were closed under bd-0czh, which also added a scan test that parses branches rather than grepping messages.

The reason it read as done is worth recording: all four files have an anti-vacuous check at WHOLE-BANK granularity, so grepping any of them for 'zero items' hits and looks guarded. I made that exact error while auditing — called verify_coverage.py GUARDED off the grep, then read the branch and found the hole. title: Drift guard has three holes — word-spelled counts invisible, wrong file reported, --require double-counts
description:
WHAT: Close three holes in verify_injection_count.py — the DRIFT GUARD itself.
Found 2026-08-14 by its port agent, reproduced faithfully rather than fixed.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this gate is what stops the L4
"gates proven to trip" claim from decaying. It sums the known-bad injections
actually executed and compares them against the number the README advertises.
A hole in the drift guard is a hole in the mechanism that detects every other
hole — the top of the certificate chain.

HOLE 1 — a count spelled in WORDS is invisible.
`_SUITE_COUNT` understands "one".."twelve"; the injection-count regex requires
`\d+`. Rewrite the README badge as "thirty-six known-bad injections" and that
check silently stops covering it. Note the shape carefully: if EVERY digit form
disappears you get "advertises no count at all" -> ERROR, so it fails closed at
the extreme. THE DANGEROUS CASE IS THE MIDDLE — a README where one of the four
advertisement sites is prose. That site just stops being checked, and the gate
stays green because the other three still parse. A partial loss of coverage that
reports identically to full coverage is the exact fooled-certificate shape.

HOLE 2 — findings hardcode `README.md:<lineno>` regardless of `--readme`.
Inside selftest_injection_count.sh this prints `README.md:3` while the file
actually under test is README_off.md. A gate that misreports WHERE the defect is
sends the next reader to an innocent file.

HOLE 3 — a suite named twice in `--require` double-counts.
`total = sum(counts.get(s, 0) for s in required)` iterates `required`, which is
`args.require.split(",")` with no dedup. `--require alpha,alpha` where alpha
reports 3 yields measured_total=6 and registered_suites=2, and prints the suite
row twice. NOT reachable from check.sh (its default roster has no duplicates) but
reachable by any other caller — and inflating measured_total is the direction
that turns a real drift GREEN. A repeated identical receipt LINE does not
double-count (dict assignment overwrites); that asymmetry is pinned by a test.

RELATED, do not fix here but read together: the README "36 injections" badge
counts shell-selftest receipts only. The Rust known-bad legs added 2026-08-14
(6 in cdcp_gate, more per port) are not in that ledger by design. So the
advertised number is drifting from the real injection count for a reason the
gate cannot see. Deciding what the badge is supposed to count is a prerequisite
to fixing hole 1 — otherwise you harden the parser around a number that is
already wrong.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_injection_count.rs go RED, then change the
port to match. Fixing the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the
differential test flags the FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide and RECORD what the injections badge counts (shell receipts only, or
  shell + Rust known-bad legs). The number is regenerated, never hand-maintained.
- Word-spelled counts either parse, or a non-digit count at any advertisement
  site is itself an ERROR. Silent non-coverage is not an option.
- Findings report the file actually scanned, not a hardcoded README.md.
- `--require` dedups, or a duplicate entry is a usage ERROR.
- Known-bad per hole: badge in words -> RED; `--readme X` reporting a path other
  than X -> RED; `--require a,a` -> RED or usage error.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all three fixes.
- Meta-test, stated correctly: MUTATE the gate, confirm the diff test trips, then
  delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm it passes.
  Deleting an assertion on an unmutated tree proves nothing.
close_reason: All three holes closed. Word-spelled counts now parse, plus MIN_ADVERTISEMENT_SITES catches a site dropping out any other way; findings name the file actually scanned; a suite named twice in --require is an ERROR rather than a silent double-count. The agent REJECTED the controller's proposed 'non-digit count is an ERROR' rule after measuring it against the live README, where it fires on innocent prose and would be edited away — an over-strict gate gets routed around, a slower death than no gate. Badge decision recorded: shell receipts only, because Rust legs emit no receipt and hand-typing the number is the defect this gate removes. Advertised total is now REGENERATED (36 -> 47) and the per-suite counts are COMPUTED, not literals.

comments.author: bd-wf2 agent
comments.text:
DECISION (prerequisite) — what the injections badge counts.

The badge counts SHELL-SELFTEST RECEIPTS ONLY: the sum of `INJECTIONS=<n> SUITE=<name>`

The Rust known-bad legs (cdcp_gate #[cfg(test)] cases, and the per-port ones landing this

Reasoning:
1. They emit no receipt. cargo test reports pass/fail, not a count, so there is nothing for

2. Their count is internal to a test binary's own accounting, which the gate cannot observe.
   A Rust leg that silently stopped asserting would be invisible here WHILE inflating the
   advertised number: a fooled certificate on the certificate-checker.
3. Consequence stated honestly rather than hidden: the advertised number is a FLOOR on the
   repo's known-bad population, not its total. README now names the population on the two

   INJECTIONS= receipt, so they are not in this total").
4. Folding them in later is a MECHANISM change, not a number change: the Rust legs must first

title: Three gates print PASS then crash — verdict emitted before a path that can still raise
description:
WHAT: Three gates print PASS (or most of a PASS report) to stdout and THEN die
with an uncaught exception. Make each fail closed BEFORE emitting a verdict.

WHY: A verdict followed by a crash is the worst possible output shape. A reader
skimming stdout sees PASS; CI sees non-zero; the two disagree, and which one wins
depends on whether anyone looked. Worse, any consumer that greps stdout for PASS
— including a human — gets the wrong answer from a gate that actually failed.
All three found 2026-08-14 by port agents, reproduced faithfully rather than
fixed, and pinned in the differential tests.

1. verify_doc_consistency.py — RAGGED ROW. `parse_doc` falls back to the
   heading's status when a data row has fewer cells than the Status column. If
   the heading is not itself a status word the fallback is None, the row is
   recorded with status=None and NO error, and main() then hits
       seen = ",".join(sorted({r["status"] for r in rows}))
   -> TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, NoneType found
   AFTER printing PASS and most of the summary. Trigger: `| M2 | ragged row |`
   under a non-status heading such as `## Notes on the waves`.
   OPEN DECISION for whoever fixes it: status=None should almost certainly be
   fail-closed ("row is shorter than its Status column") rather than rendered as
   the string None. That is a behaviour change, which is why it was not made.

2. verify_bank.py — ZERO EXAM SIZE. `exam_n_items = 0` silently falls back to 40
   because `or` treats 0 as falsy. `exam_n_items = "0"` instead reaches n/exam_n
   and raises ZeroDivisionError after printing three lines of a PASS report. Two
   spellings of the same value, two different wrong behaviours, neither an error.

3. verify_content_lock.py — two uncaught paths: the bank-hash subprocess exits 0
   with output that strips empty, so the oracle does [][-1] -> IndexError; and
   subprocess timeout=300 -> TimeoutExpired.

ALSO IN verify_bank.py, a latent nondeterminism worth fixing in the same pass:
`ALLOWED_CORRECT` is a frozenset and the diversity loop iterates it, so emission
order is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent. Harmless TODAY only because two letters cannot
both exceed 70% (they would sum past 140%), so at most one line is ever emitted.
Lower that threshold below 50% and the gate's output becomes nondeterministic
run to run — which would silently break every byte-exact differential test built
against it. The Rust ports iterate A-D and document why that is currently
equivalent.

ORDERING (load-bearing): fix the PYTHON first, watch the corresponding
crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs go RED, then change the port to match. Fixing
the Rust first makes the port non-byte-exact and the differential test flags the
FIX as the bug.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No gate emits PASS on stdout before a path that can still raise. Verdict is the
  LAST thing written, or it is not written.
- Known-bad per defect: ragged row -> RED naming the row; exam_n_items = "0" and
  = 0 -> both RED or both defaulted, consistently and stated; empty subprocess
  output -> ERROR not IndexError.
- Known-GOOD leg: the live tree still passes after all fixes.
- ALLOWED_CORRECT iterated in a fixed order; a test pins the order.
- The diff_*.rs tests pinning each defect are DELETED (not amended) as each is
  fixed — the pin exists to make the repair deliberate, not permanent.
- Meta-test as the CHARTER now defines it: MUTATE the gate, confirm the suite
  trips, then delete the assertion WITH the mutation still in place and confirm
  it passes. True exit codes, never read through a pipe.
close_reason: All three shares fixed, each Python-first with the port matched byte-identically. verify_doc_consistency: the fix separates a TABLE-level status declaration (heading-supplied, legitimate) from a ROW-level shortfall, and Row::status is now &'static str so an absent status is structurally inexpressible. Second defect inside the first: milestone_rows fell 6 -> 3 because unread rows had been counting toward the anti-vacuous counter — the gate reported having read rows it could not read. verify_bank: policy_positive_int, both zero spellings fail closed. verify_content_lock: empty subprocess output and timeout are typed errors.

title: content.lock gate has no tree-side walk — deleting a row silently stops checking that file
description:
WHAT: verify_content_lock.py has NO tree-side walk. It enumerates only rows
already in content.lock, so a file that is never listed is never checked, and
DELETING a row silently stops checking that file. Add a tree-side sweep, or
state the hole in the gate's own output rather than only in a header comment.

WHY: Confirmed empirically 2026-08-14 by the port agent, both directions:
  - Planted knowledge/smuggled_policy.toml and modules/99-smuggled.md. Both
    implementations exit 0 with `knowledge=9 modules=31` UNCHANGED.
  - Deleted the content.lock row for knowledge/claims.toml, then CORRUPTED that
    file. Both sides stayed GREEN. The only tell was the count moving to
    `knowledge=8` — a number nobody is asserting against anything.

The second direction is the dangerous one and it is the exact fooled-certificate
shape: the gate's coverage is defined by the artifact the gate is checking, so an
attacker (or an ordinary careless commit) removes coverage and the removal looks
identical to a pass. This is L7's content lock — the constellation.lock pattern —
whose entire purpose is "the pinned content still matches". A pin you can delete
without the gate noticing is not a pin.

Note the count IS emitted (`knowledge=9 modules=31`), so the information needed
to catch this is already on stdout. Nothing asserts against it. That is the
cheapest possible first fix: pin the expected counts, so a row deletion is RED.
The fuller fix is a tree-side walk with an explicit ignore list.

RELATED, same class, found the same day: scripts/verify_bank.py and
scripts/verify_knowledge_paths.py both have vacuity holes where zero-checked
reports identically to all-checked (see bd-...-jhd.5's report: a registry whose
every row is a licensed empty prints PASS / primary_notes_checked=0).

ACCEPTANCE:
- A file present under a locked root but absent from content.lock is RED, or the
  gate's OUTPUT states which roots it does not cover. A header comment is not
  sufficient — the reader of a green verdict must be told what it does not mean.
- Deleting a content.lock row is RED. Known-bad: delete the claims.toml row ->
  non-zero.
- Anti-vacuous: zero rows, or zero files discovered under a locked root, is an
  ERROR, never a pass.
- The two tests currently pinning these holes as agreed behaviour
  (`an_unlisted_file_slips_past_both_implementations`,
  `deleting_a_row_silently_stops_checking_that_file_in_both`) are DELETED in the
  same commit, because the behaviour they pin will no longer exist.
- Python first, then the port — the differential test must flag the port, not the fix.
close_reason: Fixed. content.lock now walks the three roots gen_content_lock.py writes rows from, so a regenerated lock is green by construction and any divergence is a real unpinned file. Both directions verified: a planted unlisted file is RED, and DELETING a row no longer silently stops checking that file. GREEN output now states its own scope on stdout — covered roots with counts, and an explicit NOT-covered list — so a green verdict tells the reader what it does not mean. Also wired CDCP_CONTENT_LOCK_SELFTEST, an L4 gate-proven-to-trip leg that existed fully implemented on both sides and that nothing ran. Stated limit, not closed: the walk is one level deep, so knowledge/corpus/x.toml is invisible to both generator and gate — tracked in bd-zhnd.

title: cargo fmt cannot see src/gates/*.rs — audit which other tools stop at the #[path] boundary
description:
WHAT: `cargo fmt --check` cannot see crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs. Decide
whether the glob-based gate registration keeps its `#[path]` indirection (and
check.sh keeps the compensating per-file rustfmt leg added 2026-08-14), or
whether registration changes shape so cargo's own tooling reaches the files.

WHY: The gate modules are pulled in by `#[path = ...]` from a build.rs-generated
OUT_DIR file. `cargo fmt` walks the module tree from src/lib.rs and never
resolves that indirection, so it silently formats and checks NOTHING under
src/gates/.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, not inferred:
  - substrate_guard.rs deliberately misformatted -> `cargo fmt --check` exit 0,
    zero output. `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` on the same file -> exit 1,
    47-line diff.
  - Sweeping all nine gate files with rustfmt found THREE genuinely unformatted:
    install_hooks.rs, substrate_guard.rs, verify_orphans.rs. Two of those were
    already committed in 27a0c2d. They had never been checked by anything.
  - The five port agents that used per-file `rustfmt --check` were clean. The
    ones that relied on `cargo fmt` were not. The tool was the difference.

THIS IS THE COST OF THE PARALLELISM, AND THAT TRADE SHOULD BE MADE DELIBERATELY.
The glob registration is what lets N port agents each add exactly one file with
zero shared-file collisions — verified working under SIX concurrent agents, and
it is the reason 19 ports are parallelisable at all. It is worth keeping. But it
created an unchecked surface, and a green fmt leg over files it never opened is
the same vacuous-scan pattern check.sh hard-fails on everywhere else. The bug is
not that cargo fmt is wrong; it is that we adopted an indirection without
auditing which tools stop working across it.

MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED: check.sh now runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` per
file over the glob, with an anti-vacuous floor (zero gate files scanned = ERROR).
Proven to trip: misformatted gate -> exit 2 naming the file; empty glob -> exit 2.
That closes fmt specifically. This bead exists because fmt is unlikely to be the
only tool that cannot cross a `#[path]`/OUT_DIR boundary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Enumerate every tool in the chain that walks the module tree rather than the
  filesystem, and state for each whether it reaches src/gates/*.rs. At minimum:
  cargo fmt, clippy, rustdoc, cargo-mutants, tarpaulin/llvm-cov, cargo-udeps.
  `clippy --all-targets` is believed to reach them because it compiles; CONFIRM
  that by misformatting-equivalent injection, do not assume it.
- For each tool that does NOT reach them, either a compensating per-file leg with
  an anti-vacuous floor, or a recorded decision that the tool is not required.
- A meta-test per compensating leg: it trips on a known-bad file AND errors on an
  empty glob.
- If the decision is to change registration shape instead, the six-way-concurrent
  no-collision property must be preserved and re-demonstrated, not assumed.
close_reason: Shape A: #[path] kept; rustfmt_gate_modules compensating leg + L4 plant/empty/only-mod.rs. SHA 57152d1eddb5ca3d06576ae380f5a704d37f6f72

comments.author: josh
comments.text: claimed 3/4/2. isolate. do not push. do not weaken rustfmt/clippy.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: shape A: keep #[path]+glob registration (B would edit a shared mod.rs and fight gate_shrink/build.rs + 6-way no-collision). strengthening the compensating rustfmt leg + L4 plant/empty-glob meta-test. will audit clippy/rustdoc/mutants/llvm-cov/udeps by measurement, not assumption. isolate: no rustfmt of jhd.13/gna0/pi0v/4qje files.

comments.text:
VERDICT: PASS. Shape A. SHA 57152d1eddb5ca3d06576ae380f5a704d37f6f72

Decision: keep #[path] + glob registration (B would edit a shared mod.rs and fight build.rs / gate_shrink / 6-way no-collision).

Tool audit, measured 2026-08-15, not inferred:
- cargo fmt: BLIND. Plant `install-hooks"     ;` in install_hooks.rs → rustfmt --check rc=1 naming the file; cargo fmt --check -p cdcp_gate rc=0/1 with ZERO mention of install_hooks.
- rustfmt --edition 2021 per-file: REACH. Compensating leg rustfmt_gate_modules() in check.sh.
- clippy -p cdcp_gate --lib --bins --no-deps -- -D warnings: REACH. Unused-binding plant named src/gates/install_hooks.rs:64. No compensating clippy leg.
- rustdoc / cargo test --doc: REACH. Broken doctest plant FAILED as gates::install_hooks::run. cargo test --workspace already runs doctests. cargo doc HTML is not a check.sh step — not required.
- cargo-mutants: not in check.sh, not installed — not required.
- cargo-tarpaulin / llvm-cov: not in check.sh (tarpaulin is on PATH, unused) — not required.
- cargo-udeps: not in check.sh, not installed; walks the dep graph not source modules — not required.

L4 meta-test (same function as the live scan):
- planted space/indent → RED (rustfmt --check failed: plant.rs)
- empty glob → ERROR (scanned 0 #[path] gate files)
- only-mod.rs (the file cargo fmt can see) → ERROR
- formatted non-mod.rs → GREEN (always-fail would spoof the plants)
