title: The .wasm is an eighth frozen artifact, and the coupling ledger does not know it exists
description:
WHAT: web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm is a COMMITTED BINARY (299KB, last built 2026-08-12, commit ef12275). It compiles cdcp_core + cdcp_bank + cdcp_grade, so it embeds hash_payload, canonical_json and the grader — exactly the surfaces registries/goldens-couplings.toml pins. It is not a [[golden]] row, and B2 discovery only sweeps goldens/, so nothing declares the coupling.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: after C2 changed hash_payload and the four-command block re-froze all seven declared goldens, the committed .wasm still computed the PRE-C2 address. smoke_results_wasm.mjs failed with: bank_hash mismatch: attempt has 173057eb… bank has e82817572a82d13f… — a two-day-old binary disagreeing with the tree about what a bank hash means. Rebuilding via scripts/build_web_wasm.sh fixed it (287330 -> 299556 bytes).

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: check.sh DID catch it, at L5, by a runtime digest comparison ~530 lines in — the same late/indirect signal B2 was built to replace. The ledger says a re-freeze cannot happen silently; that claim is true only for the seven artifacts it lists. An eighth frozen artifact sat outside it and went stale for two days. The gap is not that the repo is unguarded, it is that the LEDGER OVERSTATES ITS COVERAGE while the thing it misses is a shipped binary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [[golden]] row for web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm with depends_on naming bank.hash-payload, bank.item-schema, core.canonical-json, core.grade-report-shape, core.choice-letter and a justification for each.
- The B2 discovery leg is widened past goldens/ so an undeclared frozen binary is RED. Decide and record what counts as a frozen artifact — a committed build output is the class, not the directory.
- Known-bad: rebuild the wasm without re-affirming -> RED naming the surface, not just the file.
- Anti-vacuous: zero discovered frozen artifacts is an ERROR.
- goldens/PROVENANCE.md records that build_web_wasm.sh is part of the regeneration path, since the four-command block does not currently produce it.
close_reason:
CLOSED. web/assets/wasm/cdcp_wasm.wasm is now the eighth [[golden]] row in registries/goldens-couplings.toml (line 527). Verified independently: goldens-couplings exits 0 with goldens=8 couplings=41, up from goldens=7 couplings=34.

The bd-6ycw agent added it mid-walk because it was already re-freezing the wasm for the domain bump and the row was cheap at that moment — the right call, and it says so rather than leaving it implied.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTED: the ledger claimed no golden could be silently re-frozen, and that claim was true only for the seven artifacts it listed. An eighth frozen artifact — a committed 299KB binary compiling hash_payload, canonical_json, the grader and the domain constant — sat outside the goldens/ discovery sweep and went TWO DAYS STALE computing a pre-C2 bank_hash. check.sh caught it at L5 by runtime digest comparison, which is the late, indirect signal B2 exists to replace. A ledger that overstates its coverage is the exact shape milestone B is about.

RESIDUAL, NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the DISCOVERY leg still only sweeps goldens/. The wasm is now declared, so a re-freeze of it is RED — but a NINTH frozen artifact appearing somewhere else would be just as invisible as the wasm was. The bead's acceptance asked for the discovery leg to be widened past goldens/ and for a written decision on what counts as a frozen artifact (a committed build output is the class, not the directory). That half is unaddressed and is worth its own bead if a ninth ever appears; recording it here rather than pretending the acceptance was fully met.

title: build_units: two input registries can vanish entirely and the gate still reports GREEN
description:
WHAT: scripts/build_units.py (and therefore the byte-exact port cdcp_gate build-units) treats two missing input registries as ordinary, not as errors. Found by the differential harness for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.12 and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, because a port stricter than its oracle blinds the whole differential.

              load_topics_by_domain returns {}, every unit gets topic_ids: [], and the picker
              reads an empty topic set as "no preference" rather than "nothing to match", so it
              still fills each unit from the module pool.
  u-noindex   web/data/modules_index.json deleted -> exit 0, PASS: units=134 modules=16
              silently globs web/content/modules/*.md instead, which sweeps in README.md.
              The module set the docstring calls DERIVED is absent and nobody hears about it,

web/data/units_index.json feeds the Learn surface. An input registry disappearing produces a
report that is indistinguishable from one that checked everything — 134 units either way. The
16-vs-15 case is worse than silent: it is a green verdict carrying a wrong number.

tests/diff_build_units.rs go RED on u-notopics and u-noindex, and only then move the port. Fixing
the port first makes the differential flag the FIX as the divergence.

    duplicates says module 15. The import from `practice/PRACTICE-EXAM.md` numbered files by
    practice-exam question order and derived `module` from that numbering, not from the item's

- Every `mock40-*` item's `module` re-checked against the content of its stem, not against its

  only if the scan is shown to have run.

  floor the rest of the suite uses.

title: verify-objectives topic coverage is skipped entirely when knowledge/topics.toml is absent
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs:1368 opens the L7 topic-coverage section with `if Path::new(&topics_disp).is_file() { ... }`. The else-branch at ~1443 that would catch an empty topic set ALSO requires `is_file()`. So when knowledge/topics.toml (DEFAULT_TOPICS, line 152) is absent, neither branch runs: no topic is checked, no error is raised, and the gate reports the same verdict it reports when every topic is covered.

CONTRAST: the same function DOES fail closed for its other inputs — objectives_disp and claims_disp both go through `if !Path::new(..).is_file() { return Err }` at ~1139/1142. topics_disp is the one input that was left optional without a written reason.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the same absent-input-reads-as-success shape as bd-goldens-check-is-file-hole-7v9p, which was just closed in cdcp_cli. Six instances of this shape are now on record in this repo. Found during the cdcp_cli sweep; NOT fixed there because cdcp_gate/src/gates/ was out of scope for that bead.

ACCEPTANCE:
- An absent knowledge/topics.toml is an ERROR in verify-objectives, or the code carries a written reason why the topic section is legitimately optional.
- Known-bad: move knowledge/topics.toml aside, run the gate ALONE, get non-zero naming the file. Show the real exit code.
- Meta-test pair: mutate the detector -> suite non-zero; with the mutation still in place delete the assertion -> suite zero.

title: wasm dual-path test reports ok in the plain workspace run when no wasm artifact exists
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_wasm/tests/dual_path.rs::native_equals_wasm_mock40_seed42 returns early with `eprintln!("SKIP wasm dual-path: ...")` when ensure_wasm_built() cannot produce an artifact. cargo test scores an early return as PASS, so in the plain `cargo test --locked --workspace` step of scripts/check.sh (~line 466) the differential test that compares native against wasm reports ok having compared nothing.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT: check.sh has a dedicated L4 leg at ~line 494 that sets CDCP_REQUIRE_WASM=1 and hard-fails, and it prints an honest SKIP with L4_WASM=SKIP when the toolchain is missing. So the wave-level accounting is honest. The hole is narrower: one line in the test output says ok for a comparison that did not happen, and anyone reading the workspace test summary sees a green differential test.

WHY IT MATTERS: same absent-input-reads-as-success shape as bd-goldens-check-is-file-hole-7v9p. Low severity because a second gate covers it — which is exactly the reasoning that bead rejected as sufficient. Found during the cdcp_cli sweep; not fixed there because cdcp_wasm was out of scope.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either the test names its skip in a way cargo cannot score as a pass, or the code carries a written reason why a silent skip is legitimately fine here and points at the check.sh leg that makes it non-vacuous.
- Cheapest candidate fix: have check.sh export CDCP_REQUIRE_WASM=1 for the workspace test step whenever the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is installed, so the default run cannot skip when it could have compared.
- Show the real exit code for both the skipping and the enforcing run.

title: The bound sweep cannot see a floor moved behind a named constant - build_glossary_json.py MIN_TERMS left the ledger silently
description:
WHAT: scripts/build_glossary_json.py used to read 'if len(terms) < 15:' and had an INVENTORY row in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs with verdict NotAModuleBound. On 2026-08-14 a sibling rebased it onto MIN_TERMS = 15 at line 46. The floor did not move. The literal did, behind a named constant, which is one of the spellings the sweep header states it cannot see.

HOW IT SURFACED: the stale row was caught by the STRICTER assertion added in bd-ggs7 - every INVENTORY row must be matched by the detector it names. The previous count-based assertion (matched.len() >= INVENTORY.len()) had gone green over the same tree hours earlier. The row was deleted with a comment recording why.

WHY IT MATTERS: MIN_TERMS is harmless (a glossary term-count floor, not a module bound). The pattern is not. Any live module bound can be made invisible to the sweep by naming it, and the sweep would then report a smaller open count without anything having been fixed. A refactor that improves the code silently shrinks the ledger.

OPTIONS:
- Detect assignments of the form NAME = 13..16 and require them to be inventoried too. Cheap, noisy, and honest.
- Or scope the claim: state in the sweep header and in the open-count assertion message that a named constant is out of scope, and accept that the count is narrower than it reads. This is already stated, but the count still reads broader than it is.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Either the detector sees numeric module bounds bound to a name, with a known-bad that plants one and goes RED naming file and line, or the narrowed claim is stated at the count itself and not only in the header.
- Anti-vacuous: a detector added here must have a planted-input test proving it trips, not only the live tree.
close_reason: DETECTED, not narrowed. Shape::NamedBound added; three new hits, all adjudicated; open count still 0 and now states what it does not cover.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: closed by adding a detector, argued against narrowing the claim.

THE CHOICE. Detect the named-constant shape rather than narrow the claim in writing. The deciding fact is measured, not aesthetic: widening surfaced TWO lines nobody had in mind when the blind spot was written up — 'pub const MIN_TERMS: usize = 15;' in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/build_glossary_json.rs (the Rust port of the very gate that produced this bead) and 'const REPR_FIXED_MAX: i32 = 16;' in crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/validate_grounding.rs. A narrowed CLAIM would have been accurate about the one line that prompted it and silent about the two it did not know existed. A written narrowing describes the hole; only a detector finds what is in it. The residual narrowing is still stated, at the count itself and not only in the header, because the count reads broader than three detectors.

THE DETECTOR. named_bound(line) -> Option<u32>. THE WHOLE LINE MUST BE THE BINDING: optional declaration keywords (pub/const/static/let/mut/var/readonly/export/local), a dotted identifier, an optional ': TYPE' annotation, a plain '=' (not '==', not '=>'), exactly two digits in 13..=16 not part of a longer number or a float, then end-of-line / ';' / ',' / a comment. A leading '#', '//' or '*' is refused outright — PROSE IS NOT LIVE CODE, the error this suite has made three times.

THREE NEW HITS, EACH WITH A VERDICT (measured over scripts/, crates/, web/assets/js/):
  scripts/build_glossary_json.py:46  MIN_TERMS = 15                  NotAModuleBound - the glossary TERM-count floor; the line that produced this bead
  crates/.../gates/build_glossary_json.rs:110  pub const MIN_TERMS: usize = 15;  NotAModuleBound - same floor, Rust port; found only by widening
  crates/.../gates/validate_grounding.rs:288   const REPR_FIXED_MAX: i32 = 16;   NotAModuleBound - CPython float-repr cutoff; the named twin of the already-inventoried 'decpt > 16' in verify_bank.rs
None is a module bound. PINNED OPEN COUNT STAYS 0, and its message now enumerates both what the zero covers (three shapes x three trees) and what it does not (computed bounds, config-read bounds, names bound to non-integers, tables split across files, trees outside SCANNED).

KNOWN-GOOD LEGS, one per legitimate 12-16 shape actually in this tree: the 15-minute reading-time floor (learn_chrome.js 'if (min < 15) min = 15;'), both mulberry32 shifts ('>>> 15', '>>> 14'), the 16-char hash truncation (results.js), the argparse 'default=15' (validate_grounding.py), the unnamed term-count comparison (smoke_learn_v2.py), two TOML fixture strings inside Rust source, four prose/comment forms, an equality test, a macro call, a match arm, a bound expression, 150 / 15.5 / 1400, a struct field, a tuple element. 21 cases, all assert None. Measured false positives on the live tree: ZERO.

ANTI-VACUOUS. SCANNED floors unchanged (scripts 40, crates 45, web/assets/js 12); the scan SET did not change, so they were re-measured, not re-derived: the trees hold 45, 63 and 16 files today (crates was 55 earlier the same day — it is the tree that churns, which is why its floor is not pinned to its count). the_per_tree_file_floors_reject_a_tree_that_vanished still proves each floor rejects a vanished tree.

META-TEST PAIR, real exit codes, run on a clean HEAD clone:
  mutation: appended a DEAD 'MAX_MODULE = 14' to scripts/smoke_weak_links.py. Behaviourally invisible, proven: script exit 0 before AND after, stdout byte-identical (diff exit 0). Only the detector can see it.
  leg 1 (mutation, assertion present):  cargo test --test rebase_module_bounds -> EXIT 101, 'scripts/smoke_weak_links.py:284: [named-bound] MAX_MODULE = 14 [binds 14 to a name]'
  leg 2 (mutation STILL IN PLACE, unexpected.is_empty() assertion deleted): EXIT 0, 40 passed.
Plus a planted-tree leg in the suite itself: the_sweep_goes_red_on_a_module_bound_hidden_behind_a_name plants a gate whose ceiling is 'MAX_MODULE = 14' with 'int(m[:2]) <= MAX_MODULE' below it, asserts NumericBound sees nothing there, and asserts NamedBound names file and line.

VERIFIED: rebase_module_bounds 40 passed / 0 failed on a clean HEAD clone; rustfmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean. Residual blind spot tracked as bd-ob8i.

title: verify_coverage prints its PASS verdict before a write that can still fail (class instance 3 of 3)
description:
WHAT: the third and last live instance of the PASS-above-FAIL class, found by the exhaustive census run for bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65. It arrives through a different door than the first two: the verdict is not printed above a FAIL line, it is printed above a SIDE EFFECT THAT CAN STILL FAIL.

  scripts/verify_coverage.py:335-336   status = "PASS" if not errors else "FAIL"; print(status)
  ...57 lines later...
  scripts/verify_coverage.py:393-394   out.parent.mkdir(...); out.write_text(...)   <- unguarded

  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs:1024-1025  status pushed into the out buffer
  crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs:1102,1105  the only fallible `?` sites after it,
                                                           each mapping to Halt

On the Python side there is no try/except in main() covering the write, so an OSError (bad path, read-only destination, ENOSPC, permissions) propagates and CPython exits 1 with a traceback underneath a stdout that already said PASS. On the Rust side Halt is not discarded: evaluate maps it to Outcome { stdout: out, stderr: traceback, code: 1 }, which PRESERVES the already-buffered PASS, and run then prints that stdout and exits 1. Stdout says PASS, the process says 1.

REACHABILITY: the path requires --write-json. check.sh invokes `cdcp_gate verify-coverage` without it, so it is dormant in CI today. It is NOT dead code: it is the documented operator command, embedded in the artifact its own `note` field prints (verify_coverage.py:383-385, "Regenerate via: python3 scripts/verify_coverage.py --write-json web/data/coverage.json").

WHY THIS IS A CLASS AND NOT A THIRD BUG: bd-lt7 fixed instance 1 (build_units.py). bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 fixed instance 2 (build_glossary_json.py plus its Rust port). This is instance 3. Three instances of one shape means the fix is a DETECTOR, not a third patch. The detector that already exists and is proven is the per-side leg qm65 added to both builder differentials:

    for (side, r) in [("python", &py), ("rust", &rs)] {
        if r.code != 0 { assert!(!r.out().contains("PASS"), ...); }
    }

asserted PER SIDE rather than only across the two, because a differential only catches a regression that lands on one side, and two implementations that both regress agree with each other perfectly. That leg was proven to be the detector by a mutation pair: mutate BOTH sides to print PASS first and the suite goes non-zero on 3 cases; delete the leg with the mutation still in place and the suite returns to zero.

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify_coverage.py and verify_coverage.rs both compose the report AFTER the --write-json write, so a failed write cannot land under a PASS. Both sides move together, PYTHON FIRST, and the verify_coverage differential is watched go RED before the port follows.
- The no-success-token-on-a-non-zero-path leg is added to the verify_coverage differential harness, per side, matching the two builder harnesses.
- A meta-test pair proves that leg is the detector: mutate both implementations back, suite non-zero; delete the assertion with the mutation STILL IN PLACE, suite zero.
- The census that found this is re-run and reports ZERO remaining instances, so the class is CLOSED rather than decremented.

NOT IN SCOPE, recorded so it is not re-derived:
- verify_objectives writes a provisional PASS into its JSON summary before later errors could be appended, but the only thing that appends after that point is the write-failure handler, which uses `if let Err(e)` rather than `?`. A successful write therefore implies exit 0, and a failed write implies stdout FAIL. The one residual hole is a torn file from a mid-write ENOSPC, which is not a verdict surface a reader trusts. Both ports get this right and are commented for it.
- scripts/verify_content_lock.py:348 prints an `ok` line inside a `try` whose `finally` can raise PermissionError. Same class, negligible probability, no action.

FOUND BY: exhaustive census of scripts/*.{py,sh,mjs}, crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs, crates/*/src/**/*.rs and hooks/ during bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65, tracing forward from every success print to every reachable exit. check.sh is clean (fail() exits 2, so no `ok` line is reachable after a failure). All 12 selftest_*.sh, the .mjs smokes, and the remaining 16 Rust gates are clean.
close_reason: verdict composed after the write in both implementations; per-side detector added and proven by a mutation pair (101 -> 0); general detector argued and filed as bd-j8b2 [bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n]

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: FIXED and verified. Both implementations now COMPOSE the report into a buffer and emit it only after the --write-json side effect has succeeded. A failed write prints NOTHING and exits non-zero. The write is atomic (temp file beside the target, then rename), so a refused or torn write leaves no partial artifact.

RED-BEFORE-PORT, observed: Python first, diff_verify_coverage RED on 13 of 17 (the same change also carried the approved-pool fix from bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh); port followed, back to green.

KNOWN-BAD, both sides, two doors, four-tuple read from the emitted exit code:
  (a) --write-json whose PARENT IS A FILE (mkdir refuses)
      python exit=1 stdout=0 bytes stderr=1170 bytes artifact=NO tmp_residue=NO
      rust   exit=1 stdout=0 bytes stderr=147 bytes  artifact=NO tmp_residue=NO   stdout IDENTICAL
  (b) --write-json TARGET IS A DIRECTORY (the atomic rename refuses AFTER the temp write — the leg that proves the cleanup)
      python exit=1 stdout=0 bytes tmp_residue=NO
      rust   exit=1 stdout=0 bytes tmp_residue=NO   stdout IDENTICAL
  the SAME failing write against the PRE-FIX implementation: exit=1, first stdout line 'PASS', 642 bytes of report.
Chosen over a chmod because a file-as-parent and a directory-as-target are deterministic and cannot be defeated by running as root — an injection that silently stops injecting is the failure this file exists to prevent.

DETECTOR, added per side to every case in the harness: assert_no_success_token_on_a_failing_path, keyed on SUCCESS_TOKENS = [PASS, coverage GREEN]. Per side and not merely across the two, because a differential only catches a regression that lands on ONE side — and that is not hypothetical here: the Python printed above an unguarded write and the Rust buffered the same verdict into Outcome.stdout, which Halt preserves. The two agreed, byte for byte, on a PASS above exit 1.

META-TEST PAIR, real exit codes:
  1. MUTANT-A planted on BOTH implementations (the printed verdict is always the success token; exit codes, the JSON status field, stdout emptiness and artifacts all untouched, so only the verdict-shape leg can catch it)
     -> cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test diff_verify_coverage  EXIT 101, 12 failed / 11 passed, all 12 on 'with the success token'
  2. MUTANT-A STILL IN PLACE, the single assertion deleted
     -> EXIT 0, 23 passed / 0 failed
  3. both restored -> EXIT 0, 23 passed. grep for MUTANT in the three files: 0.
Nothing else in the suite catches that mutation, which is what makes this the detector rather than a coincidence.

GENERAL DETECTOR — ARGUED, NOT SKIPPED, and filed as bd-j8b2. The static form (grep for a success token on a path reachable by a non-zero exit) is rejected: sound analysis needs interprocedural reachability across two languages, and the cheap approximation fires on every CORRECT gate (verify_coverage.py buffers PASS and returns 1 from the same function, correctly). Re-running the census with an AST scan produced exactly the predicted false positives — verify_injection_count.py:275 matched because a FAIL message QUOTES the word GREEN, and fetch_public_corpus.py:167 matched a per-item progress line. That is the same fooling recorded in the bd-0czh comment in this very file. The shared-composition-helper form is sound but opt-in and does not cross the Python/Rust boundary. The tractable form is a META-GATE asserting every diff_*.rs carries the per-side leg; measured 2026-08-14 that is 3 of 11 harnesses, so landing it would have turned EIGHT sibling-owned files RED mid-swarm for a defect none of them has been shown to have. bd-j8b2 carries the measurement, the roster, and the per-gate-token problem the implementer must solve.

CENSUS RE-RUN: AST scan over scripts/*.py plus a narrowed scan of the eight Rust gates that write a file. ZERO remaining genuine instances. The residual verify_content_lock.py:348 hole this bead already recorded as no-action is unchanged. The class is CLOSED for shipped code; bd-j8b2 is what keeps a FOURTH instance from being written tomorrow.

title: verify-coverage counts retired items toward module floors — it measures the file set, not the drawable pool
description:
WHAT: `cdcp_gate verify-coverage` and `cdcp_gate verify-bank` count every FILE under `bank/items`
toward the per-module floors in `knowledge/bank_policy.toml`. They do not filter on `status`. So
they measure a pool no learner is ever assessed from.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, immediately after bd-tetz retired 24 duplicates:

    verify-coverage:  m14: 44 (min 24) [ok]        <- 44 files
    actual drawable:  m14: 42 approved             <- what cdcp_assemble can sample
    verify-bank:      modules={... 14: 44 ...}     <- same file count
    near-duplicate-items: 804 item file(s) · 779 approved

C1 restricts assembly to `approved` items (`cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids`), and C2 folded
`status` into `hash_payload` precisely because the approved/retired split decides what a learner
can be assessed on. The coverage gate is the one place that asserts a module has ENOUGH items, and
it is measuring the other set.

NO LIVE BREACH TODAY — checked, and this is why it is a bug rather than an incident. Approved-only
counts after the 24 retirements, against their floors:

    m05 30/14  m06 130/55  m07 31/14  m08 32/18  m09 117/48  m10 33/12
    m11 69/30  m12 61/28   m13 46/22  m14 42/24  (all other modules unchanged)

Every module clears its floor on the approved pool as well. The defect is that the gate WOULD NOT
HAVE SAID SO if one did not: a module could be retired below its floor and `verify-coverage` would
print `[ok]` while `cdcp_assemble` quietly assembled a narrower exam. The gate reports a number
that is guaranteed to be >= the number it should be reporting, which is the fail-open direction.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: before bd-tetz the bank held exactly one non-approved item, so
file count and approved count differed by one and no reader would notice. It is 25 now, and will
grow every time a duplicate is adjudicated.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `verify-coverage` counts `status == "approved"` items against `domain_min`, and its output names
  BOTH numbers (files scanned, approved counted) so the two can never be confused again.
- Anti-vacuous, per house rule: a module with zero approved items is an ERROR naming the module,
  never a `[ok]` on a file count.
- Known-bad injection: retire a temp module below its floor -> the gate goes RED naming that
  module. Meta-test: delete the filter -> the injection test fails.
- Decide the same question for `verify-bank`'s `modules={...}` and `correct_dist={...}` summaries.
  Correct-letter diversity over a pool that includes retired items is measuring the wrong pool for
  the same reason. If the file-count view is deliberate there, say so in the output.
- `scripts/verify_coverage.py` (the differential oracle, if it still exists) moves in the same
  change or the diff test goes RED — do not let the two sides disagree about which pool they count.
close_reason: floors measure the approved pool; before/after table recorded, no breach, no floor lowered; known-bad proven against the pre-fix binary [bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh]

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: FIXED and verified. Both implementations count status == 'approved' against the floors; every line of the report that carries a count now names BOTH numbers.

BEFORE/AFTER, every module, live tree (804 files, 779 approved, 25 retired). Format module: files->approved/floor:
  m01 36->36/20  m02 42->42/28  m03 38->38/20  m04 33->33/18  m05 31->30/14
  m06 136->130/55  m07 32->31/14  m08 34->32/18  m09 121->117/48  m10 35->33/12
  m11 72->69/30  m12 63->61/28  m13 48->46/22  m14 44->42/24  m15 39->39/16
NO MODULE BREACHES. The ten deltas sum to 25, the whole retired set, so no retirement is unaccounted for. NO FLOOR WAS LOWERED.

RED-BEFORE-PORT, observed: the Python moved first and diff_verify_coverage went RED on 13 of 17 cases (python printed 'm14: 42 approved of 44 scanned', rust still printed 'm14: 44'). The port then followed and the suite returned to 17/17, now 23/23 with the new cases.

KNOWN-BAD, the one the old code could not trip: retire 19 approved items of m14 in a TEMP COPY without deleting a file.
  pre-fix  (git show HEAD:scripts/verify_coverage.py): exit 0, 'm14: 44 (min 24) [ok]', 'coverage GREEN'
  post-fix (both implementations, byte-identical): exit 1, 'm14: 23 approved of 44 scanned (min 24) [SHORT]',
           'module 14: 23 approved < min 24 (44 scanned, 21 not approved)'
Same 804 files in both runs. The differential case asserts the SCANNED count is UNCHANGED and still clears the floor, so it cannot pass by accident.

ANTI-VACUOUS: zero items, zero modules, zero required-after-exemptions, and now zero APPROVED are each an ERROR naming the condition. A status outside the C1 lifecycle is an ERROR naming the item rather than a silent drop into not-approved; an ABSENT status is the draft default and is not an error.

LEDGER: web/data/coverage.json regenerated from a TREE COPY (never the live tree) and byte-identical to what both implementations produce. schema_version 2 -> 3 because counts changed population; approved_count and scanned_counts added so both populations are in the ledger. A differential case asserts the produced bytes equal the TRACKED artifact — the read-only proof that running either implementation in the live tree would be a no-op write.

verify-bank was DECIDED, not skipped: same defect (pool_min, modules={}, correct_dist={} all count the file set; 779 vs floor 400, no live breach). Filed as bd-8exw rather than fixed here, because verify_bank.py/.rs were owned by another agent in the same wave.

title: web/data/bank_items_seed42.json ships 25 retired items to the browser
description:
WHAT: `web/data/bank_items_seed42.json` is the full bank array serialised straight off `BankItem`
and shipped to the browser for the WASM grade path. After bd-tetz it carries 804 elements of which
**25 have `status = "retired"`** — items `cdcp_assemble` can never draw, in a pack whose whole
purpose is grading a 40-item draw.

MEASURED 2026-08-14, parsed from the committed pack:

    len(bank_items_seed42.json)         = 804
    statuses present                    = ["approved", "retired"]
    elements with status == "retired"   = 25
    items the seed-42 form actually uses = 40

THREE REASONS THIS IS WORTH DECIDING RATHER THAN LEAVING:

 1. It is the only place a retired item reaches a learner's browser. Nothing in the current web
    code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids, so there is no live bug — but the pack is the
    input to any future "review the whole bank" or "search items" surface, and the first such
    surface will silently include withdrawn duplicates. A retired item is retired BECAUSE a better
    copy of the same proposition exists; showing it is showing the copy that lost.
 2. It carries the retired items' full text, so the 24 duplicate stems and keys are still shipped
    beside their survivors — the exact adjacency the retirement was meant to remove.
 3. The count is a trap. `registries/goldens-couplings.toml` used to describe this file as "the
    full 804-item array"; that row was rewritten under bd-tetz to say 804 is a FILE count and 779
    is the drawable pool, but the pack itself still hands 804 to anyone who calls `.length`.

NOT FIXED HERE because `export_web` lives in `crates/cdcp_cli/src/main.rs`, outside the bank/goldens
surface bd-tetz owned, and the pack's byte content is `cmp`d by `scripts/check.sh` L6 — changing
what it contains is a goldens re-freeze plus a coupling walk, which is a decision, not a tidy-up.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide, and record in the `web.bank-items-pack` row of `registries/goldens-couplings.toml`:
  does this pack ship the drawable pool (779) or the file set (804)?
- If it becomes approved-only, `export.pack-shapes` moves, the pack re-freezes, and all three web
  goldens re-affirm through the block in `goldens/PROVENANCE.md`, in order.
- Either way the pack gains something a reader can check the count against — an envelope field, or
  a `status` the consumer is required to read — so `.length` stops being quotable as the item count.
- Whatever is decided, `cdcp_wasm`'s dual-path test must still pass: the grade path needs every id
  the fixture draws, and only those.
close_reason: done

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
VERDICT: DECIDED + GUARDED here; the two live learner-facing defects filed as bd-7big (P0) and bd-qqwc (P1).

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND MEASUREMENT DISPROVED IT. It said 'nothing in the current web code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids, so there is no live bug'. There is. Two independent live exposures:

1. MODULE QUIZ (bd-7big, P0). web/assets/js/quiz.js filterByModule() filters by numeric module ONLY, never status. Transcribed its mulberry32 sampler + seed derivation (42 + module*1000, +15 for learn15) into node and ran it against the committed pack — the draw is deterministic, so these are exact, not probabilistic: 8 retired items served across the 30 module quizzes, 6 of 15 default quizzes affected (m05-q200, mock40-q18, mock40-q24, mock40-q22, m12-q219, mock40-q37; learn15: m05-q200, mock40-q40). The learner is SCORED on them: gradeByKeys counts them, WASM gradeDigest digests them, recordGradedWrongs pushes misses into cdcp.drill.missed.v1 + SRS, recordQuizResult feeds mastery.
2. LEARN-PAGE UNIT CHECKS (bd-qqwc, P1). build_units never reads status, so web/data/units_index.json already bakes retired ids into check_item_ids: 05-lighting__formulas-rules-of-thumb -> m05-q200, 11-network__formulas-rules-of-thumb -> m11-q226.
Drill/results are transitive only (they look up ids the learner already answered). scripts/export_anki.py also unfiltered -> bd-fqpp (P3).

DECISION — the pack is THE CONTENT-ADDRESSED MANIFEST OF THE WHOLE BANK (804 files), not the drawable pool (779). RECORDED IN: registries/goldens-couplings.toml web.bank-items-pack justification, and web/data/README.md with the reasoning.

THE DECISION IS FORCED, NOT STYLISTIC — and this is why 'just filter the export' would have been a product outage. cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds the pack bytes to Bank::from_json_str which RECOMPUTES bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade HARD-FAILS on mismatch. Measured with cdcp bank-hash: 804-file bank = 3404d854..., 779 approved-only pool = b81a0019... (pre-bump). title: CI is RED at install-hooks --check: actions/checkout never installs the shim, and nothing in check.sh installs it either
description:
WHAT: scripts/check.sh line 313-315 runs `cdcp_gate install-hooks --check` and hard-fails. .github/workflows/check.yml runs check.sh on a fresh actions/checkout@v4, which has no .git/hooks/pre-commit. Nothing between the checkout and that line installs one.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 on a fresh clone of this repo (the closest local analogue of a CI checkout):
  git clone --no-hardlinks <repo> fresh
  ./target/debug/cdcp_gate --root fresh/course-engine install-hooks --check
  -> exit 2: '.../fresh/.git/hooks/pre-commit: NOT INSTALLED (BUILT != WIRED)'
So check.sh cannot get past step 313 in CI. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/repo_surface.rs::the_pre_commit_shim_is_installed_in_this_clone is the same failure by a second route, inside `cargo fmt/clippy/test` at line 436.

WHY IT MATTERS BOTH WAYS: a gate that is RED for an environmental reason on every run teaches the reader to ignore the colour. It is also the reason nobody has noticed that the hook is not, and cannot be, the enforcement point in CI (see bd-efm7).

FIX (one line, in the file bd-xmn5 was not allowed to edit):
  scripts/check.sh, immediately before line 313:
    echo "==> cdcp_gate install-hooks (a fresh clone has no hook; CI is a fresh clone)"
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- install-hooks || fail "install-hooks"
  install-hooks is idempotent (State::Installed prints 'already matches' and exits 0), so this is a no-op on a developer machine.

ALTERNATIVE if check.sh must not mutate .git/: add an explicit CI step before check.sh in .github/workflows/check.yml. Do NOT relax install-hooks --check; a --check that cannot fail is the fooled certificate this repo keeps finding.

ACCEPTANCE:
- install-hooks --check is GREEN in CI because the hook is genuinely installed, never because the step was weakened or skipped.
- A CI run is observed passing that step (not inferred).
close_reason:
FIXED IN THIS TICK, not deferred. scripts/check.sh now runs 'cdcp_gate install-hooks' immediately before 'install-hooks --check'. install-hooks is idempotent so it is a no-op on a developer machine, and it is the thing that makes the --check line meaningful in CI.

WHY THIS WAS A P0: the split was the worst possible shape. A fresh clone has no .git/hooks/pre-commit, and CI IS a fresh clone — so --check exited 2 on every CI run and 0 on every machine where anyone would notice. A gate that is red exactly where nobody looks and green exactly where everybody does is not a gate, it is a habit of ignoring one CI step.

title: check.sh invokes nine gates through cargo run, so a sibling's build warning is indistinguishable from gate output
description:
WHAT: scripts/check.sh invokes every Rust gate as `cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- <gate>`. Nine call sites. Raised by the bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.11/.12 port agent, which was required to use the built binary in its own differentials for exactly this reason.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY IT IS P2 NOT P1: cargo writes build diagnostics to stderr, so a compile warning from an unrelated crate arrives interleaved with gate output. In a DIFFERENTIAL that is fatal — it reads as divergence, and it cost this project a false conclusion during wave 6. In check.sh the gates are invoked as `|| fail`, so contamination cannot change the verdict; the cost is ATTRIBUTION. A gate that fails because the workspace does not compile reports identically to a gate that fails because it found a violation. During a six-agent wave, that difference is the whole diagnosis.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: this exact confusion occurred while wiring wave 7. `substrate-guard` reported FAIL twice for two entirely different reasons (a staged-snapshot registry mismatch, then a nested --prove-wired child transcript leaking into the parent log) and both looked the same at a glance.

ACCEPTANCE:
- One explicit `cargo build -p cdcp_gate -p cdcp_cli --locked` step early, with its own ok line, so a compile failure is ITS failure and names itself.
- The nine gate call sites invoke ./target/debug/<bin> directly.
- The build step and the invocations agree on profile; a missing binary is an ERROR naming the build step, never a silent skip or a fallback to cargo run.
- Known-bad: plant a compile error in a crate the gates do not use, and confirm the failure names the build step rather than a gate.
- Anti-vacuous: if the binary is absent the step must fail, not fall back.
- Note the interaction with the nested --prove-wired child, which runs a full check.sh: whatever build step is added must be idempotent and must not recurse pathologically.

title: rebase_module_bounds.rs runs build_units.py against the LIVE tree during a test
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs (around line 684, before the bd-ggs7 rewrite) invokes scripts/build_units.py against the LIVE tree, which writes web/data/units_index.json during a test run. Found by the builder-port agent while it was being held to the opposite standard.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is precisely the pattern the differential harnesses were built to avoid, and the reason is not hypothetical. A test that writes a TRACKED artifact (a) makes `git status` a function of whether you have run the tests, (b) can mask a stale committed artifact by silently refreshing it, and (c) races every concurrent agent in a multi-agent wave — this repo runs six at a time.

THE ESTABLISHED CORRECT SHAPE, already implemented twice in tests/diff_build_units.rs and tests/diff_build_glossary_json.rs: materialise a tree COPY in temp, run there, and assert the produced bytes EQUAL the tracked artifact. That read-only comparison is strictly STRONGER than running live — it proves the committed artifact is current, which running live cannot, because running live makes it current.

NOTE: bd-ggs7 rewrote this file after the finding was reported. Re-confirm the invocation still exists before working it; if the rewrite removed it, close with the measurement rather than assuming.

title: Module quiz draws RETIRED items and SCORES learners on them (quiz.js filters by module only)
description:
WHAT: web/assets/js/quiz.js filterByModule() filters web/data/bank_items_seed42.json by the numeric `module` field ONLY. It never reads `status`. The manifest ships all 804 bank files including 25 status="retired", so the module-quiz draw pool includes withdrawn items.

THIS IS LIVE AND LEARNER-FACING. bd-web-pack-ships-retired-items-4ivb assumed 'there is no live bug — nothing in the current web code indexes it by anything but the drawn ids'. That assumption is WRONG and was disproven by measurement.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 by transcribing quiz.js sampleItems() (mulberry32 + Fisher-Yates) and its seed derivation (42 + module*1000, +15 for mode=learn15) faithfully into node and running it against the COMMITTED pack. The draw is fully deterministic, so these are not probabilities — they are the exact items served:

  default 8-12 quizzes: module 5 -> m05-q200, module 6 -> mock40-q18, module 8 -> mock40-q24,
                        module 10 -> mock40-q22, module 12 -> m12-q219, module 13 -> mock40-q37
  mode=learn15 (5 Q):   module 5 -> m05-q200, module 14 -> mock40-q40

8 retired items served across the 30 deterministic module quizzes; 6 of 15 default module quizzes affected.

THE LEARNER IS SCORED ON THEM, not merely shown them. Chain verified in source:
  1. quiz.html?module=N is linked from every web/learn/NN-*.html page and from web/learn.html
  2. filterByModule -> sampleItems -> pack.items
  3. onSubmit -> gradeByKeys() counts the retired item in score_correct/score_total
  4. WASM gradeDigest() produces a GradeExact digest over an attempt containing it
  5. recordGradedWrongs() persists a miss into cdcp.drill.missed.v1 + SRS schedule (1d/3d)
  6. recordQuizResult() feeds cdcp.mastery.v1 practiced/mastered state

So a retired item is shown, scored, spaced-repetition-scheduled, and mastery-weighted. Retirement is not cosmetic: an item is retired because a BETTER COPY OF THE SAME PROPOSITION exists (cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED carries the per-id argument). Serving the retired copy drills the copy that lost.

WHY THE PACK CANNOT BE FIXED INSTEAD (already decided, do not re-litigate): the manifest must ship all 804. cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds the pack bytes to Bank::from_json_str which RECOMPUTES bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade hard-fails on mismatch. Measured: 804-file bank hashes 3404d854... , 779 approved-only pool hashes b81a0019... (pre-v2-bump values). An approved-only pack breaks EVERY client-side grade. Decision recorded in registries/goldens-couplings.toml web.bank-items-pack row and web/data/README.md.

FIX (one line, in the consumer):
  export function filterByModule(bank, moduleNum) {
    const arr = Array.isArray(bank) ? bank : bank && bank.items ? bank.items : [];
    return arr.filter(function (it) {
      return it && typeof it.module === 'number' && it.module === moduleNum
             && it.status === 'approved';
    });
  }
Also audit web/assets/js/drill.js and results.js: both look up by an id the learner already answered, so they are transitively fixed — but only if nothing else draws.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No module quiz at any module/mode serves a non-approved item. Re-run the deterministic sweep above and assert 0.
- Anti-vacuous: a module whose approved pool is empty must ERROR/adapt visibly, never render a 0-item quiz silently.
- A test pins it: known-bad = mark one drawn item retired in a fixture pack, assert the quiz pool excludes it.
- scripts/smoke_*.mjs or an e2e asserts no retired id can enter a graded attempt.

NOT MINE: web/assets/js is owned by another agent this wave. Filed with full evidence rather than edited.

description:
WHAT: A decision only Josh can make. bd-corpus-public-captures-not-licensed-class-kej removed nine body captures that the manifest itself recorded rights="publisher-retains-copyright", redistribution="not-licensed" from knowledge/corpus/public/. HEAD is now clean and gated. The bytes are still reachable in the git history of a PUBLIC repository (github.com/JYeswak/cdcp-self-study), and in every clone, fork and cache made while they were there.

THE THREE OPTIONS, and why two are already leaning:
(a) ACCEPT HEAD-ONLY — the current state, and what the parent bead recorded as a NON-GOAL. Its reasoning: docs/flywheel/PREPUBLISH-SCRUB-2026-08-14.md applies a fortiori, because these are captures of PUBLIC WEB PAGES rather than standards-body text, no publisher AI policy aggravates them, and the repo was already public. That reasoning is sound as far as it goes.
(b) REWRITE HISTORY for the nine paths. Irreversible and external: it means a force-push to a public remote, breaking every existing clone and every open PR, and it does not reach forks or caches. ESCALATION-ONLY under the autonomy grant, and not something an agent may decide is warranted.
(c) NEITHER, and record why — e.g. a note in the repo stating the removal and its date, so a reader of the history knows the current posture without a rewrite.

WHY IT IS BEADED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the non-goal was recorded by a controller, not decided by Josh. A non-goal in a bead body and a decision are different objects, and the difference matters precisely because this one is about exposure on a public remote. Without a bead the next agent to sweep the corpus re-derives the same analysis and re-escalates, which is the re-litigation the autonomy grant "record every fork you resolve" clause exists to prevent.

NOTHING IS BLOCKED ON THIS. HEAD is clean, the corpus-redistribution gate is green and fails closed, and the anti-hallucination corpus measures 573,880 characters against a floor of 20,000 without any of the removed material. The parent bead is complete either way.

ACCEPTANCE (Josh, not an agent):
- A recorded decision: (a), (b) or (c), with its reason, so the analysis is not re-derived.
- If (b) is authorised, Josh runs it or explicitly authorises the exact command; an agent never force-pushes and never rewrites history on its own.
- If (a) stands, record it as a DECISION with its reason and close this bead. Standing still is a legitimate answer; an unrecorded standing still is not.

NON-ESCALATION FOLLOW-UP, noted here so it is not lost and does NOT need Josh: src-ocp-ready was removed with the other eight rather than re-licensed. OCP publishes individual specifications under named open licences (OCPHL, CC-BY) and this row may well be re-openable — but the artefact retained was a capture of a GitHub PROJECT PAGE, not of a licensed specification document, and no licence text granting redistribution of that page was located. Re-adding it is now a mechanical licence-evidence job under the new CORPUS-R7: record redistribution_evidence {licence, url, clause} naming the licence that covers the specific document, and the body may legitimately return. That is ordinary corpus work for an agent, not a decision.

title: The module-bound sweep still cannot see a bound that is COMPUTED or read from config
description:
WHAT: bd-8mjs closed the named-constant hole in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/rebase_module_bounds.rs — Shape::NamedBound now sees 'MIN_TERMS = 15', 'pub const MAX: usize = 14;', 'MAX=14'. Three shapes remain outside every detector in that file, and they are named at the pinned open count so the number does not read broader than it is:

1. A bound COMPUTED rather than written. 'MAX_MODULE = len(declared) - 1', 'range(1, MAX)', 'n - 1' where n came from somewhere. No literal, no binding to a bare integer, invisible to all three detectors.
2. A bound read from a config file or an environment variable. 'MAX = cfg["max_module"]' or os.environ. The literal moves out of the scanned trees entirely.
3. A name bound to something other than a bare integer that still carries the bound: a tuple, a list, a dict value, a chained expression.

WHY IT MATTERS, and why this is P3 and not P1: the bd-8mjs evasion needed no intent — rebasing a literal onto a named constant is ordinary refactoring hygiene, which is what made it dangerous. These three are different: none of them is something a refactor does by accident to a module bound. They are reachable, but only deliberately. The cost of chasing them is an over-strict detector, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which is a slower death than no gate. The named-bound detector was worth building because it found three real lines (two of them in a Rust port nobody had in mind) at zero false positives; a computed-bound detector cannot make that trade without a data-flow pass.

ACCEPTANCE (whichever is argued at the time):
- Either a fourth detector with real known-GOOD legs over the legitimate computed expressions already in the tree, and every new hit inventoried with a verdict,
- or a recorded decision that the residual stays uncovered, with the reason, so the next agent does not re-derive this from scratch. The residual is ALREADY stated at the count and in the module header; this bead exists so the statement has a tracking id rather than only prose.

WHAT: the 'Gates proven to trip' table in README.md carries a per-suite n column (| selftest_orphan | 6 | ... |). verify-injection-count enforces the TOTAL at 5 advertisement sites and the SUITE COUNT, but its _ADVERTISED regex requires the number to be followed by 'injections|faults', so '| 26 |' in a table cell matches nothing. title: verify-injection-count --write-readme is unreachable from check.sh
description:
WHAT: verify_injection_count.py / cdcp_gate verify-injection-count document the advertised number as 'REGENERATED, never hand-maintained' via --write-readme. But the only log that carries every registered suite's receipt is the one check.sh mktemps, and check.sh deletes it in its EXIT trap and never passes --write-readme. So the regeneration path has no reachable caller: in practice the number is retyped by hand and the gate only says whether the typing was right.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 while closing bd-1sd.13: moving selftest_injection_count from 12 to 26 injections required typing 63 into five README sites by hand, because there was no way to reach the regenerator with a real log.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'regenerated, never typed' is a claim in the shipped module header and in README prose. A claim whose mechanism has no caller is the BUILT != WIRED failure inside a doc-truth gate.

FIX (mirrors what bd-1sd.13 shipped for the step count): honour an env flag in check.sh — CDCP_INJECTION_COUNT_WRITE_README=1 adds --write-readme to the verify-injection-count invocation, so a drifted total is repaired by re-running the chain rather than by retyping five sites. Keep the refusal-on-unsound-receipts leg.

ACCEPTANCE: adding an injection and re-running check.sh with the flag rewrites all five sites from the receipts; without the flag it is still RED; a known-bad proves the flag cannot launder an unsound total.
close_reason: VERDICT GREEN. SHA 40358c6. check.sh honours CDCP_INJECTION_COUNT_WRITE_README=1 so verify-injection-count gets --write-readme (mirrors CDCP_STEP_COUNT_WRITE_README). Without the flag, drift stays RED and README is not rewritten. Flag cannot launder an unsound total: regeneration SKIPPED, file byte-unchanged (python rc=1, rust rc=1). Proof: cargo test -p cdcp_gate --lib gates::verify_injection_count (23 passed, including check_sh_wires_write_readme_behind_the_env_flag + write_readme_refuses_to_launder_an_unsound_total + write_readme_regenerates_every_site_from_the_receipts); cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test diff_verify_injection_count write_readme (2 passed); sh scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh INJECTIONS=33 (wire snippet: flag=0 no --write-readme, flag=1 passes it; wire-unsound SKIPPED). Did not run full check.sh. Did not push.

title: Widen the ABSENT-OK path-guard scan from two files to the cdcp_gate tree
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/anti_vacuous_topics.rs::unreasoned_path_guards_are_a_defect scans exactly two files — crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs and scripts/verify_objectives.py — for block-opening existence tests (is_file/exists/is_dir) that neither record an error inside the if/else chain they open nor carry an 'ABSENT-OK:' reason in that chain or the twelve lines above it. Widening it is ONE LINE: the targets array.

WHY IT WAS NOT WIDENED IN THE bd-9nyt WAVE (argued, not skipped):
1. Five sibling agents were editing crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/ concurrently. A gate that goes red on a file its owner cannot touch gets disabled, and a disabled detector is worth LESS than none, because it also carries the belief that the class is covered.
2. 'ABSENT-OK:' is a convention this test invented. Imposing it tree-wide unilaterally means every other gate author adopts one agent's comment syntax or is flagged for it. It should survive one wave in one place first.

MEASURED SCOPE OF THE WIDENING: 72 is_file()/exists()/is_dir() occurrences across crates/cdcp_gate/src/ as of acd4d43, concentrated in verify_content_lock.rs (12), verify_objectives.rs (9), validate_grounding.rs (9), build_units.rs (6), verify_coverage.rs (5), verify_bank.rs (5). Not all are block guards; the scanner only counts lines whose trimmed form opens an if/elif/else-if.

ACCEPTANCE:
- targets extended to crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs and the .py oracles still on the path.
- Every newly-flagged site either gains an error path or an ABSENT-OK: sentence, ONE OWNER AT A TIME. A blanket sweep that adds the marker everywhere converts the detector into decoration; the existing assertion 'reasoned * 2 < total' is the guard against that and must be re-tuned per-file rather than dropped.
- The planted known-bad legs in that test (bare guard FLAGGED, ABSENT-OK guard NOT flagged, else-with-error NOT flagged) must survive the widening unchanged.
- Known-GOOD: the live tree still passes check.sh.

WHAT IT CANNOT DECIDE (carry this forward): the scanner does not read what the guarded block DOES, so it cannot tell a skipped verdict from a skipped log line; it does not follow ? or a helper that raises elsewhere; and it cannot tell a true ABSENT-OK: from a lazy one.
close_reason: VERDICT: path-guard scan now globs crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/*.rs + remaining scripts/{verify,validate}_*.py oracles (88 sites, 51 error-path, 37 ABSENT-OK, 0 unreasoned). SHA cb2b2d11fd6289f1fd44db13d75f26fcdf6cdb6d. cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test anti_vacuous_topics: 9/9 ok. reasoned*2<total retuned per-file. Did not take 99sw (already closed db0bda0). title: verify-objectives --write-json can leave a summary saying status=pass under a FAIL verdict
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_objectives.py:~735 and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_objectives.rs:~1690 compute the summary's status BEFORE writing it:

    provisional = 'PASS' if not errors else 'FAIL'
    out.write_text(json.dumps(summary_for(provisional) ...))
  except OSError as e:
    errors.append(f'could not write summary to {out}: {e}')

So the ONE path that can turn a PASS into a FAIL after the status word is chosen is the write itself. If create_dir_all succeeds and the write then fails partway (target on a full or read-only filesystem, truncated then failed), the artifact left on disk carries "status": "pass" while the gate exits 1. A machine-readable receipt disagreeing with the verdict is the receipt an operator trusts.

FOUND: during the bd-9nyt sweep of verify_objectives. NOT fixed there because closing it means either writing to a temp file and renaming (behaviour change on both sides, and the differential compares the written bytes AND the stdout in tests/diff_verify_objectives.rs::the_written_summary_is_byte_identical), or emitting the status last — both larger than the bead in hand.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SHOULD STAY RECORDED RATHER THAN INFLATED: on a successful write provisional == final, because nothing else appends to errors after that point. Nothing in scripts/check.sh passes --write-json for this gate, and nothing in the repo consumes the file (grepped: no consumer outside the gate and its differential).

ACCEPTANCE:
- The written summary's status equals the printed verdict on every path, or the file is not left behind at all when the write fails.
- Python first, then the Rust port, then the byte-differential goes green again.
- Known-bad: point --write-json at a target whose write fails after the parent exists; assert no file on disk says pass while the process exits non-zero.
close_reason: atomic write-json; SHA c95cc4435711fb7bccda2bdd71965cec7cd53ef2; no leftover pass receipt on write-fail

title: verify_coverage reads the same bank_policy.toml where ABSENCE LOWERS the floors

WHAT: bd-9nyt reasoned verify_objectives' two missing-bank_policy.toml early returns as legitimately optional and marked them ABSENT-OK. The argument is sound FOR THAT GATE and only for that gate:

  verify_objectives applies its OWN floor of >=1 item per required module and reads the policy only for [[coverage_exempt]] rows and [[domain_min]] drift. An absent ledger therefore removes exemptions, leaves every declared module required, and makes the gate STRICTER. Nothing can hide in the absence.

verify_coverage.py / crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_coverage.rs read the SAME file for the SIZED [[domain_min]] floors. There, absence removes the floors — the opposite direction. - If it silently applies no floor, that is the absent-input-reads-as-success class and it becomes an error path naming the file.

title: verify-bank enforces pool_min against the file set, not the approved pool — same class as bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh
description:
WHAT: `verify-bank` (scripts/verify_bank.py + crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs) counts every loaded item, whatever its status, in THREE places that all key on the drawable pool:

  scripts/verify_bank.py:169   `if pool_min is not None and exam_n is not None and n < pool_min` — the ENFORCED floor
  scripts/verify_bank.py:300   `correct_dist={...}` — answer-letter diversity
  scripts/verify_bank.py:301   `modules={...}` — per-module counts

MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the live tree, after bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh landed in verify-coverage:

    verify-bank:      items=804  pool_min=400 exam_n=40 multiplier~20.1x
                      modules={... 14: 44 ...}
                      correct_dist={A:198 B:228 C:190 D:188}
    drawable truth:   779 approved (25 retired), m14: 42, multiplier~19.5x

NO LIVE BREACH: 779 >= 400 either way, and the letter distribution over the approved pool is not obviously skewed. This is a defect, not an incident — but it is the SAME fail-open direction verify-coverage just had fixed: the file count can only ever be >= the number that matters, so `pool_min` can only ever be too generous, and `multiplier~20.1x` is a claim about a pool `cdcp_assemble::sample_item_ids` will never draw from.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY: bd-coverage-counts-retired-items-49jh asked its owner to DECIDE the question for verify-bank. The decision is that it is the same defect and must move the same way — but verify_bank.py and verify_bank.rs were owned by a different agent during the same wave, and reaching across would have meant two agents editing one differential. - `modules={...}` and `correct_dist={...}` either count the approved pool, or say IN THE OUTPUT which population they show. Correct-letter diversity measured over a pool that includes retired items is measuring the wrong pool for the same reason the floor was.

title: the verdict-shape class needs a META-GATE over the differential harnesses, not a fourth patch — measured 3 of 11 carry the leg
description:
CONTEXT: bd-lt7 fixed instance 1 (build_units.py). bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 fixed instance 2 (build_glossary_json.py + port). bd-verify-coverage-verdict-before-write-rk9n fixed instance 3 (verify_coverage.py + port), and its owner was asked to decide whether a mechanism can forbid the shape GENERALLY. This is that decision, recorded so it is not re-derived, plus the one tractable mechanism and why it did not land in the same wave.

THE TWO OBVIOUS FORMS, AND WHY BOTH ARE REJECTED:

1. A STATIC SCAN ("grep for a success token printed on a path reachable by a non-zero exit") is NOT tractable, and the sound approximation is worse than no gate. Sound analysis needs interprocedural reachability across Python AND Rust. The cheap approximation — flag any file containing a success token that can also exit non-zero — fires on every CORRECT gate in the tree: verify_coverage.py buffers "PASS" and returns 1 from the same function, and that is right, because the token is only in the buffer when `errors` is empty. A scan cannot see that without evaluating the condition. And this repo has already measured the failure mode of message-keyed scanning: see the bd-0czh comment in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs — three fail-opens survived an audit because grepping each file for the message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. A scan that can be fooled by the same string that fooled the auditor is a GREEN gate certifying a wrong claim.

2. A SHARED REPORT-COMPOSITION HELPER (a Report type whose verdict is structurally last) is sound but OPT-IN. It prevents the shape only in the files that adopt it, does not cross the Python/Rust boundary, and an author who does not reach for it is not caught. It is a convention, not an enforcement — and this repo does not count conventions.

THE FORM THAT IS TRACTABLE: a META-GATE over the differential harnesses. Each harness already runs both implementations on every case and already knows its gate exit code. The detector is one leg — on any case where a side exited non-zero, assert its stdout carries no success token, asserted PER SIDE. That leg is PROVEN, twice, by mutation pairs: qm65 proved it in the two builder harnesses; rk9n proved it again in diff_verify_coverage.rs on 2026-08-14 (mutate both implementations to print the token regardless of the verdict -> suite exit 101 on 12 cases; delete that ONE assertion with the mutation still in place -> exit 0). The meta-gate asserts every harness CARRIES that leg, so a new gate cannot ship without it.

WHY IT DID NOT LAND WITH rk9n — MEASURED 2026-08-14, `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs`:

    CARRIES a per-side non-zero + success-token leg (3):
      diff_build_units.rs, diff_build_glossary_json.rs, diff_verify_coverage.rs
    DOES NOT (8):
      diff_validate_grounding.rs, diff_verify_bank.rs, diff_verify_content_lock.rs,
      diff_verify_doc_consistency.rs, diff_verify_injection_count.rs,
      diff_verify_knowledge_paths.rs, diff_verify_objectives.rs, diff_verify_orphans.rs

Landing the meta-gate in that wave would have turned EIGHT sibling-owned test files RED mid-swarm, for a defect none of them has been shown to have. That is a gate tripping on other peoples work in flight, not a gate proving a claim. Converted to this bead instead of skipped.

ONE MORE THING THE IMPLEMENTER MUST SOLVE, recorded because it is the real difficulty: the success token DIFFERS per gate (PASS, ok, GREEN, `PASS: glossary terms=`). A leg keyed on the literal "PASS" is message-keyed and is exactly the shape rejected in (1). The token belongs in a per-gate registry row the harness reads, not in a grep.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Every `crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs` carries the per-side leg, keyed on a REGISTERED success token for its gate rather than on a literal.
- A meta-test enumerates the harnesses and fails when one lacks the leg. An empty enumeration is an ERROR, not a pass. An exclusion requires a reason string; an exclusion without a reason is a schema error.
- The meta-test is itself proven by a mutation pair: delete the leg from one harness -> the meta-test names that harness and is RED.
- The census that found instances 1-3 is re-run and reports ZERO remaining, so the class CLOSES rather than being decremented.
close_reason: implemented named harness meta-gate (LEG I); SHA 04d7af8

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION: the meta-gate was built, and it does NOT take the shape this bead proposed. Recorded with the argument so it is not re-litigated.

WHAT THIS BEAD PROPOSED: a meta-test that asserts every crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_*.rs CARRIES a per-side leg ("on any case where a side exited non-zero, assert its stdout carries no success token"), keyed on a registered token, with the census re-run to zero.

WHAT WAS BUILT INSTEAD: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, which moves the leg OFF the harnesses and ONTO the gate binary. For every gate cdcp_gate list names, on an empty root and (where safe) on the live root, it asserts that exit == 0 is EQUIVALENT to "stdout opens a line with this gate is registered success token".

THREE REASONS, in order of weight.

1. THE LEG IS PER-CASE AND UNBOUNDED; THE DEFECT IS PER-GATE AND THERE ARE NINETEEN GATES. A per-harness leg protects only the cases that harness happens to run, and only for as long as that harness exists. The gate probe covers every case of every gate at once, including gates that never had a differential harness (capability-maturity, doc-facts, goldens-couplings, corpus-redistribution, near-duplicate-items, substrate-guard, verify-step-count, install-hooks — eight gates this bead is silent about).

2. IT NEEDED EIGHT SIBLING-OWNED FILES EDITED IN ONE WAVE, which this bead already identified as the reason it did not land with rk9n. That has not improved: four of the eleven harnesses were owned by other agents during the 2026-08-14 wave. The gate probe needs no edit to any file another agent owns.

3. THE ORACLES ARE NOW RETIRED. check.sh invokes none of the eleven .py scripts, and the standing policy is to retire an oracle at port time and convert its differential cases into direct tests. A leg installed in eleven harnesses that are being deleted is work with a known expiry. The gate probe outlives every harness in the tree.

WHAT IS PRESERVED FROM THIS BEAD, deliberately: the success token is a REGISTERED PER-GATE ROW in registries/differential_harnesses.toml, never a literal in a scanner — this bead is right that a leg keyed on "PASS" is the message-keyed shape rejected in its own section (1), and bd-0czh already measured three fail-opens surviving an audit because grepping for the message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. The tokens differ exactly as predicted: PASS, "PASS: build_units", "PASS: glossary", "verify_content_lock: PASS", "<gate>: ok:".

MEASURED WHILE BUILDING IT, and filed: near-duplicate-items prints NO success token on either path, so nothing but its exit code distinguishes green from red (bd-near-dup-no-success-token-gj9y). It is registered token_free WITH A REASON and the meta-gate PROVES the absence — neither probe may open a line with any word from the token vocabulary — rather than taking the exclusion on trust. An exclusion without a reason string is a schema error, as this bead required.

TOKEN MATCHING IS LINE-PREFIX, NOT SUBSTRING, and there is a known-GOOD leg for it: a gate that says "expected PASS, got FAIL" under exit 1 has not claimed to pass, and a message-keyed check would fire there. The detector is proven on planted synthetics in both directions (the_verdict_shape_detector_trips_on_a_planted_known_bad).

ANTI-VACUOUS: the gate roster comes from the BINARY, not the registry, so a new gate cannot ship unregistered; an empty roster is an ERROR; every gate must FAIL over an empty root; and at least one gate must be observed GREEN carrying its token, or the token side of the equivalence never ran and "no token on a failing path" passed for free.

STILL OPEN FROM THIS BEAD ACCEPTANCE: the per-harness leg is NOT installed in the eight harnesses that lacked it, and deliberately so. If the class is later judged to need both, that is a new bead, and it should be weighed against the retirement schedule for those files.

title: A restored perturbation can leave cargo testing the STALE binary — measured false RED, and by symmetry false GREEN
description:
WHAT: the standard perturb-then-restore pattern used by every meta-test in this repo can silently defeat the rebuild, so the test exercises a binary that does not match the source on disk.

MECHANISM: `cp file file.bak` then later `mv file.bak file` restores the CONTENT but gives the file the BACKUP OBJECT.S mtime, which is older than the perturbed version cargo already compiled. cargo compares mtimes, sees nothing newer, and skips the rebuild. The next invocation runs the binary built from the PERTURBED source.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-6ycw / bd-web-pack agent, recorded in goldens/PROVENANCE.md with the mtimes): its verification reported RED for a tree that was GREEN. The agent caught it, forced a rebuild, and both bank_hash and the wasm reproduced byte-identically.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A CURIOSITY: the observed direction was a false RED, which is loud and self-correcting. THE SAME MECHANISM PRODUCES A FALSE GREEN — restore a file, skip the rebuild, and the suite passes against the binary that still contains the mutation. Every meta-test PAIR in this repo depends on exactly this restore step, and a meta-test that cannot fail is a fooled certificate, which is Sev-0 by this project standard. We have run dozens of these pairs this week.

THE PAIRS AT RISK are every one following the house pattern: (1) mutate the gate, assert the suite goes non-zero; (2) with the mutation still in place, delete the assertion, assert it returns to zero; (3) restore. Step 3 is the one that rots, and a bad step 3 makes the NEXT pair meaningless rather than this one.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A documented restore that cannot lose the rebuild — `touch` the restored file, or restore by rewriting content rather than moving the inode, or force `cargo build` before the post-restore assertion. Pick one, state why, and put it where meta-test authors will read it (the pattern is described in several test headers and in CHARTER meta-test guidance).
- A known-bad that DEMONSTRATES the trap: restore naively, assert the suite reports the wrong verdict; restore correctly, assert it reports the right one. If the trap cannot be reproduced on demand, the fix cannot be verified.
- AUDIT: how many meta-test pairs run in this repo, and how many use a restore that is vulnerable? Report the count. A sample of previously-passed pairs should be re-run under a forced rebuild to confirm their verdicts still hold — if any flips, that is a separate finding and every conclusion drawn from it is suspect.
- Anti-vacuous: a rebuild step that finds nothing to rebuild when a file demonstrably changed is an ERROR, not a pass.
close_reason: Restore helper scripts/restore_safe.inc.sh cannot leave a stale mtime; selftest_reconstructed.sh (only cargo-touching selftest restore) converted; naive-mv skip RED and helper rebuild GREEN measured. 80a3d368e85e96613cd1f3e0ffbec70d6166c9a6

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
WAVE RESULT 2026-08-14. Half 1 complete and measured. Half 2 audited but its re-run is BLOCKED, not passed.

THE TRAP IS REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, BOTH DIRECTIONS. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/restore_rebuild_trap.rs, 4 tests, all green in 6.34 s, built from a throwaway two-file cargo crate in a tempdir so it never touches this repo and can run beside any sibling suite.
  a_naive_restore_of_the_assertion_reports_a_false_green  - the Sev-0 direction: run the house pair to completion with a mv-shaped step 3 and the suite certifies exit 0 for a tree whose only honest verdict is RED.
  a_safe_restore_of_the_assertion_reports_the_true_red    - same tree, byte-rewrite restore plus a PROVEN rebuild, verdict 101.
  a_forced_build_after_a_naive_restore_is_itself_vacuous  - the anti-vacuous leg aimed at the remedy.
  touch_recovers_a_tree_that_was_already_restored_by_rename - the false-RED direction measured 2026-08-14, and touch pinned as the RECOVERY move.
Every case first asserts its own fixture discriminates (clean crate GREEN, perturbed crate RED) - a fixture that can only report one thing proves nothing.

THE PATTERN, ARGUED. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/rebuild.rs. Measured head-to-head:
  mv then cargo build  -> nothing rebuilt, fresh:true, Finished in 0.00s -> WRONG verdict
  cp then cargo build  -> fresh:false -> right verdict
  mv + touch then build-> fresh:false -> right verdict
PICK: byte-rewrite for the mechanism (it IS the restore, so there is no second step to forget) PLUS a forced build with a freshness assertion for the proof. Neither half alone is enough, and the argument turns on this: A FORCED cargo build ON ITS OWN IS VACUOUS - after a rename-restore it exits 0 and rebuilds nothing, i.e. the obvious fix passes in exactly the case it was written to catch. touch is demoted to the recovery move: it works, but it is a separate step whose omission is silent.
ALSO PINNED AS A TRAP FOR THE NEXT AGENT: do NOT prove freshness with artifact_mtime > source_mtime. The poisoned tree SATISFIES it. Compare the artifact's mtime before the build with its mtime after.

WHERE IT IS WRITTEN: .flywheel/CHARTER.md gauntlet section as step (3) of the pair; docs/TESTING.md new section 'Meta-test pairs: step 3 is the one that rots'; docs/PLAN-A-TO-Z.md line 54, which still carried the retired 'delete the assertion -> selftest RED' wording the CHARTER corrected on 2026-08-14 - fixed in place; crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/mod.rs header pointer.

MY OWN META-TEST PAIR, run under the pattern it certifies. TRUE exit codes, read off the child, never through a pipe:
  leg 1 - mutate the anti-vacuous branch of build_proving_rebuild to always report 'rebuilt' -> cargo test exit 101, EXACTLY ONE test red (a_forced_build_after_a_naive_restore_is_itself_vacuous). Single detector confirmed.
  leg 2 - mutation still live, delete that test's expect_err assertion -> exit 0. That assertion, and nothing else, is what bit.
  step 3 - both files restored by byte rewrite, then rebuild PROVEN: artifact mtime 1786753436.84 -> 1786753475.16. Suite green.
Cargo's rebuild-changes-artifact-mtime assumption was verified independently rather than assumed: touch source -> Compiling cdcp_gate -> mtime 1786753301.07 -> 1786753411.88.

AUDIT COUNTS: 19 recorded pairs; 13 exposed (mutated a cargo-compiled file); 6 not exposed (4 shell selftests, 2 Python-era); 0 of the 13 recorded a rebuild-safe restore. Ratio 13/19 = 68 percent exposed, 13/13 = 100 percent of those unproven. Floor derivation for the anti-vacuous clause: 5 in-source records and 12 closed-bead close_reasons name a meta-test today.

RE-RUN SAMPLE: NOT RUN. Five attempts, 240-600 s each, none reached a Compiling line - bd-syspolicyd-stall-blocks-all-builds-dp91 held the shared target lock for over an hour and a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR hangs identically. Tracked as bd-metatest-rerun-blocked-yhg6 with the 13 prioritised by consequence. No verdict is claimed for any of them.

FILED: bd-metatest-rerun-blocked-yhg6 (P1), bd-single-leg-metatest-closes-illw (P1), bd-stale-artifact-gate-urj0 (P2). Evidence merged into dp91.
