title: A differential harness cannot see a defect both implementations share — measured, on a case it had been passing for weeks
description:
WHAT: the byte-exact differential harnesses assert that the Python oracle and the Rust port agree on stdout, stderr, exit code and bytes written. They cannot see a defect PRESENT IN BOTH. Two implementations agreeing on a vacuous pass is still a vacuous pass.

THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL. Measured 2026-08-14 in verify_objectives: `--min-items-per-topic 0` fell straight through the comparison guard and printed

  PASS ... primary_topics=106 covered=106 shortfalls=0 min_per_topic=0 mode=strict ... EXIT 0

106 of 106 topics reported covered, in STRICT mode, with not one comparison performed. The differential harness had been running that exact case (`m min topic 0`) and PASSING it for weeks, because both sides produced the same wrong answer. The harness header already says "a defect faithfully ported is still a defect" — and the defect landed in its own blind spot.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: agreement is a necessary condition for a correct port and is NOT a sufficient condition for a correct gate. Every case in every differential harness that asserts only agreement is silent about whether the shared behaviour is right. We now have roughly eleven of these harnesses and the count is growing with each port.

RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME: bd-j8b2 proposes a meta-gate over the harnesses for the VERDICT-SHAPE class specifically (measured 3 of 11 carry the leg). This bead is the general case — verdict shape is one instance of shared-defect blindness, not the whole of it.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A recorded decision on what each differential case must assert BEYOND agreement. The candidate from the objectives work: assert the VERDICT, not only the agreement — that is, each case states what the correct answer IS, independently, and both sides are checked against it. That is more expensive per case and it is the only thing that can see a shared defect. Argue it against the alternatives.
- An audit: across all differential harnesses, how many cases assert agreement ONLY? Report the count and the ratio. That number is the size of the blind spot and it should be published where a reader meets the harnesses.
- At least the anti-vacuous and floor cases in every harness carry an independent verdict assertion, since those are the ones whose failure mode is silence.
- Known-bad: plant a defect in BOTH implementations identically, assert the harness now catches it. Under the current design it does not — that is the demonstration.
- Anti-vacuous: a harness whose case list is empty, or which compares an artifact neither side wrote, is an ERROR.
close_reason: min_per_topic=0 is ERROR with named finding; old agreement-only case pins it (d2ae50e)

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION, recorded so it is not re-derived (bd-4qje acceptance leg 1).

WHAT EACH CASE MUST ASSERT BEYOND AGREEMENT — and the answer is not the same for every case, which is why the earlier framing kept stalling.

(1) EVERY case states the correct answer independently and BOTH sides are checked against it. Rejected as a blanket rule — not because it is wrong, but because it prices in something now known to be temporary. Measured 2026-08-14: check.sh invokes NONE of the eleven .py oracles; all eleven are retired oracles. Under the retirement policy the second side goes away, so "both sides are checked against it" collapses to "the case asserts the verdict" — candidate (2). Paying the per-case cost twice, once against an oracle about to be deleted, buys nothing.

(2) EVERY case asserts an independent verdict; the byte-comparison stays only while the oracle does. ADOPTED. Agreement is NECESSARY for a correct port and NOT SUFFICIENT for a correct gate, and the independent verdict is the only half that survives retirement. The audit prices it: 36 of 326 cases assert nothing but agreement, so 36 cases (11.0 percent) evaporate to nothing the day their oracle is deleted, and 88 of 326 (27.0 percent) survive holding no claim about output at all.

(3) Independent verdicts only on the anti-vacuous and floor cases. Rejected AS THE CEILING, adopted as the ORDERING. Those cases matter most because their failure mode is silence and they go first. But the measured defect was not in an anti-vacuous case: "m min topic 0" was filed as an OPTION SHAPE. A rule scoped to the cases we already suspect cannot catch the ones we have misfiled — and 23 of the 36 blind cases sit in exactly that misfiled bucket, one test per harness named path_and_option_shapes_are_byte_identical, built to check argument parsing and then quietly given cases that change the gate semantics ("m strict flag", "m skip flag", "m both flags").

(4) A property-based oracle, or a third implementation. Rejected for now, on cost and on the same shared-defect logic: a third implementation written by the same hands against the same reading of the spec is a third vote for the same misunderstanding — it does not close the class, it makes agreement cheaper to obtain. A property oracle is the right long-run answer for the numeric gates and is not this bead.

THE PART THAT IS EASY TO MISS, and why a naive reading of (2) fails: REWRITING THE ASSERTION IS NOT ENOUGH. All 23 option-shape cases run against the LIVE tree, which is green. Asserting "this spelling still passes" on a tree that passes is worth nothing — no defect that suppresses a finding can appear in a run with no finding to suppress. The conversion must change the INPUT too: point the spelling at a tree with a KNOWN planted finding, and assert (a) the spelling normalises to the one resolved path, (b) the run scanned THAT tree — assert the item count, which is what catches a silent fallback to a default — and (c) it still reaches the planted finding and goes RED for it. Done for diff_verify_orphans.rs this wave: 7 blind cases to 0.

PUBLISHED AT: registries/differential_harnesses.toml (census, method, per-harness table, ratchet) and the module header of crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, which is the file a reader of this harness family meets. Remaining work filed as bd-diff-remaining-agreement-only-qgy9, bd-diff-coverage-agreement-only-25ux, bd-diff-injection-i32-comparator-fo1l, bd-diff-exit-code-only-verdicts-t6kv.

  scripts/verify_orphans.py:120
    bank_dir = args.bank if args.bank.is_absolute() else (ROOT / args.bank)

  becomes

                    else { join_posix(root_str, "bank/items") };

In words: a RELATIVE --bank is silently ignored and the gate scans the default bank instead. Realistic, one line each, and it is a defect a port could faithfully reproduce because it is a resolution rule rather than a computation.

THE SPECIMEN: a copy of the live bank into target/, 805 items, exactly one of them carrying topic_ids = ["zz-topic-that-does-not-exist"].

CONTROL, unperturbed oracle, exit 1:
  FAIL
    bank=/…/course-engine/target/zz-demo/lZ1Ipm/items
    items=805
    orphan_item_refs=1
    failures:

PLANTED oracle, same command, EXIT 0:

WHY THE OLD HARNESS WAS BLIND TO IT: the six option-spelling cases in path_and_option_shapes_are_byte_identical were bare assert_byte_identical(..) calls. Both sides carry the same resolution rule, so both print the identical wrong report, and stdout, stderr and exit code all match. Every differential assertion passes. The defect is invisible to agreement by construction.

WHAT THE CONVERTED CASES ASSERT, and which one fires: (1) the spelling normalises to the specimen path — this fires first, because the planted gate prints bank=/…/bank/items; (2) items=805, the count of the tree it was pointed at — this is the assertion a shared fallback cannot survive; (3) exit != 0; (4) the finding is named. The gate binary could not be rebuilt — the shared cargo build directory was saturated for the entire session (60 to 64 concurrent cargo processes, load average 8 to 12, one sibling cargo build holding the lock over 29 minutes) and a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR did not escape it. Both attempts were hard-bounded with timeout so the perturbation always restores; the tree was verified unperturbed by grep afterwards. The oracle half above is real and its exit codes are the emitted ones, read directly and not through a pipe.

title: extract_key_literals scrapes any ".. ".into() as an emitted pack key, so an error string enters a shape pin
description:
WHAT: the goldens-couplings gate derives its `keys` pin for export.pack-shapes by scraping string literals out of the emitting function. It matches `"...".into()` regardless of what the string is FOR, so a literal used in an error message is recorded as an emitted pack key.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-6ycw agent): one of its new error strings entered the export.pack-shapes pin. It worked around it by writing `.to_string()` instead of `.into()` and noted the fact in the row — a correct local fix that leaves the scraper wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE STRING: this pin is load-bearing. It is what makes a changed pack shape RED under every frozen artifact. Two failure directions, and the second is the bad one:
  - FALSE POSITIVE (what happened): a non-key string enters the pin, so the pin over-describes the shape and an unrelated code edit forces a spurious ledger walk. Noisy, self-announcing.
  - FALSE NEGATIVE: a key emitted by any route the scraper does not recognise — a constant, a format!, a helper, a loop over a slice — is ABSENT from the pin. The pin then silently under-describes the shape, and a real pack-shape change passes the coupling ledger green. That is the fooled certificate, and nothing currently tells us whether it is happening.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE BEAD. Working around the false positive by avoiding `.into()` at call sites teaches authors to route around the scraper, which is exactly how the false negative arrives.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decide what the pin should be derived FROM. Scraping literals out of a function body is a heuristic over syntax; the emitted key set is a property of the serialised OUTPUT. Deriving the pin by running the emitter and reading the keys off the produced JSON is the obvious alternative and should be argued for or against explicitly.
- Whichever is chosen: a key emitted by a route the deriver cannot see must be an ERROR, never a silent omission. Fail closed.
- Known-bad, both directions: (a) add a non-key literal, assert it does NOT enter the pin; (b) emit a key by a route the current scraper misses (a const, a format!, a helper), assert the pin goes RED rather than quietly shrinking.
- ANTI-VACUOUS AND LOAD-BEARING HERE: a pin that derives to ZERO keys, or fewer keys than the artifact actually has, must be an ERROR. A shrinking pin is the silent failure and it currently looks identical to a correct one.
- Audit the other derived pin kinds (fields, const, region, toml_array_contains) for the same asymmetry and report which fail open.

title: Six allowlist rows claim 'load-bearing check.sh gate, grandfathered pending the Rust port' for gates that are ported and no longer invoked
description:
WHAT: registries/substrate_allowlist.toml carries a `reason` per exempted .py file. Six rows still read some form of "Load-bearing check.sh gate ... Grandfathered pending the byte-exact Rust port" for files that ARE ported and that check.sh does NOT invoke:
  verify_orphans.py · verify_injection_count.py · verify_doc_consistency.py
  verify_knowledge_paths.py · verify_bank.py · verify_content_lock.py

MEASURED 2026-08-14: every one of those has crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/<name>.rs, and `grep -oE "python3 scripts/[a-z_]+\.py" scripts/check.sh` returns only six DIFFERENT files — export_anki, smoke_diagrams, smoke_feedback_links, smoke_learn_chrome, smoke_learn, smoke_weak_links. Those six are the only genuinely load-bearing Python left.

WHY IT IS A P1 AND NOT COSMETIC. The `reason` field is not decoration; it is the justification that keeps the exemption alive, and it is the only thing a reader consults when deciding whether a row may be removed. Six rows currently assert a status that would make removal WRONG ("check.sh hard-fails if it is absent, so it cannot simply be deleted" — verify_orphans) when in fact removal is exactly what is owed. The registry is arguing FOR keeping Python on a project whose Substrate Law wants it gone, using a fact that stopped being true when the port landed.

It also cost real work today: the controller issued a "fix the Python first, then the port" instruction to two agents based on the assumption that these files were still on the path. They are not. The instruction was corrected mid-flight.

THE UNDERLYING SHAPE, and the reason this belongs to milestone B: these reasons were true when written and became false when the code changed underneath, and nothing mechanically ties a row to the thing it describes. That is the doc-truth class B3 built `cdcp_gate doc-facts` for. A registry field is prose with a schema.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the six rows states its true status: ported, not invoked, retained (if at all) as a differential oracle, with the port bead named.
- A ROW THAT CLAIMS "load-bearing" IS MECHANICALLY CHECKED against whether check.sh actually invokes it. Derive the invocation set from scripts/check.sh; do not hand-maintain a second list. A row claiming load-bearing for a file check.sh never calls is RED, and so is the inverse — a file check.sh calls whose row does not say so.
- Known-bad both directions: flip a row to claim load-bearing for a ported gate -> RED naming both sides; add a python3 invocation to check.sh for a file whose row says oracle-only -> RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: zero invocations discovered is an ERROR (check.sh always calls something), and zero allowlist rows is an ERROR.
- Consider whether this is a doc-facts row rather than a new gate — the polarity lives in the registry prose and the probe is "does check.sh invoke this path". If doc-facts can carry it, prefer that over a twelfth bespoke gate.

title: Retire a differential oracle when its gate changes behaviour, instead of maintaining two implementations forever
description:
WHAT: record and enforce the policy the controller got wrong today, and apply it to the eleven retired oracles still in the tree.

THE DEFECT IN THE OLD RULE. The standing instruction was "PYTHON FIRST: fix the .py, watch the differential go RED, then move the port." That rule is correct only while the oracle is proving the port FAITHFUL — during migration, changing the Rust first makes the differential flag the FIX as the divergence. Its job COMPLETES AT PORT TIME. Applied afterwards it means every deliberate behaviour change is implemented twice, forever, and the second implementation is Python on a project whose Substrate Law puts Rust on the load-bearing path. The migration tool becomes a maintenance tax.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: eleven .py files have Rust ports and check.sh invokes NONE of them (verify_coverage, verify_objectives, verify_bank, verify_content_lock, verify_orphans, verify_doc_consistency, verify_injection_count, verify_knowledge_paths, validate_grounding, build_units, build_glossary_json). The only genuinely load-bearing Python is six unported smokes.

AND THE PROTECTION BEING PAID FOR IS BOUNDED, measured separately: a differential CANNOT see a defect both implementations share (bd-differential-shared-blindspot-4qje). verify_objectives reported "covered=106 of 106, mode=strict, EXIT 0" with not one comparison performed, and its harness passed that case for weeks because both sides produced the same wrong answer.

THE POLICY:
  1. A .py with no Rust port that check.sh invokes -> genuinely load-bearing. Do not grow it. Port it (epic bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd).
  2. A .py with a Rust port that check.sh does not invoke -> a retired oracle. NEVER add behaviour to it. A behaviour change is the trigger to RETIRE it.
  3. RETIREMENT IS CONDITIONAL, and this is the part that must not be lost: convert the harness cases into direct tests of the Rust that assert the VERDICT independently — what the correct answer IS — not that two implementations agree. Anti-vacuous and floor cases first; their failure mode is silence. If a case cannot carry across, KEEP the oracle and file the residual. Retiring an oracle and leaving the Rust with a weaker net than it had is a net loss.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The policy is written where agents will meet it, not only in this bead.
- Per-oracle disposition table for all eleven: retire now / retire when touched / keep with reason. Driven by the per-harness agreement-only ratio from bd-differential-shared-blindspot-4qje — a harness whose cases are ALL agreement-only cannot have its oracle retired without losing everything it tested, and that list is the stop-sign.
- Every retirement removes the allowlist row in the same change (see bd-allowlist-stale-load-bearing).
- Anti-vacuous: a converted harness that ends with zero cases, or whose floor cases were dropped in conversion, is an ERROR.

RETIREMENT BLOCKER FOUND, and it is the reason the six stale allowlist rows read the way they do.

scripts/check.sh HARD-FAILS if a ported oracle is ABSENT. Six presence checks, measured 2026-08-14:

  501  [ -f scripts/verify_orphans.py ]         || fail 'orphan gate required'

So  of any of those six takes check.sh RED at a step that says the file is REQUIRED. That is why verify_orphans' allowlist row says 'check.sh hard-fails if it is absent, so it cannot simply be deleted' — the row is describing a real mechanism. What makes it stale is the CONCLUSION, not the observation: the mechanism was correct while the .py was the implementation and is now a lock holding a retired oracle in place.

NOTE THE TWO SHAPES, because they retire differently. Lines 501, 760 and 800 assert the gate is 'required' — written when the .py WAS the gate. Lines 493, 678 and 709 already say 'differential oracle', so somebody had updated the wording without noticing the check itself had become a retention lock.

THIS IS ALSO WHY RETIREMENT MUST BE ATOMIC, and it belongs in the acceptance: retiring an oracle is a FOUR-part change in one commit — delete the .py, remove its allowlist row, remove its check.sh presence check, and convert its harness cases to independent verdict assertions. Any three of those without the fourth leaves the tree red or leaves a lie in a registry. A partial retirement is worse than none, exactly like the partial domain bump bd-6ycw refused to make.

I wrote this bead claiming eleven ported .py files are retired oracles because check.sh invokes none of them. That grep was true and the conclusion was false: check.sh calls six other shell scripts, and those invoke oracles check.sh never names.   ALSO INVOKED, and its allowlist row falsely says 'not on the check.sh path':
    build_learn.py
  PRESENCE-CHECKED (-f, hard-fails on absence) — a second, independent retention lock:
    validate_grounding · verify_doc_consistency · verify_injection_count · plus the four above

  1. is it still invoked, directly or transitively?
  2. is it presence-checked by check.sh or a nested script?
  3. is its differential harness all agreement-only, so retiring loses everything it tested?
Clearing two of three and deleting the file leaves the tree red or a lie in a registry — the partial-retirement failure this bead already warns about, with more edges than I knew.

ONLY ONE RETIREMENT HAS HAPPENED: build_units.py, verified afterwards to have no surviving invocation in scripts/ or crates/. It does leave dangling advice — two error strings and a generated_by literal still tell users to 'run build_units.py' (bd-stale-build-units-py-refs-milf, plus new instances in smoke_learn_v2). title: verify-bank: a bank_policy.toml with zero [[domain_min]] rows checks zero per-module floors and reports PASS
description:
WHAT: scripts/verify_bank.py and crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/verify_bank.rs read [[domain_min]] rows from knowledge/bank_policy.toml. If the table is absent or empty, the per-module loop iterates zero times and the gate reports PASS with no indication that fifteen floors were not checked.

This is the empty-input-set-is-a-pass pattern: a policy that LOST its domain_min rows reports identically to one that enforced all fifteen. The live policy currently carries 15 rows, so nothing is breached today.

DONE IN bd-8exw (partial, deliberately): both implementations now print '  domain_floors=N checked (approved pool)' in the PASS report, so a zero READS as zero instead of as silence. That makes the vacuity visible; it does not make it RED.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is a policy call and not a code call: should zero enforced domain floors be an ERROR? Arguments both ways —
  FOR: 'an empty input set is an ERROR, never a pass' is standing doctrine, and this is a textbook instance.
  AGAINST: bank_policy.toml's [[domain_min]] is optional by design (the gate has working built-in pool_min/exam_n defaults and no built-in module list), and ~30 differential fixtures deliberately declare no domain floors because they are testing something else. Making it RED means every one of those fixtures grows a domain_min row.

ACCEPTANCE (whoever takes it, decide the question first and record the decision):
- Either zero domain floors is RED when bank/items is non-empty, with every fixture updated in the same change — or the row count stays advisory and the reason is written into the gate header so the next reader does not re-open it.
- If RED: known-bad is a policy file with the [[domain_min]] table deleted -> RED naming the condition, on a bank that is otherwise green.

NOTE the related, already-correct legs so they are not swept up: 'zero items loaded', 'zero approved items (N scanned)', and the per-file 'items[] yielded zero items' are all ERRORs today (verified 2026-08-14, exit 1 on both implementations).

title: scripts/verify_bank.py cannot be retired: scripts/check.sh reaches it through smoke_slo.sh, one level of indirection
description:
WHAT: during bd-8exw the instruction was to retire the oracle — `git rm scripts/verify_bank.py`, drop its substrate_allowlist row, convert the differential into direct Rust verdict tests — on the stated premise that 'scripts/check.sh does NOT invoke python3 scripts/verify_bank.py anywhere'.

That grep is TRUE and the conclusion drawn from it is FALSE. check.sh reaches the oracle one level of indirection away:

  scripts/check.sh:719        sh scripts/smoke_slo.sh || fail "L7 SLO budgets"
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:31     [ -f scripts/verify_bank.py ] || fail "missing scripts/verify_bank.py"
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:150    run_timed "bank_verify" "$VERIFY_MS"  python3 scripts/verify_bank.py
  scripts/smoke_slo.sh:96-99  run_timed fails on a NON-ZERO rc, not only on the wall clock

So both the FILE and its VERDICT are load-bearing on the check.sh path, and slo.toml:18-19 budgets it as bank_verify_ms = 10000.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 rather than argued — a temp root carrying slo.toml, scripts/smoke_slo.sh and the golden fixture, with verify_bank.py deliberately absent:
  smoke_slo: FAIL: missing scripts/verify_bank.py
  exit 2

The retirement was therefore NOT performed, under the conditional in the same instruction ('do not retire the oracle if that leaves the Rust with a weaker net than it had'). Both implementations were fixed together instead, PYTHON FIRST, and the differential was watched go RED (exit 101, 30 of 35 cases) before the port followed.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this row: `grep -n python3 scripts/check.sh` does not enumerate what check.sh runs. check.sh dispatches to sh scripts and to cargo, and both can reach anything. Any future 'is this script still on the path?' question must be answered by RUNNING the entry point with the file absent, not by grepping the entry point.

ACCEPTANCE, in order:
1. Decide where the bank_verify_ms wall should be measured. The obvious answer is the Rust gate — `cdcp_gate verify-bank` is what check.sh:481 actually enforces, and timing the oracle budgets a program nothing depends on for its verdict.
2. Repoint scripts/smoke_slo.sh:31/150 at the built binary, and update slo.toml:18's comment. NOTE the budget will need re-measuring: the Rust is not the same wall as CPython + tomllib over 804 files.
3. THEN, and only then, retire the oracle: git rm scripts/verify_bank.py, delete its registries/substrate_allowlist.toml row (substrate_guard's stale_row_for_a_deleted_file_is_red makes leaving it an error), and convert crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_bank.rs from byte-equality against the oracle into direct assertions on the Rust's verdict.
4. CARRY EVERY CASE ACROSS. The 43 cases in that file are the gate's whole behavioural spec. Two need real thought rather than mechanical translation:
   - the_correct_letter_order_is_pinned_and_hash_seed_independent — its behavioural leg (stdout byte-equal across four PYTHONHASHSEED values) and its structural legs (the ordered tuple exists in the .py source and the loops iterate it, not the frozenset) are BOTH oracle-specific. The Rust has no equivalent hazard because ALLOWED_CORRECT is an array and the counters are BTreeMaps, but the replacement must assert THAT — an array-order pin plus a 'no HashMap in this gate' source check — or the coverage is lost, not carried.
   - an_oracle_raise_matches_on_stdout_and_exit_code_but_not_traceback_text — becomes a direct assertion that the raise paths emit empty stdout, exit 1, and a non-empty stderr naming the exception.

Both are carryable, which is why this is a scheduling problem and not a refusal.

title: export_anki.py ships 25 RETIRED bank items into the learner Anki deck
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py never reads BankItem.status. load_bank_items() globs every bank/items/*.toml (804) and load_seed42_bank_items() returns every row of web/data/bank_items_seed42.json (804). Both are 779 approved + 25 retired. --source bank and --source seed42 therefore emit 25 WITHDRAWN questions as Anki cards. --source keys is fine (40 drawn-form items, already approved-only by export-web's write guard).

WHY IT MATTERS: the Anki deck is a SHIPPED LEARNER ARTIFACT — registries/substrate_allowlist.toml calls it exactly that ('Load-bearing check.sh step: V11 Anki export, a shipped learner artifact'). Anki is a spaced-repetition tool, so this does not merely SHOW a withdrawn item once, it drills it on a schedule, off-platform, where no gate can reach it afterwards. An item is retired because a BETTER COPY OF THE SAME PROPOSITION exists (argument per id in cdcp_bank::SANCTIONED_RETIRED), so the learner memorises the copy that lost.

THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSUMER OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE. bd-7big (quiz.js draw) and bd-qqwc (units_index check items) are fixed 2026-08-14; learn_units.js pickItems topic/module fill was a third, found in the same sweep and fixed with them. This one is outside that wave's ownership and is filed rather than edited.

DO NOT FIX BY FILTERING THE PACK. web/data/bank_items_seed42.json must ship all 804 rows or client-side grading breaks: cdcp_wasm::grade_digest_json feeds those exact bytes to Bank::from_json_str which recomputes bank_hash, and cdcp_grade::grade hard-fails on a mismatch. Decision recorded in web/data/README.md and the web.bank-items-pack row of registries/goldens-couplings.toml. THE MANIFEST SHIPS WHOLE; THE CONSUMER FILTERS.

FIX: filter status == 'approved' in load_bank_items() and load_seed42_bank_items(). Report both counts separately (manifest rows AND approved pool) — collapsing 804 and 779 into one number is the exact confusion that produced this whole defect class.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No exported card carries a non-approved item id, for every --source.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a filter that removes every row is an ERROR naming the fault, never an empty deck. Zero cards exported is a FAILURE.

Left wrong ON PURPOSE for one wave and documented as such in that file's header, because fixing it REWRITES THE TRACKED ARTIFACT and that regeneration deserves its own verified step rather than riding along on a documentation fix.
  2. docs/ROADMAP-WAVES.md:102 — "packaging artifact: `build_units.py` mechanically emits one unit per `##` heading". The sentence is still true of the behaviour; the name is wrong.
  3. scripts/smoke_learn_v2.py:27 — the failure message for an absent web/data/units_index.json says "run build_units.py". That instruction cannot be followed.

HOW TO DO (1), the only one with a tripwire:
  a. Change the Jv::Str literal in build_units.rs to "cdcp_gate build-units" and update the header note directly above it.
  b. cargo build -p cdcp_gate --bin cdcp_gate   (the BUILT binary, never cargo run)
  c. Regenerate ONCE, from the engine root, in a single command:
       cd <engine root> && ./target/debug/cdcp_gate --root <engine root> build-units
  d. cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test diff_build_units
     live_inputs_are_green_and_reproduce_the_tracked_artifact is the tripwire: it compares the gate's bytes to the committed artifact and stays RED until the regeneration lands. Do not silence it — it is the read-only proof that the committed copy is current.

CWD TRAP — cost ~40 minutes on 2026-08-14 and is the reason (1) was deferred rather than finished. `./target/debug/cdcp_gate build-units` appeared to HANG for 7+ minutes, twice, and was misdiagnosed first as a cargo build-directory lock and then as a sandbox write block. There is no defect in the gate. The same trap then made the agent believe web/data/units_index.json had been deleted; it was present the whole time.

Three rules that follow, and they generalise past this bead:
  - Always `cd <absolute engine root> &&` in the SAME command, and pass --root explicitly.
  - Verify a builder's write by READING THE FILE. Never infer it from an exit code, and never read an exit code through a pipe.
  - A command that appears to hang against this tree is a cwd question before it is a lock question.

THE RECIPE, proven in diff_verify_orphans.rs this wave, and the part that is easy to get wrong: REWRITING THE ASSERTION IS NOT ENOUGH. Every option-shape case runs against the LIVE tree, which is green. Asserting "this spelling still passes" on a tree that passes is worth nothing — no defect that suppresses a finding can show up in a run that has no finding to suppress. The INPUT must change too. For each spelling: point it at a tree with a KNOWN planted finding and assert (a) the spelling normalises to the one resolved path, (b) the run scanned THAT tree — assert the item count, which is what catches a silent fallback to a default — and (c) it still reaches the planted finding and goes RED for it. For the flag cases, assert the flag changed the MODE the report names, since that is the claim the case exists to make.

title: export_anki.py .apkg is NOT byte-reproducible: 98.4% of bytes differ between two runs of the SAME script
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py writes dist/anki/*.apkg through write_apkg_pure(), which stamps now = int(time.time()) into col.crt, col.mod, col.scm and every notes.mod / cards.mod row, then zips the temp collection.anki2 with zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED so the entry carries the temp file's mtime. The deck is a function of the WALL CLOCK, not only of the bank.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13). Two runs of the ORACLE ITSELF two seconds apart, on byte-identical copies of the live bank, genanki absent so both took the pure-sqlite backend:
  dist/anki/cdcp_bank.tsv    IDENTICAL
  dist/anki/README.txt       IDENTICAL
  dist/anki/cdcp_bank.apkg   209382 of 212731 bytes DIFFER (98.4%)
Same uncompressed size (565248) and same compressed size (212511) both times; only the content differs. The zip entry date_time moved 18:19:34 -> 18:19:36 and the collection.anki2 sha256 changed completely, because a one-second shift in an embedded integer avalanches through the DEFLATE stream.

WHY IT MATTERS TWICE:
1. PRODUCT. dist/anki/** is a SHIPPED LEARNER ARTIFACT. A rebuild produces a bit-different deck from identical content, so a checksum, a CDN cache key, a signature, or any 'did the deck change?' comparison is useless. Nothing today notices; nothing today could.
2. THE PORT. bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13 requires the Rust port to be BYTE-EXACT with the oracle. Against a non-reproducible oracle that criterion is UNSATISFIABLE — not hard, impossible. The .apkg leg is consequently BLOCKED: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs returns ERROR (exit 4) naming this bead rather than writing an unverified hand-rolled SQLite file to learners. The TSV/CSV/README/stdout/stderr/exit surface IS ported and byte-verified.

FIX (in the ORACLE FIRST, per the bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.12 precedent): make the deck a pure function of its inputs.
  - source now from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH when set, else a pinned constant, NOT time.time()
  - set a fixed date_time on every ZipInfo instead of letting zipfile read the temp file's mtime
  - keep the existing content-hash-derived note/card ids and _guid_for GUIDs (already deterministic — they are why re-import still merges today despite the byte churn)

ACCEPTANCE:
  - two consecutive runs of scripts/export_anki.py produce byte-identical dist/anki/cdcp_bank.apkg
  - crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_export_anki.rs::the_oracle_apkg_is_not_byte_reproducible_against_itself goes RED (it is a PINNED DEFECT and says so in its failure message)
  - only THEN port the .apkg leg, add dist/anki/cdcp_bank.apkg to the compare() file set, and delete that pinned test
  - the dependency argument for rusqlite + zip in crates/cdcp_gate/Cargo.toml is made at that point, not before

title: export_anki.py: 'correct in "ABCD"' is a SUBSTRING test, so a missing or 2-letter answer key crashes with a TypeError traceback
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py format_answer() does

    correct = str(item.get('correct') or '').strip().upper()
    idx = letter_to_index(correct) if correct in 'ABCD' else -1

'correct in "ABCD"' tests SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT, not membership in a set. Python says '' in 'ABCD' is True and 'AB' in 'ABCD' is True. Both take the letter_to_index branch, which calls ord(letter.upper()) — and ord() requires a string of length exactly 1. The script dies with

    TypeError: ord() expected a character, but string of length 0 found

MEASURED 2026-08-14 while porting to Rust (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13). Not reachable from --source bank today (all 804 bank TOMLs carry a single-letter 'correct'), but DIRECTLY reachable from --source keys: load_keys_seed42_pack() does k = key_map.get(it['id'], {}) then k.get('correct') or '', so ANY mock40 item whose id is absent from keys_seed42.json produces correct='' and crashes the export. One missing key kills the deck for all 40 cards, with a traceback instead of a named error.

Note the asymmetry that makes it look harmless: a correct of 'E' is NOT a substring of 'ABCD', so it falls through to idx=-1 and ships as the bare letter. The BAD inputs crash and the OUT-OF-RANGE input ships. That is backwards.

FIX: 'correct in ("A","B","C","D")', or len(correct) == 1 and correct in 'ABCD'. Then decide what an unresolvable key should DO — see bd-anki-answerless-card-ships; a traceback and a silently-shipped bare letter are both wrong.

REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED, in the port: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs::format_answer takes the same branch and returns GateError::Error (exit 4) where the oracle emits a traceback (exit 1), because a Python traceback is not portable output. That divergence is recorded in the module header. Fixing it in the Rust alone would make the port stricter than its oracle and blind the differential.

ACCEPTANCE: a keys pack missing one answer key produces a NAMED error identifying the item id, not a traceback; a test injects a missing key and asserts the message; crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/export_anki.rs::format_answer_reproduces_the_substring_defect_rather_than_fixing_it is updated in the same commit.

title: export_anki.py ships cards whose answer key resolves to nothing, and exits 0
description:
WHAT: scripts/export_anki.py format_answer() ends with

    if 0 <= idx < len(choices): return f'{correct}) {choices[idx]}'
    return correct or '?'

so an item whose 'correct' letter points past the end of its 'choices' list — or is not an A-D letter at all — is EXPORTED as a card whose Back is just the bare letter ('D', 'E') or the literal '?'. No warning, no count, exit 0, deck shipped.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13), byte-identical in the Python and the Rust port: an item with choices=['only'] and correct='D' ships as a card reading 'D'; correct='E' ships as 'E'. A learner sees a question with no answer.

Two related shapes in the same code, all reproduced by the port and none of them a verdict today:
  - module 0 is unreachable by --module 0, because filter_items does int(it.get('module') or -1): the falsy 0 becomes -1. Harmless while no module 0 exists; a trap the day one does.
  - --source seed42 falling back to the bank still prints 'source=seed42' and writes 'Source: seed42' into dist/anki/README.txt while the deck it built is the BANK deck under the cdcp_bank stem. The operator note records the source that was ASKED for, not the one used.

WHY IT MATTERS: dist/anki/** is a shipped learner artifact. The exporter has NO admissibility check of any kind — it does not verify the answer resolves, does not verify the stem is non-empty, and does not filter by status (bd-fqpp). Its only floor is 'more than zero cards'.

FIX: count unresolvable answers during the export; make a non-zero count a NAMED failure (never a silent pass) or, at minimum, report it on stdout with the ids. Anti-vacuous: a run where EVERY card is unresolvable must be an ERROR.

ACCEPTANCE: an item with an out-of-range 'correct' makes the export RED and names the item id; the count is printed on the green path too; crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_export_anki.rs::an_answer_letter_outside_the_choice_list_falls_through_to_the_letter is updated in the same commit (it currently PINS the exit-0 behaviour and says so).

WHAT: the audit for bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w enumerated every recorded meta-test pair in this repo. Two of them are not pairs. Both closed a bead.

  bd-hardening-c-status-hzs.1 (C1, approved-only assembly): 'Meta-test at authoring: filter deleted -> exit 101, 6 of 9 RED; restored -> 0.'

title: check.sh line 779 runs 'export_anki.py --check', a flag that does not exist, so the first branch is dead and always exits 2
description:
WHAT: scripts/check.sh line 779 reads

    python3 scripts/export_anki.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 || python3 scripts/export_anki.py >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "V11 Anki export"

MEASURED 2026-08-14: export_anki.py has no --check option. argparse rejects it:
    export_anki.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --check
    exit 2
The first branch NEVER succeeds. Every check.sh run pays for a guaranteed-failing invocation and then falls through to the real one. The gate is not broken — it is dishonest about what it runs, and a reader of check.sh believes there is a cheap --check mode that never existed.

Two further problems on the same line:
  - Both invocations send stdout AND stderr to /dev/null, so when the export genuinely fails the operator gets 'V11 Anki export' and nothing else. The FAIL: line the script wrote — 'zero items to export', 'unknown format(s)', 'keys/seed42 packs not found' — is discarded. Same class as the 2026-08-13 sweep's cron-piped-to-/dev/null findings.
  - The step WRITES dist/anki/** as a side effect of a check, with the default --format tsv,apkg. A gate that mutates the tree to decide a verdict cannot run concurrently with anything that reads it.

REQUESTED REPLACEMENT (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13 does not own check.sh; these are the exact lines to wire, replacing line 779):
    echo "==> cdcp_gate export-anki (V11 · deterministic export surface, byte-exact vs scripts/export_anki.py)"
    cargo run -q -p cdcp_gate -- export-anki --format tsv,csv --out dist/anki || fail "V11 Anki export (tsv/csv)"
    ok "V11 Anki export tsv/csv (byte-exact with the oracle)"
    echo "==> V11 Anki .apkg deck (oracle; port blocked on bd-anki-apkg-not-reproducible-e13a)"
    python3 scripts/export_anki.py --format apkg --out dist/anki || fail "V11 Anki .apkg deck"
    ok "V11 Anki .apkg deck"
No --check, no /dev/null swallowing the failure text, and the .apkg stays on the oracle until it is made reproducible.

ACCEPTANCE: check.sh contains no invocation of a flag the target does not accept; a planted failure in the export surfaces its FAIL: line in the check.sh log rather than only 'V11 Anki export'.

title: The safe restore pattern is documented but not enforced — no gate can tell an agent it just read a verdict off a stale binary
description:
WHAT: bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w documented and reproduced the restore trap (crates/cdcp_gate/tests/support/rebuild.rs, crates/cdcp_gate/tests/restore_rebuild_trap.rs) and stated the rule in .flywheel/CHARTER.md and docs/TESTING.md. Nothing enforces it. An agent that restores with mv and reads the verdict is corrected by no mechanism — which is the same shape as every other convention this project has had to replace with a gate.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY DONE HERE: the fix belongs in crates/cdcp_gate/src/, which the p65w agent did not own this wave (four sibling agents held adjacent surfaces).

WHAT WILL NOT WORK, MEASURED — do not re-derive it: a gate that asserts artifact_mtime > source_mtime is USELESS. title: smoke_a11y: the marker census is context-blind — markers inside an HTML comment satisfy every check
description:
REPRODUCED AND FILED under the port standard for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19: found while porting scripts/smoke_a11y.py to Rust, ported as-is rather than fixed, because a port stricter than its oracle blinds the differential harness.

WHAT: smoke_a11y searches the WHOLE FILE with nine regexes and never looks at where a match lands. A page whose ONLY skip link, honesty banner, main landmark and stylesheet link are inside an HTML comment is GREEN. So is a page whose markers live inside a script string or a template body. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the vacuous-pass shape the L4 doctrine is about. The gate reports 'pages_checked=7' with a six-marker checklist, and a reader takes that to mean the seven shipped shells carry those markers. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an argument for an HTML parser in the gate. The same class covers a skip link that is present, uncommented, and last in the DOM, or hidden with display:none. A byte census cannot decide reachability at all.

title: smoke_learn_v2: check_item_ids coverage passes VACUOUSLY when units is empty — 'ok: coverage 0/0'
description:
REPRODUCED AND FILED under the port standard for bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.20. The Rust port reproduces it and pins it; it does not repair it.

WHAT: scripts/smoke_learn_v2.py:51 reads

    if units and with_checks / len(units) < 0.8:
        fail(...)
    else:
        ok(f'check_item_ids coverage {with_checks}/{len(units)}')

The leading 'units and' is there to avoid a ZeroDivisionError, and it does — by routing zero units into the ok() branch. An empty units array therefore prints 'ok: check_item_ids coverage 0/0'. A coverage assertion computed over nothing reports exactly like one computed over 134 units and satisfied.

MEASURED: with units set to [] and by_module left populated, the run prints that ok line. crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_learn_v2.rs case 'zero units, vacuous coverage ok' shows BOTH implementations printing it, and the surrounding fixture is GREEN overall — exit 0 — because nothing else in the gate looks at the units array.

THE SAME SHAPE, ONE LINE DOWN: line 59, 'if m01 and min(...) < 2', vacuously prints 'ok: M01 every unit has >=2 check items' when the M01 module list is empty. That one is currently masked because the module-unit floor at line 31 fires first on an empty m01 — masked, not fixed. If the floors are ever loosened, or the module id is ever renamed in only one of the two places, the mask goes away silently.

A THIRD, RELATED WEAKNESS worth deciding in the same pass: unit_count is a DECLARED FIELD, not len(units). A file with unit_count 134 and an empty units array clears the unit_count floor and the coverage check together.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Zero units is an ERROR, not a pass: a distinct fail() naming the vacuity, in the shape 'zero units in units_index.json (vacuous coverage is ERROR)'.
- The m01 leg gets the same treatment rather than relying on an upstream floor to mask it.
- Decide whether unit_count should be cross-checked against len(units); if not, say so in the gate header rather than leaving the reader to assume.
- Both implementations change together, or the Python oracle is retired in the same commit. The reproduction tests named above become the known-bad legs.

title: five gates never get their success token probed on the GREEN side — a wrong token would read as covered
description:
FOUND 2026-08-14 while building crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, and found by READING SOURCE rather than by any probe, which is the point.

The meta-gate asserts, per gate, that exit == 0 is EQUIVALENT to "stdout opens a line with this gate registered success token". Five of the nineteen gates are registered live_probe = false with a reason, so the equivalence is only ever exercised on the RED side for them:
  build-units, build-glossary-json   — they WRITE tracked artifacts (web/data/*.json); a probe must never mutate the tree
  install-hooks                       — writes into the clone .git; also empty_probe = false
  verify-injection-count              — requires --log/--readme; no argument-free invocation
  verify-step-count                   — requires --measured; no argument-free invocation

CONSEQUENCE, and it already bit: verify-step-count was registered with the token "verify-step-count: ok:" by pattern-matching the gates around it. Its actual verdict line is PASS (verify_step_count.rs:658, out.push_str(if failed { "FAIL" } else { "PASS" })). A gate whose token is never observed on the green side cannot have a wrong token detected — the red-side check "no token on a failing path" is satisfied for free by a token the gate never prints. The row read as covered while checking nothing. It was corrected by reading the source; nothing in the harness would have caught it.

This is the same failure this repo has measured elsewhere: LEG F of the meta-gate exists precisely to stop the token side passing vacuously across the whole roster, and it does — at least one gate must be observed GREEN carrying its token. But that floor is global, not per gate.

FIX, in increasing order of cost:
1. Per-gate green-side floor rather than a global one: every gate registered with a token must be observed GREEN carrying it at least once, or carry an explicit exclusion with a reason. That converts these five from silently-unprobed to declared.
2. Give the two argument-requiring gates a probe with minimal valid arguments built in a tempdir, so they have a green path a probe can reach.
3. Probe the two builders against a COPY of the engine root rather than the live tree, so their green path is exercised without writing a tracked artifact. The tree is roughly 9 MB, so a copy is affordable.

ACCEPTANCE: every registered success token has been observed on a green run at least once, or its absence is a registered exclusion with a reason; and a mutation pair proves a wrong token is caught (register a deliberately wrong token for one gate; the suite must go non-zero and name that gate).
close_reason: VERDICT: 3/5 probed GREEN (install-hooks, verify-injection-count, verify-step-count); 2 retired from dispatcher (build-units, build-glossary-json). cargo test -p cdcp_gate --test differential_verdict_census exit 0. SHA 9cff2f78f4535743d8389fd55d34ff1d0b1f5933

title: Fleet-level cargo build-lock deadlock: 55 concurrent cargo processes, oldest 1h, zero CPU — verification work cannot run at all
description:
WHAT: measured 2026-08-14 19:20 on the live tree at /Users/josh/cdcp-self-study/course-engine. 55 cargo processes alive, the oldest started 18:24 (about one hour), every one at 0.0% CPU in state S, load average 9-10 with essentially no CPU work happening. Every new invocation prints 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' and never proceeds. Three separate attempts to run 'cargo test -p cdcp_assemble' timed out at 500-600s without reaching a single 'Compiling' line.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN CHASED: it blocked the re-run half of bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w. That audit needed to re-run previously-passed meta-test pairs under a FORCED rebuild to confirm their verdicts still hold, and could not, so the sample is reported as BLOCKED rather than as passed. A verification that cannot run must not be recorded as a verification that passed.

TWO WORKAROUNDS TRIED AND BOTH FAILED, so do not re-derive them:
  1. A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the agent scratchpad. Cold builds HANG at the first crates that carry build scripts (proc-macro2, libc, serde, version_check): the build-script executables appear as live processes at 0.0% CPU and 32 bytes RSS and never advance. Reading: build-script binaries under the scratchpad cannot be exec'd by the sandbox, and the failure presents as a hang, not an error.
  2. A full rsync copy of the tree with its own target dir. Same hang, same crates.
So an agent that needs an isolated build has NO working route today; it must contend for the one shared target dir.

RELATED, CLOSED, AND NOT THE SAME THING: bd-gl4j ('Concurrent check.sh runs corrupt each other — a false RED is indistinguishable from a real one') covered correctness under concurrency. This is LIVENESS: nothing is corrupted, nothing runs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A named cause for the stall (lock holder identified, not guessed), or a mechanism that prevents N agents from serialising on one target dir.
- A supported way for one agent to build in isolation — either a target dir location whose build scripts can execute, or a documented shared-target protocol with a build slot.
- Anti-vacuous: the fix is demonstrated with concurrent agents actually building, not with a single agent on a quiet machine.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of bd-syspolicyd-stall-blocks-all-builds-dp91, which a sibling filed for the same stall with the actual culprit named (syspolicyd pegged; every newly linked binary hangs in _dyld_start). I filed mine from process forensics before seeing theirs. All my evidence has been moved onto dp91 as a comment - the 32-byte-RSS build-script signature, the six agent target dirs, and the finding that the private-CARGO_TARGET_DIR workaround hangs identically and therefore is not an escape. Nothing is lost by closing this; dp91 is the one to fix.

title: grep python3 check.sh does not enumerate what check.sh runs — the invocation set is transitive through shell scripts
description:
WHAT: the question "which Python is still load-bearing" was answered three times today by grepping scripts/check.sh, and was wrong every time. The invocation set is TRANSITIVE: check.sh calls six other shell scripts, and those invoke oracles check.sh never names.

THE THREE ERRORS, in order, all mine:
1. `grep -oE "python3 scripts/[a-z_]+\.py" check.sh` -> reported 6. The character class has NO DIGITS, so it silently dropped smoke_a11y.py and smoke_learn_v2.py. A pattern that cannot match a legal input under-reports without erroring.
2. Corrected to `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` -> reported 8. Still only check.sh itself.
3. Correct answer, sweeping scripts/*.sh and scripts/*.mjs -> THIRTEEN python3 invocations. Four ported oracles are still invoked transitively (verify_bank, verify_coverage, verify_objectives, verify_orphans), plus build_learn.py whose allowlist row claims it is "not on the check.sh path".

MEASURED BY A SUBAGENT, which is how it was caught: check.sh:719 calls smoke_slo.sh; smoke_slo.sh:31 hard-fails on scripts/verify_bank.py absence and :150 TIMES `python3 scripts/verify_bank.py` with run_timed failing on non-zero rc. A temp root without that file exits 2. The agent refused a retirement instruction on that evidence, correctly.

WHY IT IS P1: this measurement decides whether a file may be deleted. Acting on the wrong answer deletes a file the build needs, or leaves a Substrate Law violation in place believing it is already gone. It also fed a wrong instruction to four subagents mid-wave.

THE UNDERLYING SHAPE: the same one as bd-8mjs (a bound moved behind a named constant is invisible to a literal scan) and the DCG guard firing on prose. A scan that stops at the first file, or at one syntactic form, reports like a scan that covered everything.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A DERIVED, transitive invocation set: start at check.sh, follow every shell script it invokes, and report every interpreter invocation and every -f presence check reachable from it. Not a hand-maintained list — the hand-maintained list IS the defect (see bd-allowlist-stale-load-bearing-seq9, where six rows describe a status that stopped being true).
- The allowlist `reason` for every .py is checked against that derived set. A row claiming "not on the check.sh path" for a file reachable from check.sh is RED, and so is the inverse.
- Known-bad both directions: add a python3 invocation inside a nested shell script for a file whose row says oracle-only -> RED; mark a row load-bearing for a file nothing reaches -> RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a traversal that discovers zero invocations is an ERROR — check.sh always runs something. Assert a floor derived from the tree.
- Cover .mjs too: four node gates are on the path and js/mjs is deliberately outside the substrate floor (bd-yp9x).

title: BUILDER SHAPE: smoke_feedback_links writes topic_anchors.json before the verdict, so a RED run leaves an artifact
description:
FINDING (builder verdict-shape, class bd-builder-verdict-shape-qm65 — third instance found; REPRODUCED not fixed).

WHAT: scripts/smoke_feedback_links.py is listed in scripts/check.sh's own header as a step that MUTATES a tracked file (web/data/topic_anchors.json [M] regenerated). The write happens at source line ~291, inside the topic-anchor refresh block. The verdict is not decided until line ~450. Every error collected BEFORE the write — registry defects, results.js surface defects, slug-map drift in either direction, learn_md.js defects — reaches the write and then goes RED. So a RED run leaves a freshly regenerated tracked artifact behind.

THE GATE THEREFORE HAS TWO DIFFERENT RED SHAPES, which is what a builder audit has to know:
  * RED via a COLLECTED error  -> artifact IS rewritten.
  * RED via an EARLY RETURN (missing results.js, MODULE_LEARN_SLUGS not found, missing/invalid/empty keys, missing/empty bank) -> the return happens before the write, so a stale artifact survives untouched.

SUCCESS-TOKEN LEG, checked explicitly because three prior instances of that class exist: NO. Measured across four RED shapes — collected error, early return, missing registry, assessed-but-untaught — the oracle prints no PASS token on any non-zero path. The verdict is composed once at the end and the early returns print 'FAIL: smoke_feedback_links — ...'. This is NOT a fourth instance.

EVIDENCE: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_smoke_feedback_links.rs — a_red_run_still_writes_the_artifact_in_both_implementations, the_early_return_legs_do_not_reach_the_write, no_red_path_prints_a_success_token. All three run BOTH implementations in SEPARATE tree copies and compare the bytes written.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: byte-exactness against the oracle includes the bytes written; moving the write after the verdict would make the port diverge from the oracle on every collected-error case.

ACCEPTANCE (when the oracle is retired): compose the artifact in memory, decide the verdict, and write only on the green path — or write through a temp file and rename only after the verdict, the shape scripts/verify_coverage.py already uses for --write-json. Either way a RED run must leave the tracked artifact exactly as it found it.

    if a and (row.get('module') is None or int(row.get('module')) == mod_n):

Reachable only through the FALLBACK path (an existing artifact plus a failed build_learn import), because a freshly generated map always writes an int or null — which is exactly why it has never been seen.

PORT BEHAVIOUR: crates/cdcp_gate/src/gates/smoke_feedback_links.rs treats a non-coercible module as 'does not equal mod_n' and carries on, so it reports where the oracle crashes. Both are non-zero on a tree where this matters only if something else is also wrong; on a tree where nothing else is wrong the Rust is GREEN and the oracle is a traceback. That is a REAL divergence and it is recorded rather than papered over.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE ORACLE: the oracle is frozen as the differential reference for the port.

ACCEPTANCE: when the oracle is retired, keep the Rust behaviour (a malformed module field disqualifies the anchor) and add a named error for it, so a corrupt topic_anchors.json reports instead of either crashing or being silently tolerated.

title: Two subagents died mid-task from API errors under fleet load; their beads need re-dispatch and their partial work needs adjudication
description:
WHAT: two of nine concurrent agents terminated early with "API Error: Connection closed mid-response" during wave 8. Their work is partially on disk and neither reported.

DEAD AGENTS AND THEIR STATE:
1. PORTS .14 smoke_diagrams + .15 smoke_learn_chrome. Left FOUR substantial files on disk, all brace-balanced (structural check: open==close in every one): src/gates/smoke_diagrams.rs 123807B, src/gates/smoke_learn_chrome.rs 32100B, tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs 50632B, tests/diff_smoke_learn_chrome.rs 27557B. Oracles untouched. NEVER COMPILED OR TESTED — the fleet was deadlocked on cargo when it died. build.rs globs src/gates/*.rs, so these files are ALREADY IN THE BUILD for every other agent.
2. STALE-BINARY TRAP AUDIT (bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w). Last words: "build scripts can not execute under the scratchpad sandbox. Reverting to the live target dir." Almost certainly left little, but the audit half — re-running previously-passed meta-test pairs under a forced rebuild — was never started, and that half is the one that tells us whether existing evidence is sound.

THE CAUSE IS MINE, and it belongs in the record: nine concurrent agents against one cargo target directory. Cargo serialises on a GLOBAL package-cache lock, so an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR does not help — measured by a sibling: 52 queued cargo processes, 0 rustc, lock holder asleep 47+ minutes. Under that, agents cannot build or test, so they cannot verify their own work; two handed back explicitly unverified suites and two died. Prior waves of six ran cleanly. The limit is not agent count in the abstract, it is CONCURRENT CARGO CONSUMERS.

- ADJUDICATE the four orphan port files before anything else: they are in the build. Either they compile and their differentials pass — in which case finish the port properly and claim it — or they do not, in which case remove them and re-dispatch .14/.15 clean. Do NOT leave unverified generated code sitting in a globbed directory; that is a fooled certificate waiting to happen, since a gate file that exists reads like a gate that works.
- Re-dispatch bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14 and .15 and the bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w audit.
- RECORD A CONCURRENCY CEILING derived from the measurement, not from taste, and put it where the next controller will read it. Note the asymmetry: agents that only read files parallelise fine; agents that build or test do not.
- A blocked verification honestly reported is worth more than an assumed one. Both surviving agents that hit this said so explicitly and named what they could not run — that behaviour is correct and should be the documented expectation, not an apology.

title: grep python3 check.sh does not enumerate what check.sh runs — two oracles hide behind $CHECKER
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14. A survey concluded that check.sh invokes none of the ported .py oracles, by grepping check.sh directly. That is false twice over, and the second way is the interesting one.

FIRST INDIRECTION — check.sh calls other shell scripts, and THOSE invoke the oracles. A sibling falsified the original claim with smoke_slo.sh (check.sh:719), which hard-fails on scripts/verify_bank.py absence at :31 and times "python3 scripts/verify_bank.py" at :150.

SECOND INDIRECTION, found while correcting the first and NOT in the corrected count either — two oracles are invoked through a VARIABLE, so no grep for a .py filename anywhere in the tree can see the call site:
  scripts/selftest_doc_consistency.sh:49   CHECKER="scripts/verify_doc_consistency.py"
  scripts/selftest_doc_consistency.sh:144  python3 "$CHECKER" --root "$1"
  scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh:86   CHECKER="scripts/verify_injection_count.py"
  scripts/selftest_injection_count.sh:196  python3 "$CHECKER" ...   (also :202, :208)
Both selftests are run by check.sh (:767 and :802).

FULL TRANSITIVE CENSUS, resolved by following check.sh run_selftest / sh scripts/*.sh calls into each script and then grepping each for both literal and variable python3 targets:
  verify_orphans.py          INVOKED, 8 sites  check.sh:508 -> selftest_orphan.sh
  verify_objectives.py       INVOKED, 6 sites  check.sh:714 -> selftest_l7_objectives.sh
  verify_coverage.py         INVOKED, 3 sites  check.sh:683 -> selftest_l6_coverage.sh
  verify_bank.py             INVOKED, 2 sites  check.sh:719 -> smoke_slo.sh
  verify_doc_consistency.py  INVOKED, 1 site   check.sh:767 -> selftest_doc_consistency.sh via $CHECKER
  verify_injection_count.py  INVOKED, 1 site   check.sh:802 -> selftest_injection_count.sh via $CHECKER
  validate_grounding.py      NOT invoked — check.sh:493 is a "-f" presence check only
  verify_content_lock.py     NOT referenced by any script
  verify_knowledge_paths.py  NOT referenced by any script
  build_glossary_json.py     NOT referenced by any script
  build_units.py             RETIRED — file deleted, no surviving invocation
So SIX oracles are still invoked, not zero and not four.

THE GENERALISABLE FORM, which is worth more than the count: A GREP OVER AN ENTRY POINT DOES NOT ENUMERATE WHAT THAT ENTRY POINT RUNS. Shell dispatch is transitive and its targets can be variables. This is the same class as the message-keyed scan recorded in the bd-0czh comment in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/diff_verify_coverage.rs, where three fail-opens survived an audit because grepping for a message returned a hit and READ AS GUARDED. In both cases a grep produced a confident answer to a question it structurally cannot answer.

WHY IT MATTERS OPERATIONALLY: retirement decisions were being taken on the false premise. An oracle that is still invoked cannot be retired at any price until the invocation is repointed; deleting one would have turned check.sh red at a line nobody had connected to the deletion.

FIX: make the answer computable rather than grepped. A gate that resolves check.sh transitive closure — follow every "sh scripts/*.sh" and run_selftest target, resolve single-assignment variables, and emit the set of interpreters and scripts actually reachable — and asserts that every .py in the substrate allowlist is either in that set or explicitly marked unreferenced. Anti-vacuous: a closure that resolves to zero scripts is an ERROR. Cross-check: registries/substrate_allowlist.toml currently carries a row claiming build_learn.py is "not on the check.sh path"; scripts/_run_build_learn.sh:6 invokes it. That row is a live counterexample and should be the gate first known-bad.

ACCEPTANCE: the transitive set is computed by a gate, not by grep; every allowlist row claim about check.sh path membership is checked against it; the build_learn.py row is corrected; the gate is proven by a mutation pair.

title: FLEET BLOCKER: syspolicyd is pegged at 100% and every newly-linked binary on this Mac hangs in _dyld_start — no cargo build or cargo test can complete, for any agent
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 ~19:45-19:55 while working bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.13.

SYMPTOM: every 'cargo build' / 'cargo check' in this tree hangs indefinitely. 29-32 cargo processes alive, ZERO rustc processes, load average only 3.9 — the machine is idle and deadlocked, not busy.

ROOT CAUSE, isolated to a 4-line reproduction that has nothing to do with cargo:

    printf 'int main(){return 7;}' > /tmp/t.c
    /usr/bin/clang -o /tmp/t.bin /tmp/t.c
    /tmp/t.bin              # never returns; killed at 90s

A freshly-linked 16 KB binary that does nothing but 'return 7' NEVER STARTS. 'sample' on a stuck process shows the entire stack as '_dyld_start (in dyld) + 0' — it is blocked before main. Meanwhile:

    ps -o pcpu= -p 522   ->  99.7 - 103.1   (/usr/libexec/syspolicyd)

syspolicyd, the Gatekeeper / provenance evaluation daemon, is pinned above 100% and is not draining. Every new executable queues behind it.

RULED OUT, each by measurement:
  - NOT quarantine: 'xattr -l' shows only com.apple.provenance, no com.apple.quarantine
  - NOT signing: ad-hoc 'codesign -s -' on the binary changes nothing (still 45s timeout)
  - NOT the inode: a plain 'cp' of the binary also hangs
  - NOT the path: rebuilt under $HOME instead of /tmp, same 30s timeout
  - NOT load: load average 3.9, no rustc running at all

BLAST RADIUS — THIS IS NOT ONE AGENT'S PROBLEM. 8 build-script-build processes belonging to OTHER agents are stuck in _dyld_start, one of them for 36 minutes. One of those (target/debug/build/cdcp_gate-*/build-script-build, ppid a sibling's 'cargo build -q -p cdcp_gate --bin cdcp_gate') holds the lock on the SHARED course-engine/target/debug/.cargo-lock, so every other agent's cargo prints 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' and waits forever. The whole cdcp_gate migration wave is stalled behind one hung OS-level exec.

LIKELY TRIGGER: N agents each linking fresh unsigned Mach-O binaries in parallel saturated syspolicyd's evaluation queue and it wedged. Same family as the known NTM/Gatekeeper trauma, in a new form — that one was quarantine on a downloaded cask, this one is provenance evaluation on locally-linked build artifacts.

FIX REQUIRES JOSH (restarting a security daemon is escalation-only, not autonomous):
    sudo killall syspolicyd     # launchd restarts it; releases the queue
then clear the wedged builds:
    pkill -f build-script-build
Consider also whether N-way parallel cargo across agents needs a build-slot lock (Agent Mail acquire_build_slot exists for exactly this) so the fleet stops generating hundreds of simultaneous first-exec evaluations.

WORKAROUND FOUND, and it is worth keeping: rustc ITSELF is an already-evaluated binary and runs fine. A crate can therefore still be TYPE-CHECKED without cargo, by regenerating the build.rs output by hand and invoking rustc with --emit=metadata:
    OUT_DIR=<dir with a hand-generated gate_modules.rs> CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=crates/cdcp_gate \
    rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type lib --crate-name cdcp_gate crates/cdcp_gate/src/lib.rs \
      -L dependency=target/debug/deps --extern toml=<rlib> --extern serde=<rlib> --emit=metadata
This type-checks. It does NOT execute anything, so it verifies compilation and nothing else — a differential harness still cannot RUN.

ACCEPTANCE: 'clang -o /tmp/t.bin /tmp/t.c && /tmp/t.bin; echo $?' prints 7 in under a second; 'cargo build -p cdcp_gate' completes; pgrep -f build-script-build returns nothing.
close_reason:
RESOLVED. Same root event as bd-syspolicyd-exec-wedge-i0z4: the operator restarted
syspolicyd. Re-verified 2026-08-17, three days after the incident:

  timeout 20 ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list  ->  exit 0, 1638 bytes
  syspolicyd                                ->  0.3% CPU (was 100% pegged)

This bead was filed independently by a subagent doing its own process forensics
while I was filing the sibling, and its evidence was better than mine on two
points worth preserving:

  - It sampled the wedged process rather than inferring: a build-script child at
    0.0% CPU and 32 BYTES RSS — forked, never exec'd — holding the shared target
    lock for 26+ minutes, with 50 such processes across six agents' target dirs
    at peak. A single frame in the sample: _dyld_start. It never reached main.
  - It measured that a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR IS NOT AN ESCAPE, because cargo's
    package-cache lock is GLOBAL. Six agents apparently tried that independently
    and all six wedged at the first build-script crate.

THE PREVENTION HALF, which is the part that outlives the outage and belongs here
rather than on the sibling:

The exposure was mine. I dispatched NINE concurrent agents against one cargo
target directory. The consequence was not slowness — it was that agents could not
build or test, therefore could not verify their own work, therefore reported
unverified claims or died. Four agents terminated on API errors; two handed back
explicitly unverified suites. Prior waves of six ran cleanly.

The limit is not agent count in the abstract. It is CONCURRENT CARGO CONSUMERS.
Agents that only read files parallelise fine; agents that build or test do not.
The operating rule adopted from this: dispatch ports and any cargo-heavy work ONE
AT A TIME, and treat "I could not verify this" as a first-class, expected report
rather than an apology — the three agents that said so plainly are the reason we
knew which claims to re-run.

Not closed by this bead, and deliberately not re-filed as a gate: there is no
mechanism preventing a future controller from over-dispatching. That is a
controller-discipline item, and building a gate for it would be exactly the
gate-on-gate reflex bd-engine-not-gate-ar39 exists to stop. It lives as the
operating rule above.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION from the bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w audit, measured 2026-08-14 19:20-19:45. I reached the same conclusion from the other end (process forensics, not syspolicyd) before seeing this bead, so the two observations are not the same measurement twice.

WHAT I SAW:
- lsof target/debug/.cargo-lock -> cargo PID 68231, later 68771 ('cargo build -q -p cdcp_gate --tests'), holding the shared lock for over an hour.
- Its child PID 27915 was target/debug/build/cdcp_gate-4df17c8fce7ff308/build-script-build: 23 minutes elapsed, 0.0 percent CPU, 32 bytes RSS, state S. 32 bytes RSS is a process forked and never through exec - which is _dyld_start, exactly as this bead says.
- At peak, 50 hung build-script-build processes across SIX different target dirs belonging to different agents (scratchpad target, tgt, t, tgt-sd15, tg3, tg2) plus the shared live target. Crates: proc-macro2, libc, serde, serde_core, version_check, generic-array - i.e. every ordinary build-script carrier, not one bad crate.

title: HALT: syspolicyd wedged — no locally-built binary can execute; every Rust verification in this window is unsound
description:
WHAT: from roughly 19:00 MDT 2026-08-14, ad-hoc / linker-signed binaries — everything cargo produces — cannot execute on this machine. They block before main(). Apple- and Developer-ID-signed binaries are unaffected.

MEASURED, controller, independently of the reporting agent:
  ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list        -> exit 124 under timeout 20, ZERO bytes written
  /usr/bin/python3 -c print(...)        -> exit 0, works
  git --version                         -> exit 0, works
  br --version                          -> exit 0, works (Developer-ID signed)
  syspolicyd                            -> 99.1% CPU, 179m50s accumulated
Agent measurements from the same window: 75 cargo processes queued on target/debug/.cargo-lock with ZERO rustc running; the lock holder build-script-build at 47m18s elapsed and 0:00.00 CPU; sample(1) showing a single frame, _dyld_start — it never reached main. Every build-script-build across four different agents CARGO_TARGET_DIRs in the identical state. Processes at 0.0 CPU / 32 B RSS.
Tried and measured USELESS: a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR (cargo package-cache lock is global); xattr -c on the binary and its build script then re-exec.

THE DECISION IS JOSH.S AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE BLOCKING THE FLEET: `sudo killall syspolicyd`, or reboot. sudo is escalation-only under the standing grant; the controller will not run it.

WHAT THIS INVALIDATES, and this is the part that matters more than the outage. ANY RUST SUITE REPORTED GREEN IN THIS WINDOW WAS READ OFF A STALE ARTIFACT. A binary that cannot exec produces no output and no exit code; a harness that mistakes that for a pass, or that falls back to a previously built artifact, reports success for a run that never happened. Treat every Rust verification claim timestamped after ~19:00 as UNVERIFIED until re-run — not as false, as unknown. Three agents said so explicitly and unprompted, which is the correct behaviour and is why we know.

THE CONTROLLER MADE THE MATCHING ERROR IN THE OTHER DIRECTION and it is recorded here as the worked example: I ran ./target/debug/cdcp_gate build-units, saw exit 124 and zero output twice, and nearly filed a P0 claiming the gate hangs. It does not. It could not start. A wedged exec and an infinite loop are indistinguishable from the outside if you only look at the exit code and the empty log — you must check whether the process accumulated CPU. Mine had not.

ON RESUME, IN ORDER:
1. Confirm a locally-built binary execs: `timeout 20 ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list` must exit 0 with output.
2. cargo build -p cdcp_gate --tests, then re-run every suite any agent reported green after 19:00.
3. Adjudicate the four orphan gate files left by dead agents (bd-wave8-agent-deaths-redispatch-qb01) — they are in the glob and have never compiled.
4. Only then trust a check.sh run.

ANTI-VACUOUS NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS A GUARD FROM THIS: the failure signature is a timeout with an EMPTY log and no CPU accumulation. A gate that treats "no output" as "no findings" would have reported GREEN throughout this incident. That is the fooled certificate arriving through the operating system rather than through a gate.

WHAT THIS INCIDENT IS WORTH KEEPING, since the outage itself is over:

1. A WEDGED EXEC, AN INFINITE LOOP, AND A PASSING RUN ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE if you only read the exit code. A binary blocked before main() produces zero bytes and no exit code. I nearly filed a P0 claiming  hangs; it could not start. THE TELL IS CPU ACCUMULATION — an infinite loop burns CPU, a wedged exec does not. That check is now the first thing to run against any apparent hang.

That is a fooled certificate arriving through the operating system rather than through a gate, and it is the reason every anti-vacuous leg in this repo asserts a floor rather than merely non-zero.

title: INCIDENT (RESOLVED, for the record): syspolicyd pegged at 100% stalled every ad-hoc-signed binary at _dyld_start for ~50 minutes
description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-14 ~19:50 MDT when syspolicyd restarted (pid 522 replaced by 41143). Filed after the fact because the br binary needed to file it was itself stalled by the condition. Filed so the signature is recognisable the next time five agents build Rust concurrently on this machine.

SYMPTOM: cargo made no progress in course-engine for roughly 50 minutes. At peak, 75 cargo processes were queued on target/debug/.cargo-lock with ZERO rustc running.

MEASURED, in order:
1. Lock holder cargo pid 68229, whose child build-script-build had 47m18s ELAPSED and 0:00.00 CPU TIME. sample(1) showed a single frame: _dyld_start (in dyld). It never reached main.
2. syspolicyd (pid 522) at 98-100% CPU with 171 minutes of accumulated CPU time. mds_stores at 1032 minutes.
3. EVERY build-script-build in the process table, across four different CARGO_TARGET_DIRs belonging to four different agents, was in that same state.
4. An already-built, previously-run binary showed it too: ./target/debug/cdcp_gate list produced no output and no CPU in 2m48s wall; a retry under timeout 25 returned 124.
5. Apple-signed and Developer-ID-signed binaries were unaffected throughout - python3, git, rustfmt and cargo itself all exec normally.

MECHANISM: cargo artifacts are adhoc, linker-signed (codesign -dv) and carry com.apple.provenance. Ad-hoc-signed binaries need a fresh execution-policy authorization from syspolicyd on every exec; Developer-ID binaries have a cached decision. Five agents each rebuilding cdcp_gate produce hundreds of fresh ad-hoc binaries per hour. syspolicyd saturated, every ad-hoc exec queued behind it, and the queue presents as a hang inside dyld rather than as an error.

WORKAROUNDS TRIED AND MEASURED USELESS:
- A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Same wedge; its build scripts were among the stalled.
- xattr -c on the binary and on its build script, then re-exec. Still timed out at 25s.
- Killing the wedged build-script (pid 68230) released the lock, but the next holder wedged the same way inside 60 seconds. Recorded because it was done, not because it worked.

WHAT ACTUALLY CLEARED IT: syspolicyd restarted. sudo killall syspolicyd is the manual form; launchd relaunches it.

PREVENTION WORTH CONSIDERING: exclude the repo target/ trees from Spotlight - mds_stores had burned 17 CPU-hours indexing them and was the other half of the load.

READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GREEN FROM THAT WINDOW: agents cannot distinguish a stalled exec from a slow one. Any suite reported green between 19:00 and 19:50 MDT on 2026-08-14 was read off a stale artifact and should be re-run.
