title: The overclaim honesty scan cannot tell an overclaim from a disclaimer of one — every compliant gate header trips it
description:
WHAT: crates/cdcp_gate/tests/repo_surface.rs::no_overclaiming_language_in_the_shipped_surface is a lowercase SUBSTRING match for "guarantee", "proves" and "makes impossible" over the shipped (non-test) region of every gate source. It cannot distinguish a claim from a denial of that claim.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: export_anki.rs:43 read

  //! It therefore does not "guarantee", "prove", or "make impossible" anything
  //! about the learner s experience.

and the honesty gate flagged it as an overclaim. That sentence is the gate AUTHOR DOING EXACTLY WHAT THE PROJECT ASKS — every gate is required to state its claim as a floor-raise plus what it cannot decide, and the most natural phrasing of "what it cannot decide" quotes the very words the scan bans.

SO THE RULE AND ITS ENFORCEMENT POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The standard says "say what you do not prove"; the gate says "do not write the word prove". An author who follows the standard trips the gate, and the cheapest way out is to write a WEAKER disclaimer — which is the opposite of what the rule wants. A gate that penalises compliance teaches people to stop complying.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SUBSTRING-SCOPE CLASS in this repo, and the pattern is now worth naming as a class rather than fixing case by case:
  - DCG blocked a bead-filing heredoc and a git commit under core.git:restore-worktree because the word "restore" appeared in PROSE inside a heredoc.
  - substrate-guard --prove-wired went RED on its own comment, which said "NEVER add a row for scripts/__cdcp_probe_unlisted__.py" — the comment read as the row it warned against (bd-ip10).
  - This one.
Each time the fix was to reword the prose, because narrowing a detector is weakening it and is escalation-only. Three reworded prose sites is a pattern, not three coincidences.

WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED: both export_anki.rs sites are reworded and the header now carries a pointer to this bead explaining why it is phrased oddly. That is a wart, and it will recur on the next gate that documents its ceiling honestly.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The scan distinguishes an assertion from a negation, OR the project adopts a sanctioned way to disclaim (a marker the scan honours, e.g. a CANNOT-DECIDE: block that is exempt from the word list, with the exemption REQUIRING a reason so it cannot become a blanket).
- Known-GOOD legs, and they are the point of this bead: a header that says "this gate does not prove X" PASSES; a header that says "this gate proves X" is RED. Both must be asserted, or the fix has only moved the failure.
- Known-bad: a genuine overclaim in a newly added gate is still RED.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: the existing floor (files.len() >= 8) stays; a scan that reads zero shipped regions, or that reads only test modules, is an ERROR.
- Sweep for the class: any other detector in this repo that substring-matches prose it did not author. Report the count; three known instances suggests more.
close_reason: Scan distinguishes claim from denial. SHA b9379e449b1d0cb6e844861c4dfaec0954e3e7f1. Measured disclaimer GREEN; this gate guarantees X RED.

title: Six wave-8 gate ports were moved to .parked-wave8/ with no note, no bead and no owner notification
description:
COORDINATION FINDING, filed rather than fought over. Measured 2026-08-14 20:19-20:23 MDT.

WHAT HAPPENED: while I was mid-verification on bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19 and .20, both of my gate files and both of my differential harnesses were moved out of the crate into a new untracked directory course-engine/.parked-wave8/. The move happened twice, roughly four minutes apart, taking the smoke_a11y pair first and the smoke_learn_v2 pair second. At its widest the directory held six ports belonging to at least four agents: smoke_a11y, smoke_learn_v2, smoke_learn, smoke_feedback_links, smoke_diagrams, smoke_learn_chrome, each with its diff_ harness.

The parking itself is defensible - build.rs globs src/gates/*.rs, so one gate file that does not compile takes the whole crate down and every sibling with it. Quarantining incomplete ports to get the crate green is a reasonable integration move.

WHAT IS NOT DEFENSIBLE, and is the actual finding:

1. NO NOTE. The directory contains twelve .rs files and nothing else. No README, no reason, no date, no criterion for coming back. Nobody reading the tree can tell quarantine from abandonment.
2. NO BEAD. Nothing tracks that six ports are out of the build. The migration epic still reads as though they are in it, which is the exact failure mode that produced .19 and .20 in the first place - work that is invisible because the ledger does not mention it.
3. NO OWNER NOTIFICATION. No Agent Mail, no bead comment on the port beads. An agent that finishes a port and finds its file gone has to reconstruct what happened from mtimes, which is what I did.
4. NO SELECTION CRITERION RECORDED. My two were parked while compiling, passing and clippy-clean. They were taken because they were wave-8, not because they were broken. A quarantine keyed on a wave rather than on a compile result removes working code.

WHAT I DID: restored my four files by cp (byte-rewrite into the existing path, never mv - the stale-binary trap on bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w), verified the crate still builds, and measured: diff_smoke_a11y 13 passed, diff_smoke_learn_v2 15 passed, 41 lib tests passed, clippy exit 0 with zero warnings naming my files. I did not touch the other four agents' files, which are still parked.

ACCEPTANCE:
- .parked-wave8/ gets a README naming the reason, the date, the owner and the criterion for un-parking, or the directory is emptied.
- A bead tracks each parked port so the epic count stays honest.
- If the quarantine mechanism is kept, key it on 'does this file compile' rather than on which wave it came from, and notify the owning agent.
close_reason: README names date, owner, reason, unpark criterion. Ports stay parked per ar39.3.

title: Three wave-8 ports landed with 7 agreement-only differential cases, tripping the blind-spot ratchet
description:
WHAT: registering the three wave-8 port harnesses took the tree-wide agreement-only count from 28 to 35 and the ratchet in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs went RED, correctly.

MEASURED by the census re-deriving from source (the registry numbers are a BUDGET; the measurement is what the test does):
  diff_smoke_a11y.rs      15 cases,  1 agreement-only  (bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.19)
  diff_smoke_learn_v2.rs  32 cases,  5 agreement-only  (.20)
  diff_export_anki.rs     27 cases,  1 agreement-only  (.13)

THE BUDGET WAS NOT RAISED, DELIBERATELY. The ratchet says the blind spot may fall and may not rise, and it did rise — that is a true statement about the repo, not a gate being fussy. Raising a budget to get green is weakening a gate, which is escalation-only here. The three rows carry the correct measured `cases` and a budget of 0, so the tree is RED on exactly this, with the reason recorded.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO PAY IT. An agreement-only case asserts that two implementations produce the same bytes and says NOTHING about whether those bytes are right. Measured precedent, verify_objectives: `--min-items-per-topic 0` printed "primary_topics=106 covered=106 shortfalls=0 mode=strict, EXIT 0" — 106 of 106 topics covered with not one comparison performed — and its harness PASSED that exact case for weeks because both sides produced the same wrong answer. Every case in this count is one that no shared defect can fail.

AND THESE SEVEN EVAPORATE ON RETIREMENT. The standing policy retires an oracle at port time; a case saying only "the two sides agree" is worth nothing once there is one side. So these seven are simultaneously the blind spot AND the retirement cost for three oracles we intend to retire.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the 7 asserts an INDEPENDENT verdict: what the correct answer IS (exit code plus a required substring, or the resolved path plus the item count plus the named finding), checkable if only one implementation existed.
- The recipe that worked on diff_verify_orphans.rs (7 -> 0 in one wave) is the precedent: rewriting the assertion is NOT enough, because a case running against the GREEN live tree has no finding to suppress. Point the input at a tree with a PLANTED finding, then assert the resolved path, the item COUNT (this is what catches a silent fallback), and the named finding.
- The ratchet returns to 28 or below without its budgets being edited upward.
- Known-bad: plant a defect in BOTH implementations of one converted case and assert it now fails. Under the old assertion it passed.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: a converted case that ends up asserting nothing about output, or that compares an artifact neither side wrote, is an ERROR.
close_reason: 7/7 converted; census 5<=28; KNOWN_BAD trips; SHA 1b592bc; leftover 5 in injection_count

title: smoke_diagrams: an unclosed honesty-banner element swallows the rest of the page
description: WHAT: `scripts/smoke_diagrams.py`'s DiagramHTML tracks banner nesting with a counter that is only decremented by a NON-VOID end tag. If the element carrying class="honesty-banner" is never closed, _depth stays >= 1 to end of file and EVERY subsequent text node on the page is appended to the banner text. WHY IT MATTERS: the disclaimer predicate (\bnot\b AND 'certif') then reads the WHOLE PAGE, which is the exact fooling shape the current version of this gate was written to close — its header says 'parses the HTML for the honesty-banner element ... instead of grepping the file for not/certif. A file whose whole content is `not certif fire-sequence` now fails.' An unclosed banner reopens that door: a hollow banner plus an unrelated 'this does not grant certification' footer elsewhere in the document scores GREEN. MEASURED 2026-08-14 during bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd.14. The same counter also cannot be closed by an unbalanced </br>, because handle_endtag returns before touching _depth for anything in VOID_TAGS. REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED: the Rust port cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams reproduces it and tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs pins it in the adversarial table ('an unclosed banner swallows the rest of the page'), because a port stricter than its oracle blinds the differential. ACCEPTANCE: decide the correct behaviour (candidates: cap the banner at the first end tag whose name matches the opening tag; or treat depth>0 at EOF as a FAIL 'honesty-banner is never closed'), change BOTH implementations in the same commit, and convert the pinning case to assert the new verdict.
close_reason: Product extract fails unclosed banners. Python gone. Pinning case now asserts RED. b61ef78.

title: smoke_diagrams: the 'unparseable HTML' branch is unreachable dead code
description: WHAT: check_diagram() wraps parser.feed(text); parser.close() in 'except Exception as exc: return [f"{did}: unparseable HTML: {exc}"]'. CPython's html.parser is a tolerant tokenizer with no error recovery to fail: every parse helper returns an index or -1, goahead()'s only assert is on a branch reachable solely through interesting.search() lying, and no input reaches it. MEASURED 2026-08-14 by reading Lib/html/parser.py at 3.14.2 and by the 41-row adversarial table in tests/diff_smoke_diagrams.rs, none of which produces the message. WHY IT MATTERS: it reads as coverage of a class that has none. A reviewer counting the gate's failure modes counts one that cannot fire, and the message is untested by construction — there is no input that can exercise it, so it could be wrong in any way and nothing would notice. The Rust port cdcp_gate smoke-diagrams has no counterpart and says so in its evaluate() header. ACCEPTANCE: delete the try/except from the oracle (leaving feed/close bare), or replace it with a branch that CAN fire, in the same commit as any Rust change. If deleted, the port's residual-divergence note goes with it.

description:
WHAT: reverse the size inversion. cdcp_gate is 64,955 lines; ALL product Rust combined (core+grade+bank+assemble+cli+wasm+registry_check) is 6,417. The checker is 10x the thing it checks and 267x the grader it exists to protect.

WHY NOW, MEASURED 2026-08-14:
- One port landed today replacing 362 lines of Python with 6,586 lines of Rust — MORE THAN THE ENTIRE PRODUCT — of which 3,106 are py_compat.rs, a transcription of CPython html.parser internals (2,231 entity mappings, 737 printability ranges) so a diagram smoke test can be byte-identical to a retired oracle. That file alone is 18x cdcp_grade.
- Our own tick ledger convicts the campaign: of T1..T8, exactly TWO changed what a learner experiences (T1 unapproved items cannot reach a mock exam; T6 module-15 progress reaches the learner). Six were guards denying other guards. All eight were logged GREEN.
- The repo already wrote the doctrine it then violated: build_units.rs header says "a differential is not correctness"; FRANKEN-EXTRACT.md Doctrine #0 says "process work earns zero capability credit"; the flywheel charter says a gate that never denies scores ZERO. The standing P0 epic is to write seventeen more of them.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE METRIC, NOT THE ROADMAP. Every port bead currently passes when a Rust file exists that agrees byte-for-byte with a retired Python file. Nothing in that acceptance mentions the product, so the cheapest way to pass is to add lines to cdcp_gate. Change the acceptance to "cdcp_gate got SMALLER" and the same work routes into extraction instead of transcription.

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT: a roadmap v5, a new charter, or a rewrite. CHARTER.md and FEATURE_SURFACE.md are edited in place. No crate is created that does not remove more lines than it adds.

THE GATE CAMPAIGN WAS NOT WASTE, and the sequencing must not pretend it was. It found the single most learner-visible defect anyone has found here (learners SCORED on withdrawn questions, SRS-scheduled and mastery-weighted), the retired-items-in-units_index hole, the module-15 hub gap, and today an unclosed-banner hole that reopens the whole-file-substring fooling path. title: GATE-SHRINK RATCHET: cdcp_gate line count is a ceiling that may only fall
description:
WHAT: a compiled ceiling on cdcp_gate total Rust lines, pinned at todays measurement, that a change may lower and may never raise. Modelled exactly on the agreement-only ratchet in crates/cdcp_gate/tests/differential_verdict_census.rs, which has already worked twice: it caught a controller guessing budgets, and it refused an unregistered harness on arrival.

WHY THIS IS FIRST. Every other bead in this epic is a suggestion without it. The inversion did not happen because anyone decided to grow the gate; it happened because NOTHING MEASURED IT and the acceptance criterion for a port never mentioned size. A rule with no enforcement mechanism is a suggestion, and systems ignore suggestions — this repo has written that sentence down and then proved it three times.

THE NUMBER TO PIN, measured 2026-08-14:
  cdcp_gate total .rs              64,955   <- the ceiling
    src                            ~38,400
    tests                          ~26,300
  ALL product Rust combined         6,417
  cdcp_grade (the oracle)             243

WHY A LINE COUNT AND NOT SOMETHING CLEVERER. It is crude, it is gameable in principle (one long line), and it is the right instrument anyway: the failure mode was not subtle, it was six thousand lines of CPython transcription landing in one commit. A metric an author can see moving is worth more than a metric that is theoretically sound. Gaming it requires deliberate effort, which is the point — the inversion happened by DEFAULT, and a ratchet removes the default.

RULE ZERO SELF-CHECK, because this bead is itself a process artifact. Per FRANKEN-EXTRACT Doctrine #0, a process artifact exists only as a hard gate for a NAMED PRODUCT CAPABILITY with a DELETION CONDITION. Named capability: the product crates hold the product law, so a learner-visible behaviour can be found, tested and changed without reading a 2,000-line gate. Deletion condition: DELETE THIS RATCHET when cdcp_gate is under 15,000 lines AND no src/gates/*.rs compiles a learner-visible artifact. Write that condition into the test itself so it cannot outlive its purpose.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A test asserts total cdcp_gate .rs lines <= the pinned ceiling. Over -> RED, naming the current count, the ceiling, and the per-file deltas since the pin so the author sees WHERE it grew.
- Lowering the ceiling is a one-line edit; raising it is not possible without editing the test, which is the point. State plainly in the header that raising it is weakening a gate and is escalation-only.
- ANTI-VACUOUS, and this is the leg that matters: a scan that finds ZERO .rs files under crates/cdcp_gate is an ERROR, never a pass. A ratchet that counted nothing would report identically to one that counted everything and passed. Derive the file-count floor from the tree and assert it.
- KNOWN-BAD: add a 500-line file under src/gates/ -> RED naming the file and the delta. KNOWN-GOOD: delete a gate file -> GREEN, and the test PRINTS the new headroom so shrinking is visible and rewarded.
- Meta-test PAIR: (1) mutate the comparison so over-ceiling passes -> suite non-zero; (2) with the mutation STILL in place, delete the assertion -> back to zero. Use tests/support/rebuild.rs (byte-rewrite restore), never mv — bd-stale-binary-mtime-trap-p65w.
- Wired into check.sh in the same change. BUILT != WIRED.
- The ceiling and the product-Rust total are BOTH printed on the green path, so the ratio is visible in every run rather than needing to be re-derived by a critic.

title: Reframe the substrate epic: a port passes when cdcp_gate got SMALLER
description:
WHAT: rewrite the acceptance criterion of bd-substrate-rust-migration-jhd and demote it from the default P0. Do NOT close it — the remaining Python IS a live Substrate Law violation and closing it leaves that with no owner.

THE EPIC IS WRONG IN THREE WAYS AND RIGHT IN ONE:

2. WRONG COUNT. The title says 17. Measured: ELEVEN are already ported and are now differential oracles; EIGHT .py remain genuinely invoked. The demotion argument is stronger than the epic knows.

title: cdcp doctor / health --robot / repair: the product needs an operator surface, not a shell script
description:
WHAT: add doctor, health --robot and repair to cdcp_cli. Measured: the CLI today has bank-hash, grade, export-web, serve, goldens — and no preflight, no machine-readable status, no idempotent rebuild.

WHY IT IS PRODUCT AND NOT ERGONOMICS: every franken-family CLI (whisper, tts, ocr) exposes doctor/health as its FIRST agent surface, because the alternative is that every operator and every agent learns to read a 900-line shell script to find out whether the tree is sane. We built check.sh instead of a product command, and the cost showed up today: four agents spent real time spelunking check.sh to answer questions like "is the bank loadable", "is the wasm present", "what is the current bank_hash".

SHAPE:
  cdcp doctor          preflight: bank loads, wasm artifact present and fresh, goldens present, port bindable, python3 present for any surviving oracle
  cdcp health --robot  versioned NDJSON envelope: schema_version, bank_hash, approved_n, manifest_n, unit_count, engine identities, goldens state
  cdcp repair          idempotent: rebuild units/glossary/export-web. MUST NOT re-freeze goldens.

THE ONE HARD RULE: repair is NOT a golden laundromat. UPDATE_GOLDENS stays a human/env gate and the four-command block in goldens/PROVENANCE.md stays the only regeneration path. A repair verb that silently re-freezes is the exact silent-re-freeze hole B2 exists to close — it would route around the coupling ledger from inside the product.

ACCEPTANCE:
- The three verbs exist, are documented in README, and doctor exits non-zero on a tree that cannot serve.
- health --robot emits a VERSIONED envelope; an unversioned or unparseable one is an ERROR. Field names are pinned by a test so a consumer can rely on them.
- ANTI-VACUOUS: doctor on an empty tree is an ERROR naming what is missing, never a green "nothing to check". health with zero items is an ERROR.
- repair is idempotent: run twice, second run writes nothing. Asserted by mtime, not by exit code — a tree-cleanliness check cannot see an idempotent write (measured, bd-rebase-bounds-live-tree-write-ohgr).
- Known-bad: delete the wasm artifact -> doctor RED naming it; corrupt content.lock -> doctor RED.
- These are cdcp_cli lines, not cdcp_gate lines. The ratchet must not move.

title: EXTRACT cdcp_schedule: the learner runs a second, unpinned implementation of the review law in JS
description:
WHAT: move the review-interval ladder and the mastery thresholds out of web/assets/js and into a Rust crate the browser calls through WASM.

WHY: the dual-path conformance proves the GRADER agrees between native and browser. It proves nothing about the rest of the learner law, and there is quite a lot of it: srs.js owns the interval ladder, mastery.js owns the thresholds, learn_units.js owns unit selection. Those are a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of product rules, unpinned, untested against the Rust side, and shipped to every learner. We already found what that costs — quiz.js filtered by module and never read status, so learners were scored on withdrawn questions while every Rust gate was green and could not have been otherwise.

HONESTY ITEM RIDING ALONG: it is not SRS. INTERVAL_STEPS=[1,3] with a 3-day cap is short-interval review. FEATURE_SURFACE, README and srs.js all call it SRS, which claims a spaced-repetition algorithm we do not implement. Rename in the same change — this is the same class as the L3 correction, and we do not get to keep one overclaim because it is old.

ACCEPTANCE:
- crates/cdcp_schedule holds the interval ladder and mastery thresholds as Rust constants + functions, with its own tests.
- cdcp_wasm exports them; srs.js and mastery.js CALL rather than reimplement. JS renders, WASM decides.

- Known-bad: change a constant in Rust, assert the browser behaviour moves — proving the JS is really reading it and not shadowing it.
- These are product-crate lines. The ratchet must not move.

title: L.1: rust types + local sqlite/jsonl attempt log (no psychometrics)
description:
WHAT: rust types + sqlite/jsonl local attempt log (item_version, bank_hash, learner_pseudonym, mode, exposure_count, chosen_option, correctness, latency, timestamp, prior_attempts). Opt-in export flag default OFF. Refuse to compute IRT/difficulty.

WHY: item difficulty and discrimination are sample-dependent and unreliable at small N. Round 2 was explicit: do not build cdcp_stats before there is data. Capture first; analyse never-until-there-is-enough. A minimum-N warning has to exist in the schema from day one so a later analysis crate cannot ship without naming the floor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `crates/cdcp_attempts` (not a module in `cdcp_gate`; do not grow the gate).
- Local-first store writes both SQLite and append-only JSONL under a caller-chosen directory.
- Recorded fields are exactly the EPIC L set (plus a schema_version so the log can migrate). No `difficulty` / `discrimination` field; no `f32`/`f64` in `src/`.
- `ExportPolicy` defaults OFF. Export without an explicit opt-in is an ERROR, even when the store has events.
- Known-bad empty store is an ERROR on read/export (never a zero-N analysis that looks like success).
- `estimate_item_response_model` / `compute_item_difficulty` / `compute_item_discrimination` always return `Err` (psychometrics refused) at any N.
- `MIN_N_FOR_ITEM_STATS` and `minimum_n_warning(n)` are part of the public surface; an opted-in export receipt carries the warning when `n < MIN_N`.
- `cargo test -p cdcp_attempts` and `cargo clippy -p cdcp_attempts --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
